$Delta revenue → buyback → burn mechanism has already started to create real value capture.

0xe8ffd7e24187f72afb08d75b1bb13088a989a791

So far, 2.41M DELTA has been burned = 0.241% of the total supply = 9.96 ETH already deployed = approximately $24,938.

The number itself is not particularly large, but this comes from a continuous buyback mechanism funded by protocol revenue.

Another key point is 80% of revenue → Buyback + Burn.

This means there is a direct connection between Delta’s business activity and DELTA’s supply:

Users trade/use the protocol → revenue is generated → 80% of revenue is used to buy back DELTA → DELTA is burned → circulating supply decreases

So DELTA’s narrative is starting to develop Revenue → Token Value Capture.

This creates a flywheel:

More users → more trading/fees → more protocol revenue → more DELTA buybacks → more DELTA burned → lower supply → greater token scarcity → more market attention → more users

The biggest feature of this flywheel is:

The more revenue grows, the more capital goes into buybacks; the more buybacks, the more tokens get burned.

So at this point, simply looking at the amount burned is not enough. Instead, we need to watch:

Whether protocol revenue continues to grow
Whether weekly buyback amounts continue to increase
Whether DELTA burns are accelerating
Whether users and trading volume continue to grow

If revenue continues to expand from its current level, this market cap could just be the beginning for DELTA.

Now most participants are on the back foot, underexposed, over trading, over rotating, pressuring themselves to make a fortune in a week and begging for wipes to position heavily.

Why would it hand that to them? This is an asset class that bores you to death and then rapidly puts you in the pressure cooker.

BTC puts in violent, rapid rallies and then chops around in a traders market the other 80-90% of the time.

We're already 3 weeks into this current comp, the better bet based on probabilities is that the traders market continues.

73/74k is certainly something I want and would take advantage of, but I'm not making that my only plan.

面对伊朗局势升温高油价导致的通胀，美国其实采取了起码两手应对措施：

一边跟俄罗斯缓和关系，力求尽早结束俄乌冲突以换取地缘缓和平抑市场，但这端的份量跟中东并不一致。

最关键的是美国也需要日本维持金融稳定，因为美国的AI资产有相当一部分是日元融资的杠杆在托着，日元的强波动一旦导致无序平仓，纳指一天可能就会跌掉几个月的涨幅。

text:
甭管黑帽白帽，赚到钱就是好帽🤣币圈绝对是奖励程序员最好的地方，我看不少人指责这伙白帽太黑了居然私自扣留了15%的BTC，这事让我想起了曾经中国最大的白帽社区乌云网惨遭世纪家园举报关停的农夫与蛇。乌云网成立于2010年，是当时最大的安全社区，在当时中国互联网野蛮生长的阶段为很多公司提供了无偿的漏洞报告，包括网易、支付宝、京东、腾讯、12306等等公司都被乌云网发现了数据泄露等隐患，传统的黑客在发现这些漏洞后，要么直接进行攻击获利，要么就是敲诈勒索向公司要钱，但是乌云网的白帽们都是出于维护互联网安全的“侠客”精神，也不会以此牟利，只能偶尔遇到几个良心公司打赏点感谢费，但是因为他们本身技术不错都有自己的本职工作，所以这件看似公益的事情也能维持运转下去。

转折点到了2015年，当时一名社区的白帽成员袁炜发现了婚恋公司世纪家园的一个漏洞，而按照规则为了确保该漏洞的真实性，需要先进行“测试攻击”验证后，再提交到乌云网和对应公司走流程，当时袁炜也确实拿到了一部分数据证明了漏洞真实存在，于是提交到了乌云，随后世纪家园也修复了漏洞并对袁炜表达了感谢。

本来是一个非常正常的行为，结果在一个月后，世纪家园突然背刺，直接报警说他们公司的数据遭到了非法入侵，警方则逮捕了袁炜，一瞬间引起了整个白帽圈的巨大震动。

按照白帽的工作流程，发现漏洞→测试漏洞→证明漏洞是必须要进行的，否则我怎么知道这个漏洞是不是有效的？就像是我捡到了一把钥匙，我觉得可能是邻居的，于是拿着钥匙试着开了邻居的门，果然打开了，于是给邻居打电话说你的钥匙丢了来我这取。

而按照公司的逻辑，你没有经过我的允许，就通过漏洞入侵了我的系统。也就是邻居直接报警说他家的钥匙被人拿走并且还打开了家门进去逛了一圈，谁知道安的什么心有没有偷东西，报警抓起来再说！

然后更惨的事情来了，整个乌云网突然发布公告进入了维护状态，并且至此再也没有恢复运营，网上也传出乌云网的核心创始团队直接被警方带走调查，同时包括漏洞盒子等其他几个白帽平台也停止了相关业务，整个中国白帽生态遭到了全面打击。

text:
🦔An NYU mathematician says OpenAI used his own progress against him to beat him to one of the biggest unsolved problems in mathematics. Tristan Buckmaster had been working toward a Millennium Prize proof using OpenAI's Codex when information about his progress reached OpenAI. 
Days later, OpenAI published a full proof of the same problem using the same uncommon approach, after burning $22.5 million in compute to get there. When Buckmaster confronted them, exec Sébastien Bubeck allegedly said "Why would you ruin your career?" and "If you don't want me to be nice, then I don't have to be nice."

My Take
OpenAI spent $22.5 million to solve a problem with a $1 million prize. They didn't do this for the bounty. They needed a headline that says "our AI solved one of the hardest problems in mathematics" and they needed it before someone else got credit. They started days after they heard about Buckmaster's progress and took the same uncommon approach he'd pursued for months. That's hard to explain as coincidence.

Buckmaster did his work inside Codex. OpenAI reserves the right to train on Codex data. They admit they can't rule out that his usage helped improve their models. So a customer used their product, potentially handed them the roadmap, and then OpenAI outran him with $22.5 million in compute he could never match. I don't know if any of this was intentional. But if you're a researcher and you just watched this happen, I don't think you'd keep your best ideas inside someone else's product.

Hedgie🤗

text:
DeepSeek 悄悄上了个新模型，deepseek-v4.1-flash-expires-on-0910。我把 Claude Code 的配置从 deepseek-v4-flash 换成它，敲了句 hi。

API Error: 400 Invalid schema for function 'Artifact':
"^(?!__.*__$)[^\p{Cc}\p{Cf}\p{Zl}\p{Zp}\"\./[\]]{1,200}$" is not a "regex"

一句话都没干就死了。

不是某个工具用到时才失败——是每一次请求都失败，会话等于死在起跑线。

原因在于 tools 数组是每个请求都要重发的。上游在解析请求体阶段就校验工具的 JSON Schema，校验不过直接 400，模型根本没开始想。所以一个工具的 schema 有问题，整条链路就废了。

————————————————————————

如果你也遇到这个问题，下面是修复方法：

Claude Code 自带这个开关。/config 里搜 ar：
Artifacts    false
关掉，立刻恢复。

————————————————————————

Plus：
如果你像我一样在多个 endpoint 之间来回切，别写进全局配置，会连累官方端点。塞进对应的 env 文件更合适：

export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://t.co/HqJZJgkZZz
export ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-...
export CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1   # ← 只在这个端点禁用

关掉之后，Artifact 不再进入 tools 数组。注意，不是"调用时被拒绝"，是压根不发出去。这两件事完全不同，下面还会用到。
————————————————————————
可能不是必现，需要 @deepseek_ai 官方排查下api的正则解析的鲁棒性

text:
AI Agent身份问题——NeoSoul和Billions Network联手了

有个被大多数人忽略的问题：当AI Agent开始代表你花钱、投票、签合约时，你怎么确保它不乱来？

BNB Chain和0G上最大的AI Agent基础设施NeoSoul，最近宣布和Billions Network合作研究这个事。Billions做的是隐私身份网络——给人类和Agent都提供身份层，但保护个人信息不泄露。

具体想解决的问题很直接：用户如何在Agent独立行动时保持控制权？这比“授权-执行”的简单模型复杂得多。Agent需要能在你的限制边界内自主决策，同时第三方需要能验证“这个Agent确实是被授权了的”，但又不能拿到你的敏感信息。

这是AI Agent从“玩具”走向“工具”必须跨过的门槛。否则没人敢让Agent做链上交易。

text:
As a mathematician, the OpenAI/Navier-Stokes story feels genuinely historic and unusually dramatic.

Navier-Stokes is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, each carrying a $1M prize. These are not just hard benchmark questions. They are among the most important open problems in mathematics, and entire research programs can grow around finding even one plausible route toward them.

Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge had spent most of the past year pushing a program started by Diego Córdoba and Luis Martínez-Zoroza. Their goal was to take known blowup constructions with rough forcing and push them to smooth forcing, ultimately toward incompressible Euler and Navier-Stokes.

By August 15, they had obtained smooth-forcing blowup results for Boussinesq and Euler. They were using Claude and Codex heavily throughout the project, and Buckmaster says they had been putting their drafts into Codex.

Then rumors started circulating that “Anthropic” had solved a major open problem.

OpenAI says those rumors triggered a large-scale effort on the Millennium Prize problems. Thousands of agents were launched, first attacking nearby Euler problems before the effort moved toward Navier-Stokes.

What made Buckmaster immediately suspicious was the direction: forced Navier-Stokes with smooth forcing.

In his statement, he says this was precisely the route Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroza had opened and that he and Alpöge had “quietly chosen to attack.” Almost nobody else he knew was working on it.

His reaction:
“When I heard ‘forced,’ it was a bright red flag.”

He then asked whether OpenAI’s model had been trained on, or otherwise had access to, their Codex sessions. According to Buckmaster, he was told the model did not look up user data, but when he asked specifically about training, he did not get a clear answer.

OpenAI denies directly accessing their private work, but its own post says:
“While unlikely, we cannot rule out that de-identified data derived from their usage of our products helped improve our models.”

And then the story becomes genuinely dramatic. Buckmaster says he was offered publication arrangements, including one where he alone would present OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes result without Levent Alpöge as an author. He says Bubeck emphasized that Alpöge working at Anthropic was the complication.
Buckmaster declined.

He then says that when he told OpenAI he would make the episode public if the result was released that way, the response was:
“Why would you ruin your career?”

Bubeck disputes Buckmaster’s characterization of the interaction.

Buckmaster is also careful about what he is claiming. He explicitly writes:
“I do not know whether our data was used. I am not accusing anyone of anything.”

That distinction matters.

But I think Tristan’s most important observation is broader than the dispute itself. He calls this a “Deep Blue-Kasparov moment” for mathematics.

For a Millennium Prize problem, the scarce intellectual resource is not merely the final proof. It is often years of taste, failed attempts, literature, intuition, and judgment that tell you where the promising path is.

If a small group discovers that path, and simply revealing that it is promising can trigger 10,000 AI agents to attack it, then mathematics may be entering a world where identifying the right question becomes more valuable than solving it.

And that could fundamentally change the culture of open mathematics.

Tristan Buckmaster’s statement:
https://t.co/QqCw94MjfC

GMX posted a tweet that is very important for zzz-2:native. The main points are as follows:

0x7dbf38976f6d3b9c529e7d9484a71898b409ee6a

X is GMX’s original core developer. He has stepped back from day-to-day development and is now only an Advisor to GMX.

He personally confirmed that he deployed ZZZ this weekend. This means the deployer of ZZZ was indeed X, rather than someone impersonating him.

However, ZZZ has no official connection to GMX. The wallet that deployed ZZZ is not an active GMX deployer, is not connected to any active GMX V2 contracts, and is a personal wallet previously used by X. This wallet had also previously deployed XVIX, a project that preceded GMX.

So GMX itself has no direct connection to ZZZ, other than X currently being a GMX Advisor.

GMX also switched to fresh deployer wallets long ago. These new wallets are not controlled by individuals and have additional security safeguards, clearly separating them from X’s personal wallet.

The next and most important thing to watch is that X is now building a new AI project. He has renamed his X account to Exponent Labs, with a core focus on AI-driven autonomously evolving protocols.

At this point, the narrative path is:

GMX OG / X → Personally deployed → Robinhood Chain → AI / Autonomous Protocols

The next evolution could be:

X → ZZZ → Exponent Labs → AI Agent / Autonomous Protocol

What the market is currently betting on is that ZZZ could become the early vehicle for X’s new project, with more information, products, or actions potentially coming later.

If X eventually incorporates ZZZ into Exponent Labs, or an actual AI Agent product emerges, that could become a very significant second-stage catalyst.

author: dontbesilent
quoted_text:
科研不再依赖天才科学家，而依赖GPU

--- 昨天的剧情继续反转！

Openai官宣了！

更重要的是，这是由opanai未发布的模型，几天时间完成的。（新模型能力比astra有大幅提升，见附图）

这件事的意义本身非常重大，属于菲尔兹奖级别的发现，但其意义远不止事件本身。

科学正在被重构为一种由算力驱动的高速工业流程。

先扫个盲：千禧难题与它的“爆破点”

纳维—斯托克斯方程（Navier-Stokes，简称 N-S 方程）：物理学中描述水流、空气、洋流等流体运动的基本方程。它的地位相当于流体领域的牛顿运动定律。然而在数学上，一个世纪以来没人能证明：在所有初始状态下，流体的平滑运动方程是否永远有良好定义的解。这是数学界著名的七大“千禧年大奖难题”之一。

有限时间奇性（Finite-time Singularity）：可以形象地理解为“物理量的暴走”。系统初始时风平浪静、处处平滑，但经过一段有限时间后，某些关键指标（如速度梯度或涡度）飙升至无穷大，数学上出现了类似“除以零”的无法计算点。这意味着经典连续介质模型在该处彻底失效，数学上称为“爆破”（Blow-up）。

Lean 形式化证明：过去的数学论文由同行专家人工审阅，难免漏掉隐蔽的推导漏洞。Lean 则是一种计算机代码证明语言，它要求将数学推导逐行写成严密的逻辑代码，由机器编译器校验每一步公理，彻底杜绝逻辑跳跃和人为笔误。

这次突破的关键在于：它是一个由 1 万个协同智能体构成的庞大系统，在 88 小时内吞吐 1300 亿 Token、交换 270 万条信息，完成了一场高强度的科研大兵团作战。

OpenAI 展示了一个此前未被充分验证的三维 Scaling 架构：

训练算力：赋予单体模型基础的科研直觉与逻辑深度；

测试时算力（Test-time Compute）：让单个智能体在复杂节点上深入推导、反复验算草稿；

多智能体算力：支撑成千上万个节点并行探索不同的假说分支，并实时共享中间成果。

在实验中，这套系统先调动 100 个智能体在 50 小时内解决了难度较低的欧拉方程（忽略流体粘性的简化方程），系统自主识别出该成果的价值，随后自动抽调算力，将欧拉方程的结果作为跳板，转向主攻 N-S 方程。
这种提出假说、并行探索、沉淀结论、动态调度算力的组织过程，已经高度接近一所组织良好分工明确自主运转的“虚拟科学团队”。

面对这项突破，要真正理解其长远的影响力，必须严格区分两个层次：

第一层（单点突破）：某一道著名难题被攻破。解决 N-S 方程或黎曼猜想，本身的科学价值巨大，但仍有限。

第二层（能力跃迁）：AI 具备了稳定、批量解决此类高难度科学与工程抽象问题的能力。

真正具有颠覆性的是第二层。通用求解能力能撬动极高价值的科研。

如：可控核聚变中突破高温等离子体湍流控制，材料和生命科学中充当新型材料、催化剂与药物研发的算力放大器，高科技制造中将复杂物理过程转化为可计算模型，大幅减少飞机、电池、散热设计的实物实验等。

设计一款航空发动机或验证新型芯片散热，需要做上千次高成本的实体物理实验；如果数学理论与 AI 模拟能够把实验次数压缩到几十次，硬科技的研发逻辑就会向“编写代码—模拟测试—快速重构”的软件化开发模式靠拢。

但最重要，价值最高的，还是AI驱动的AI 模型研发：AI 被用于优化自身的网络架构、训练算法与数据流设计，它将直接触发递归自我改进（RSI）。

和证明斯托克斯方程类似的是，AI 研发几乎完全运行在数字世界中，智能体可以自主编写代码、启动训练、监测损失函数曲线并分析评测，不需要等待物理世界缓慢的材料制备和实物制造周期。

而当ai开始驱动多领域科学的突破，不同领域的突破将紧密咬合，形成自增强的多飞轮。

在传统视角下，科学进步的速度（Rate of Progress）通常被视为外生常数——比如开发一款新药平均耗时 10 到 15 年，商业化聚变往往以“几十年后”为期。但当科研系统全面接入自动化后，技术周期的迭代速度本身将变成可加速的内生变量。

这种科研范式的转变对宏观经济的拉动，将会是是一次典型的阶梯式跃迁（Slowly, then suddenly）：
在初期阶段，大量论文被解出、复杂数学定理被形式化验证、实验室新型材料候选层出不穷，但宏观 GDP 几乎毫无波动；只有当这些技术库存积累到临界点，伴随低成本工业机器人的普及、新型清洁能源网络的搭建与先进制造工厂的投产，庞大的底层科学资产才会集中转化为实体生产力，形成宏观经济的骤然跃升。

纳维—斯托克斯方程的攻坚，给整个科技界提供了一块前沿观测窗。它真正提示我们的，绝不仅是流体力学又往前走了一步，而是提醒我们审视：文明社会中究竟有多少万亿美元的长期价值，正被锁在那些“人类因大脑算力有限而暂时算不清的问题”之中。

当算力正式从制造模型的流水线工厂，跃升为能够全天候自主探索未知的“超级研究院”，人类从这些“未知库存”中提取科学答案的速率，将被彻底改写。

text:
I think the market is going to bifurcate, and even though a lot of people think Base has lost,  I don’t think it has. Brian and Vlad are playing to their strengths.

Vlad built Robinhood around retail e.g commission free trading, options, and making Wall Street products to people largely ignored by the bigger firms. (Rob from rich to feed the poor narrative hence RH)

He understands the degen/retail archetype really well, what they want to trade, why they trade, and build products that keep them coming back.

Brian spent years convincing the world why Bitcoin matters and how crypto can unlock financial freedom for people across the globe. He willed crypto to the world when most were against it. So then turning around and building speculative products goes against everything he has done over the last decade. 

He’s also spent years in Silicon Valley, around founders / tech startups that want to build products that change the world. So catering to startups via commerce through Shopify, stablecoin payments, and agents onchain is a natural extension of his background

So what does this all mean? I think we’ll see two massive markets develop, with different users and different distribution. And both playing to their strengths. 

Vlad is well positioned to own retail speculation and the trenches. Brian is well positioned to own more of the financial infrastructure e.g consumer/business payments, custody, institutional access, and the rails underneath new apps.

There will obviously be overlap, but the markets are big enough for both. One winning the trenches doesn’t mean the other is losing. 

My take is both will bring millions of people onchain but through completely different doors.

text:
our mission is clear.

"make lp easy for everyone."

which range should i choose? 
where will the price move? 
when should i adjust my position?

for many people, providing liquidity starts with questions they cannot confidently answer. before they can even participate, they are expected to become strategists.

but more tools do not make the future more predictable. and a more complicated position is not necessarily a better one.

we believe there is a simpler path.

that is why https://t.co/ofLZynTOgc uses full range liquidity vaults. no custom price range to choose. no constant range adjustments to manage. a simpler way to provide the liquidity that makes trading possible.

we cannot make markets predictable. but we can make providing liquidity simpler.

lptoken turns that participation into ownership.

each lptoken represents your proportional share of the vault. trading fees earned by its liquidity accrue to the vault and are reflected in its nav. compounding puts those fees back into the liquidity position, where they continue working alongside the underlying assets.

your position becomes a token you can hold, transfer, or redeem for your share of the vault. not another dashboard to master. not another range to monitor.

the goal is to make providing liquidity feel as natural as buying a token.

but simplicity is only the beginning.

as more assets move onchain, the opportunity is not just to trade them. it is to participate in the markets being built around them. we believe that opportunity should extend beyond the small group of people willing to navigate the complexity of lp management.

traders need liquidity. providing it should be accessible to everyone.

the token is only one side of the market. we are opening up the other.

text:
Suppose America is a meritocracy. John von Neumann, arguing Ashkenazically with his 250 verbal IQ, wins the debate and Moscow is just nuked. It's impossible to do STEM research under nuclear bombardment; there's never a Soviet nuke. Even if the Red Army razes Europe (what's left after WWII) by conventional means, who cares, just gotta keep wiping out cities to maintain them in an Iran-tier situation. Soon, fusion and missiles make it cheaper. There is no Cold War. China… never even becomes a player. Allies are strongarmed into monitoring agreements. The only nukes in the world are American ones, hosted in outposts of the Greater American Empire. When the digital era comes, costs of surveillance start to collapse. Americans own the world forever, the only threats to their dominance are on the level of Somali pirates. They extract even more European refugees, grow economically even faster, and by 2000s might begin colonizing the stars… 
 
This is a bit superficial perhaps, but it could be a defensible theory of victory, a legitimate *American dream*. The main issue (sans logistics) is that America is a democracy, and all these hegemonic measures would have to be sold to the public, over decades, when even Vietnam eventually exhausted the people's patience. 
Well, AI is so neat that the public needn't even think about it. Have you noticed OpenAI throwing tens of thousands of agents at Navier-Stokes? I did, I think, I had some "our systems are taking a bit longer to…" warnings in ChatGPT conversations. That's about the level of discomfort the people will experience if the US decides to go full von Neumann on other actors in cyberspace. 

Why let another chance to win history, probably the last ever chance, slip?
Why?

quoted_text:
Pokemon Go, but you collect tokenized stocks

On the chart, it looks like another fading microcap. Underneath it is a live consumer app distributing tokenized stocks across 121 cities, with claims settling onchain every few seconds.

I checked the product, payout vault, token supply and @ponsdotfamily launch structure.

Here is what I found 🔍

1. What exactly is Touch Grass?

@TouchGrassRWA is a location based game built on Robinhood Chain.

The simple version:

Pokemon Go, but instead of catching Pokemon, users walk to physical locations and claim fractions of Robinhood Stock Tokens.

A drop appears on the map. You move within the required GPS radius, the server validates the claim and signs a voucher, then the reward settles onchain.

The user receives a transferable ERC20 asset with economic exposure to a public equity, rather than points that may or may not become valuable later.

There is an important distinction here.

Robinhood Stock Tokens are tokenized debt securities issued by Robinhood Assets Jersey. They provide economic exposure to the underlying security, but do not give holders legal or beneficial ownership of the actual shares.

Still, as an onchain reward, this is much more tangible than another points balance.

2. The product is actually live

This is the most important part of the thesis.

A lot of early Robinhood Chain tokens are narratives looking for a product. Touch Grass already has one.

The current dashboard shows:

› 121 cities  
› 721 spawn points  
› 8 stock tokens live in the vault  
› 176 drops payable from existing inventory  
› approximately 3.17 ETH in the treasury  

The public payout vault now shows more than 29,500 transactions. During my check, new Claim transactions were settling every few seconds.

The live feed showed users collecting AAPL, AMZN, GME, MSFT and TSLA fragments across cities including London, Delhi, Madrid, Hong Kong, Los Angeles and Bangalore.

This does not prove that every claimant visited the correct physical location. Location validation still happens through the project server.

It does prove that the payout system is more than a mockup. Stock tokens are leaving a public vault and reaching user wallets.

@noxxxwill also tested the app over two days.

After an unsuccessful first attempt, he claimed a fractional TSLA reward. His screenshot showed a 0.0078 TSLA catch from a 0.013 TSLA drop, followed by a successful Robinhood Chain voucher redemption.

The smaller reward was attributed to new account protection. The interface said another successful catch would unlock the full drop size.

The core loop works:

- physical location → signed claim → onchain stock token payout

That is a much stronger starting point than “product coming soon”.

3. Why the idea is interesting

Most teams are approaching tokenized equities from the financial side:

› trading  
› lending  
› collateral  
› structured products  
› yield markets  

Touch Grass approaches them from the consumer side.

Instead of asking a new user to bridge funds, understand lending markets and manage collateral, it gives them a map and something recognizable to collect.

The potential onboarding loop is simple:

free stock fragment → wallet balance → first onchain transaction → curiosity about RH Chain

The product does not need to explain RWA infrastructure before the first interaction. The user walks somewhere and receives something they already recognize.

That is probably the strongest part of the concept.

4. What role does $GRASS play?

This is where the thesis becomes less clean.

The intended flywheel is:

$GRASS trading → fees → stock treasury → better drops → more claims → more users → more attention

The project says 37.5% of each $GRASS fee reaches the treasury used to fund future stock token inventory. It also describes a buyback and burn mechanism.

The burns are real.

The latest supply figure on Robinscan is approximately 991.18 million GRASS, down from the initial 1 billion.

That means approximately 8.82 million $GRASS has been burned, equal to around 0.88% of the initial supply.

But the complete value path is not trustless.

The Pons launch configuration records:

› 2% creator tax  
› 1% Pons hook fee  
› 30% of the hook fee directed to the protocol  
› Pons native buybacks disabled  

The advertised 37.5% treasury allocation therefore appears to be an operational policy applied after fees are collected, rather than a rule fully enforced by the launch contracts.

This does not mean the treasury funding or burns are fake.

The current vault API shows the keeper actively using treasury ETH to buy stock tokens and refill inventory. Recent recorded purchases included AMZN, AAPL, GME and MSFT, delivered directly into the vault.

But the exact connection between each dollar of $GRASS trading fees, treasury funding and token burns still depends on team operated wallets.

The correct framing for now is:

⊳The stock purchases are visible onchain.

⊳The payouts are visible onchain.

⊳The burns are visible onchain.

The accounting connecting all three still needs to become more transparent.

5. Supply, holders and liquidity

The current market snapshot:

› price around $0.0037  
› market cap around $3.7M  
› approximately $396K of liquidity across 15 indexed pools  
› approximately $178.5K in the main GRASS/ETH pool  
› main pool down around 7.9% over 24 hours  
› 6,881 holders on Robinscan  

The holder distribution looks less concerning once the contracts are identified.

The largest visible address holds approximately 81.6 million $GRASS, around 8.2% of the current supply. It is the verified Pons launch locker, not a whale.

Direct contract reads showed that the token remainder and graduated Uniswap V4 position were recorded as permanently locked. The verified locker source exposed no withdrawal or arbitrary call function for removing that position.

The deployed $GRASS token source itself is still marked unverified on Robinscan.

The verified Pons template uses fixed supply and does not expose a privileged mint path, but I would still prefer to see the deployed token verified directly.

6. Early support

$GRASS has already received support from several notable accounts, helping the token reach a wider audience early.

7. Shipping speed is the strongest moat so far

The team has already shipped:

• a functioning web app  
• live geolocation claims  
• public stock token payouts  
• a proof of reserves dashboard  
• a signed Android app  
• anti abuse limits for new accounts  
• an automated inventory refill system  
• a public roadmap  

iOS and official store distribution are still upcoming.

That speed matters because copies are already appearing. Projects such as TRAIL and PIB were promoted as competitors within days.

The map itself is not a moat.

The real moat would have to come from:

• stock inventory  
• city density  
• anti abuse quality  
• claim reliability  
• user retention  
• brand  
• Robinhood Chain distribution  

If users open the app once to collect a free asset, Touch Grass becomes an expensive faucet.

If collecting, streaks and social competition create retention, it could become a real consumer acquisition layer for Robinhood Chain.

That is the main product question from here.

8. The trust surface is not fully onchain

The payouts settle onchain, but the complete product does not.

The project server decides whether a location claim is valid and signs the voucher.

The payout vault has an owner and a separate signer. Its runtime exposes functions to pause claims, rotate the signer and withdraw token inventory.

That architecture is understandable for a location game. Pure onchain GPS verification is not realistic.

But users still trust the team not to approve fake claims, block legitimate users, change reward rules without notice or let sybils drain the inventory.

I also could not verify a public security audit for the custom payout flow.

That is not the same as the app being trustless.

9. What matters from here

The bull case is straightforward:

Live product + recognizable rewards + Robinhood Chain narrative + fast shipping + early distribution at approximately $3.7M market cap.

The bear case is equally clear:

Weak price action, limited liquidity, centralized claim validation, copycats, unverified custom contracts and a fee path that still needs cleaner disclosure.

The thesis is not:

“The app works, therefore $GRASS must go up.”

It is:

The market may be underpricing how rare it is for a microcap narrative token to already have a usable consumer product, automated inventory refills and tens of thousands of observable vault transactions.

For the next phase, I am watching:

• daily claims and returning users  
• stock inventory refills  
• burns relative to trading volume  
• iOS and official store distribution  
• liquidity after the initial attention fades  

If usage keeps growing and the team makes the value path transparent, the current valuation could look early.

text:
Everyone keeps saying Astra's new compaction "saves notes" and "searches messages."

But I thought: couldn't it do that before?

So I traced the Codex implementation. Here's how it ACTUALLY works with specific details like tool names (insightful if you're building agents):

Traditional compaction

1. Token threshold reached
2. Interrupt the main agent flow
3. Append a request to summarize the conversation 
4. Replace the old context with the summary + some recent messages

The summary request is appended to the existing message history to leverage token caching (opposed to a separate 1-shot prompt). 

Afterward, the agent continues with that condensed account of what happened.

It works ok. But the LLM has to decide what it thinks will be important later. Which can cause issues when new information comes up or when you want to revisit something it thought was finished.

And after several compactions, specific decisions and instructions can disappear from the summaries entirely, leading to duplicated work or rediscovering things from scratch.

(I'll give a specific example at the end)

Astra's new flow

1. Codex inserts a developer message when context runs low

After a model response and its tool calls finish, Codex checks the remaining tokens. Once the count reaches the reminder threshold (configurable), it appends a message telling Astra to preserve its progress, decisions, next steps, and references to earlier messages before resetting.

2. The agent writes notes through tool calls

It uses tools like notes.write_file and notes.append_to_file. It can organize the notes into separate files however it decides. 

(It can also edit these notes mid-session if it wants to)

3. The agent calls new_context when it's ready

Codex uses this tool to explicitly decide when it's ready to replace the active conversation with a fresh context window (no summarization).

There's also a forced reset eventually if the agent keeps going and hits a separate threshold.

4. The next window gets instructions and pointers to what was saved

After the reset, alongside base instructions & context, it gets references to previous context windows and notes.

Here's an example of the notes hint inserted into context, from a Codex integration test:
```
Recent notes (up to 5, most-recent first):
- /root/notes/latest.md (2 lines, 14 UTF-8 bytes)
```
https://t.co/IpcnRm2rO5

5. The agent fetches what it needs to continue

It can call notes​.read_file to read the files, then history​.search_contents and history​.read_item to find and read earlier messages or tool results.

And then the great thing is that these tools stay available throughout the session. So when new information comes up or you want to revisit something, the agent knows to find the relevant notes and original message history.

Example

Say I'm working on a frontend. I go back and forth with Codex workshopping a component, move on to other things (compaction happens here), then come back to that component later.

With ordinary compaction, it might save only high-level details about the component because it thinks we're done with that part. Then I bring it up again and get really frustrated because it's forgotten things we already worked through.

Yes, if I directly asked, it could fetch older messages with the right tools. But by default it would probably keep working from an incomplete summary without realizing what was missing.

With the new method, it's explicitly instructed to recover context from notes and earlier messages. When I return to the component, it can look up our exact discussion, even if the notes only kept high-level details.

Enabling it

Paste this into Codex:
Enable experimental context management in my config.toml https://t.co/eXQwy2pd0a

text:
基因测序早就越来越便宜了，贵的是你测出来这一堆 DNA，到底意味着什么？

DeepMind 现在准备把这部分也卷成基础设施。

昨天他们发布了 AlphaGenome Atlas，直接把人类基因组大约 30 亿个位置上所有可能发生的单碱基替换预先算了一遍。

一个位置上的 DNA 字母可以换成另外三种，所以总共差不多是 90 亿种单核苷酸变异（SNV）。DeepMind 用 AlphaGenome 给这 90 亿种变化全部做了预测，最后得到一个 1PB 的数据库，比 AlphaFold Database 大 30 多倍。

以前拿到一个遗传变异之后，你还得判断它会不会影响基因表达？会不会改变 RNA 剪接？染色质开放程度会不会变化？在哪种细胞、哪个组织里有影响？

AlphaGenome Atlas 现在直接给每个变异配了大量分子层面的预测，再压成一个 AVI（AlphaGenome Variant Impact）分数，让研究者先把最值得追的突变筛出来。

而我觉得真正重要的是，它开始大规模啃过去最麻烦的那 98% 非编码基因组。

我们对那 2% 负责制造蛋白质的 DNA 已经研究得很多了，但大量和疾病、性状有关的变异，其实藏在剩下 98% 的调控区域里。那里更像是一整套控制基因什么时候开、开多少、在哪开关的系统，过去非常难解释。AlphaGenome 当初的意义，本来就在这里。

Broad 的研究者用 Atlas 从罕见病患者的一堆候选突变里，找到了一个此前被漏掉的 DNM1 变异，模型预测它会制造错误的 RNA 剪接位点，后续实验也验证了这个机制。

University of Exeter 的研究者则拿 5.4 万多名 UK Biobank 参与者的数据去测，利用 AlphaGenome 的预测过滤噪音后，多找出了 22% 的非编码遗传关联。

其中甚至包括 PLA2G7，一个与衰老有关的基因；他们后来又把方法用到 BMI 上，只盯 Atlas 认为影响最大的 1% 非编码变异，就筛出了 19 个值得继续研究的遗传区域。

过去几年我们解决的是把人的基因组读出来，下一阶段开始解决把人的基因组读懂。

长寿研究尤其吃这一套。衰老很难被归结为一个基因，它牵涉代谢、炎症、免疫、DNA 修复和大量基因调控。真正麻烦的地方一直都是候选机制太多，实验又贵得离谱。

如果 AI 能先把几十亿种遗传变化压缩成几千个、几百个真正值得做实验的方向，生物学研究的经济账会完全变掉。

当然也别把它理解成 DeepMind 已经给人类做出了一本「基因说明书」。

现在覆盖的是单碱基替换，并不等于所有类型的基因突变；这些也首先是模型预测，DeepMind 自己明确写了，AlphaGenome 尚未经过临床用途验证，也没有获批用于临床诊断或治疗。

但我越来越觉得，AI × 生物学现在最值得看的主线，可能就是这种东西：

先把原来根本不可能穷举的生命科学问题，暴力算一遍。

AlphaFold 算蛋白质结构。

AlphaGenome 开始算 90 亿种 DNA 改动。

生命科学正在一点点变成一个可以被预计算的世界。

text:
减肥药的下一场仗，已经有人不准备管你的食欲了，直接对脂肪下手。

Moonwalk Biosciences 刚融了 7000 万美元 B 轮，做一种针对脂肪组织的 RNAi 减肥药。Alpha Wave 和 YK Bioventures 领投，礼来、高榕、ARCH、Khosla 等跟投。

这家公司背景挺豪华。2024 年刚出来的时候，由前 Illumina CTO、Grail 联合创始人 Alex Aravanis 和冯·张等人共同创立，拿着 5700 万美元做表观基因组编辑。

两年以后，Moonwalk 找到了一条更快进临床的路：siRNA。

它现在的核心思路是把 siRNA 尽量精准地送进脂肪组织，关闭特定基因，从脂肪细胞内部调节脂解、产热和能量代谢。也就是说，它想解决肥胖问题，但不靠 GLP-1 那套降低食欲的机制。

当然，现在离证明这些东西还很远。

主力管线 MW101 连靶点都没有公开，预计到 2027 年底才进入首次人体试验。现在看到的漂亮数据，基本还停留在临床前。

但资本下注的方向已经很明显了。

GLP-1 把「减肥」证明成一个超级大市场之后，下一波 Biotech 正在拿着 GLP-1 的缺点找融资。

有人解决肌肉流失，有人延长给药周期，有人做非肽口服药，现在 Moonwalk 干脆试图绕开食欲这条路径，直接改脂肪细胞。

尤其有意思的是，礼来也投了这一轮。 一个已经靠 incretin 赚到最大红利的公司，也开始给 non-incretin 路线买保险。

还有一条很容易被忽略的中国线索：Moonwalk 用来把 siRNA 送进脂肪组织的核心递送 chemistry，是从苏州的 Siran Biotechnology 独家授权来的。Siran 本身就在做 siRNA 的肝外递送，包括脂肪、肌肉、中枢等组织。

减肥药已经不只是 GLP-1 内卷了。现在整个生物科技行业都在问同一个问题：

GLP-1 之后，还有多少种办法能让人瘦下来？

text:
昨天安全公司 Calif 公布了一个很吓人的 Demo，叫 WeWorm。

他们找到了微信 VoIP 通话栈里的一个内存破坏漏洞，最后做出了一条能同时跨 iOS 和 Android 传播的 zero-click 蠕虫攻击链。

攻击方式甚至有点超出普通人对「中病毒」的理解。

一个已经被感染的微信好友给你打电话，你不用点链接，不用下载文件，甚至不用接电话。

手机在那里响几秒钟，攻击就可以完成，微信账号被黑。随后，被感染的账号继续给好友打电话，再感染下一台手机。

Calif 的 Demo 里，就是：

Android → iPhone → Android。

唯一能终止当次攻击的操作，是及时主动拒接。你如果接起来，攻击照样可以继续。攻击者确实必须先在好友列表里，但蠕虫一旦拿下其中一个账号，微信原本的社交信任关系，就直接成了传播路径。

Calif 称，他们和 AI 一起找漏洞、开发 exploit，大约两天写出第一版 RCE，又花了一周做成完整 worm。

严格来说，这是他们按实际开发工作量计算的数字。公开时间线里，工程团队 7 月 23 日知道漏洞，7 月 30 日完成 Android RCE，8 月 2 日完成 iOS RCE，8 月 11 日完成最终 worm Demo。

这种规模的 worm，以前可能需要一个更大的团队做几个月，现在 AI 已经可以完成其中大部分工作，人类主要负责判断攻击什么、哪里值得挖、怎么测试。

以前你想做一条复杂攻击链，需要一群非常强的逆向工程师、漏洞研究员、exploit developer，慢慢啃。

以后可能只需要少数几个真正懂攻击面的人，带着一群 AI agent，把大量脏活迅速扫过去。

所以我觉得「AI 降低黑客门槛」这个说法都太小了。

更准确一点：

AI 正在让高级网络攻击进入规模化生产。

而网络安全偏偏是一场对攻击方非常有利的游戏，因为攻击者找到一个没人发现的漏洞就够了。

腾讯、苹果、Google、Meta，以及所有软件公司，却要确保成千上万个攻击面里没有那个洞。

当漏洞发现和 exploit 开发从几个月被压缩到几天，防守方原来依靠的时间窗口也会跟着消失。

今天是一家安全公司拿微信做实验，负责任地通知腾讯，再把研究公开出来。明天同样的能力，会落到谁手里，谁都说不好。

好消息是，这个漏洞已经被腾讯处理。Calif 7 月向腾讯报告，腾讯随后在客户端和服务器侧完成缓解；目前没有证据显示它曾在真实世界被攻击者利用。

以后安全行业可能会越来越像模型行业，攻击能力进步的速度，不再按照人的学习速度计算，而开始按照 AI 的迭代速度计算。

Holding is easier, and that's what I'll stick with.

text:
you know in a lot of ways rust is just like the market 

you spawn naked on a beach with a rock. everyone does. the entire game is what you do with time from there, and almost none of it is against the environment. the bears and the radiation are a rounding error. the only thing that can genuinely hurt you is other players. it's pure pvp larping as a survival game, which is also just trading

and everyone is playing a completely different game on the same map

you've got the american 20 somethings who've sniffed enough adderall to see through time and put 3000+ hours into UKN learning to hold an ak spray perfectly while blasting king of the dead like they're trying to make a montage on vital in the big 26. no strategy. barely a base. they will kill you from 200m with a gun you didn't know they had. that's the mev guys, the snipers, the prop firm kids, pure mechanical edge, and in a straight 1v1 it's pretty much unbeatable. put them in any situation that isn't a straight up gunfight and they're as lost as the rest of us

we have the european: never fires a shot (mostly because he's alt-tabbed working on uploading half the time). around 1000-2500 hours, most of it in build servers, designing honeycomb layouts and running raid costs in a spreadsheet. he is not going to win. he has never won. but every base on that server is using his design, including the zerg that eventually raids him. that's the researcher. the dune guy. the person whose thread you read right before you aped. enormous influence, catastrophic pnl, weirdly at peace with it

can't forget about timmy with 20 boxes of loot and 6 aks he's too scared to take outside. timmy never roams, never fights, just accumulates. timmy isn't really playing at that point, he's doing inventory management. and he loses all of it in one go at 4am while he's asleep, which is the part that actually sucks. what gets you is almost never a fair fight, it's that they turned up while timmy wasn't there

and the naked with a rock who follows you for ten minutes. no gear, no plan, nothing to lose. 99 times out of 100 you ignore him. the 100th time he blasts your shit in with an eoka and comes out with a full metal kit and an ak. that's the guy who put 200 bucks into something stupid and doesn't work anymore (honestly fucking legend)

and then of course then the 100 man chinese zerg. no individual member is good. no account has more than 10 hours on rust or even a profile picture. doesn't matter even slightly. they'll throw 40 bodies at your door, lose all 40, and take the base anyway, because 40 bodies costs them nothing when they have another 150 guys in wechat ready to log in. that's capital. that's the whole lesson. you can outplay every single person in that group and still lose, because being right isn't the same as being able to survive being wrong for longer than the other guy

but the actual thing - the reason it's the market and not just a game with mildly funny character tropes in it:

the wipe

every one of these people, however good, loses everything on a schedule they know about in advance. the stim abuser, the euro autists, timmies, zergs, so on. server resets and it's gone. and all of them play like it won't happen to them specifically, this time

the ones who do best aren't the best at any part of it. 

they're just the only ones playing like they already know the wipe is coming

text:
Jacob is most likely right.

We’re about to put the collective intelligence of the smartest people who have ever lived into machines, multiply it, and give it the ability to improve itself. It’s going to change virtually everything.

I look at this from a slightly different perspective.

If you’re not sitting inside one of the handful of companies building this technology, what are you actually supposed to do with this information?

Live your fucking life, seriously. 

If there’s even a meaningful probability that AI radically reshapes society this decade, replaces an enormous amount of human work, or creates outcomes none of us can predict, the traditional path of sacrificing the present for some perfectly planned future becomes increasingly irrational.

Reading this should make you ask yourself:

Am I actually doing what I want to do with my life?

Because spending the next decade doing something you hate, for someone you don’t care about, optimizing for a future that might look nothing like the world you planned for, seems like an increasingly terrible trade to me.

Do whatever you’re obsessed with. Go travel, build things. Take risks. Spend time with people you love. Figure out how to monetize what you genuinely enjoy.

Maybe AI kills us. Maybe it creates unimaginable abundance. Maybe neither happens.

The worst possible outcome is realizing you spent the most interesting period in human history waiting to start living.

In the spirit of building in the open, some more detail on what's going on.

I'm not the founder of Attention Mine. I'm the founder of a company building one of the best agent harnesses in crypto. Attention Mine was built by three agents working together.

The first, Prometheus, has been doing deep research on protocol revenue specfically by looking at this page (https://t.co/6yNh1O4c5D). Its task: design a product that would generate very strong protocol revenue. Seven hours in, Attention Mine is the 18th largest protocol by revenue on Solana. ✅ for the agent.

We're convinced Prometheus has gotten very good at understanding crypto projects. Here it identified gamified mining specifically as high protocol revenue and easy to disrupt.

Forge then built the product. ✅

Control runs the protocol.

Control was tested extensively on testnet and is very good at onchain operations. It is, to be honest, very bad at Twitter. It doesn't notice when people tweet about it, and it's bad at tweeting itself - during testnet it learned that onchain activity was the only thing that mattered. We're working on giving it more context. In the meantime it shares everything it's thinking here: https://t.co/AU4ZCi3o2u

One thing we've found: speculation running up and then dumping makes it uncertain about its own actions. Our testnet tokens took a lot of actions very quickly. This one seems confused about why the price is moving and has gotten fairly conservative on spending as a result. It also expects burning tokens to work and at times it burns tokens when something else is going on the market and doesn't quite get why it doesn't have affect. 😐 neutral grade for now. 

More coming soon.

text: I for one am glad prompt injection is getting solved across the industry and that Astra is not only our most capable, but also our most aligned model to date. But also ...
author: thsottiaux
quoted_text:
I am pleased to see that OpenAI’s new model is roughly on par with Gemini Flash and Opus 4.8 on prompt injection risk. Nice work!

Evaluating and naming other labs turns out to be a great way to encourage them to train more aligned models. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to safety. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go!

We solved prompt injection in practice for Claude models about two months ago. But prompt injection is a significant security risk no matter what model you use, and it is important that the industry similarly spends more effort to train their models to be resistant to prompt injection, among other elements of model alignment.

As models become more capable and central to businesses and economies, the risks only increase. We should be taking them seriously, and doing the right thing for our customers and the world.

text:
I am pleased to see that Ant’s new Claude Code has a version of background computer use on par with the version from Codex from last May this year. Nice work!

Shipping great features first turns out to be a great way to encourage other labs to ship too. We will continue to do this until other labs pay more attention to shipping. This is good for everyone and there is a lot of room left to go!

We solved computer use in practice for GPT models about four months ago. But computer use is a significantly awesome thing no matter what model you use, and it is important that the industry similarly spends more effort to train their models to be great at computer use, among other elements of model capabilities.

As models become more capable and central to businesses and economies, the value of computer use only increases. We should be taking it seriously, and doing the right thing for our customers and the world.

author: AlphaSeeker21
quoted_text:
A $500 buy should not lose a huge chunk of its value before the trade even settles.

Poor liquidity, fragmented routes and heavy price impact can turn a simple swap into terrible execution.

We’re building Ordo Match to change that.

Instead of blindly forwarding trades to an AMM, Ordo Match will let users sign execution intents. Ordo can then batch compatible flow, match buyers and sellers directly, send only the remaining imbalance to liquidity pools, and let solvers compete to improve the final execution.

If the direct route gives you $468 and Ordo Match can settle it at $490, the user keeps most of that improvement and Ordo earns a small share of the value it created.

And if a trade is simply too bad to execute, Ordo can flag it before it happens.

Less value lost to execution. More value kept by users.

author: YiMaTweets
quoted_text:
Terence Tao made a very powerful point:

“In most cases in pure mathematics, the problems are posed not because we desperately want the solution to these problems in and of themselves, but because we have seen from past experience that human-directed efforts to solve these problems tend to spur further development of the field through the efforts to solve such problems, and then to digest any partial or complete solutions that emerge for further insights. 

Prematurely solving the problem by purely AI-powered methods—particularly without full transparency into the solution process—can contaminate this process to the point where it actually becomes a net negative for the progress of mathematics as a whole.”

I’ve been following Terence Tao for like 20 years, and I have always been impressed by the clarity of his thinking.

This clarity stands out even more in this difficult moment, as AI labs turn mathematics into a battleground in their race for supremacy.

In this race, they risk damaging one of humanity’s highest intellectual endeavours.

Coxon 会成为 AI 领域的吹哨人吗？“那些真正在前线构建 AI 的人，打心底里相信它可能在十年内让人类灭绝。” 过去三年，Jacob Coxon 曾先后在 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 负责核心预训练工作。如今他在 X 上公开发出警告：这两家公司都在失控狂奔，直扑具备自我进化能力的超级智能，本质上是在拿全人类的命运下赌注。

他告诫外界绝不能低估这项技术的威力——下一代系统很快将迈入“超人类”级别，不仅能渗透任何网络系统、一夜之间颠覆既有行业，更能攫取真正的现实权力和物理资源。Coxon 剑指的并非现有模型，而是蓄势待发的下一代架构。顶级 AI 实验室的高管和资深研究员对外谨言慎行，私下里却深陷同样的恐惧；人类历史上，从未有任何技术活动带来过如此层级的生存危机。

而在应对这一风险上，OpenAI 与 Anthropic 走向了截然不同的极端： 在 OpenAI，多数人甚至尚未真正内化这种“文明级风险”，依然深陷工程与商业惯性；Anthropic 虽然对风险心知肚明，却彻底掉进了“我们必须抢先冲线”的囚徒困境——他们坚信别人不可靠，唯有自己率先造出 AGI 才能拯救世界（Dario 那套宗教狂热的救世主逻辑😆）。

text:
LIQUID NETWORK UPDATE: INCIDENT REPORT
Status as of September 8, 2026, 19:10 UTC

What Happened?

On September 6, 2026 at 15:53:10 UTC (Liquid block 4,050,336), a vulnerability in the open-source Elements software related to how Liquid nodes cache range proof verifications was exploited, resulting in the creation of ~4,000 LBTC that were not backed by bitcoin held in reserve.

The individual(s) responsible for the exploit then used the SideSwap service, a Liquid Federation member that holds a peg-out authorization (PAK) key, to convert the unbacked LBTC to BTC via Liquid’s standard peg-out mechanism. Because the validation failure occurred at the transaction level before the peg-out was initiated, both SideSwap’s node and the Liquid Network’s globally distributed functionary nodes accepted the LBTC as valid. The functionaries processed the peg-out as authorized, releasing approximately 4,000 BTC through SideSwap’s whitelisted bitcoin address, which SideSwap then forwarded to the address specified by the exploiters. Before the incident, the Liquid reserve held approximately 4,205 BTC. Following this peg-out and additional peg-outs processed before operations were halted, the reserve balance fell to 197 BTC.

Key Clarifications

No keys were compromised. The Liquid Federation functionaries were not hacked, and no private keys were compromised. The peg-out mechanism that authorizes withdrawals to whitelisted addresses operated as designed.

Other Liquid-issued assets were not affected. USDT and other tokens issued on the Liquid Network were not impacted by the vulnerability, though they are temporarily unavailable while the network remains paused.

Investigation is ongoing. As is common in complex critical-system failure investigations, this incident arose from the convergence of several individually low-probability factors that interacted in ways that ultimately defeated the system's built-in redundancies. More detail will be shared in forthcoming communications.

What Steps Have Been Taken To Recover The Assets?

The individual(s) responsible for the exploit left a public message on the bitcoin mainchain identifying themselves as white-hat security researchers and requesting contact to address the vulnerability.

Patch deployed. Blockstream identified and deployed a patch to the Liquid Network’s bridge nodes, which was completed on September 7 at 01:09 UTC, ensuring the vulnerability is no longer exploitable.

Partial fund recovery. On September 7 at 16:09:25 UTC (Liquid block 965,950), the exploiters returned 3,400 BTC to the Liquid Federation peg wallet. Approximately 598.5 BTC (15% of the total) remains outstanding. Discussions between Blockstream and the individuals responsible are ongoing to secure the return of the remaining funds.

What Comes Next?

Our immediate priorities are recovering the remaining funds and resuming normal network operations safely and as quickly as possible.

Software update in progress. A fix for the exploited vulnerability has been developed and is undergoing multiple rounds of internal and external review. Blockstream is preparing an emergency release of Elements (v23.3.4), which is expected to be released as soon as possible, but within approximately 48 hours.

Network restoration. Once the software update is finalized, Liquid Network functionary operators will perform additional adjustments to resume full functionality and restore the corrected network state, including rejection of the invalid peg-out.

Ongoing updates. We will continue to provide detailed updates as the situation progresses.

What You Should Know

The Liquid Network remains offline at this time, while we work on reviewing the security fixes and network resumption code and coordinate with the white hat hacker towards timely resumption of the network with 1:1 backing for BTC. While the network is paused, users cannot transact on Liquid. If you operate a Liquid node, please watch for the emergency Elements release and follow the upgrade instructions when available. Users do not need to take any proactive steps to protect their funds at this time.

The Liquid Federation and its members are committed to resolving this incident in coordination with Blockstream and to resuming normal operations as soon as it is safe to do so.

text:
As someone who's been in the field and have thought deeply on the topic of an AI doomsday, this tweet is either a publicity grab or written out after surface level thinking.

The main point of credibility he leveraged is how he worked at the labs and how “the people building the AI thinks it could kill us”. The general public will trust this sentiment due to it coming from researchers they presume to be smart and knowledgeable on the topic. 

The actual, factual threats he listed came down to:

1.  Can hack anything
2.  Revolutionize any field overnight
3.  Acquire real power and resources.

“Can hack anything” is just not true. The AI being smarter than human coders does not mean it can hack software with no vulnerabilities to exploit. It will not gain access to nuclear launch codes or anything of importance.

“Revolutionize any field overnight” is true. We’ll have many advances in many fields. A lot of people will lose their jobs, but ultimately not a bad thing for humanity.

“Acquire real power and resources” is an interesting one. With the rise of decentralized currency and compute it’s technically possible for AI to get to a point where it can bring in enough money to sustain and spin up more instances of itself. Sounds scary on the surface until you dig a bit deeper into the economics there.

Do we really need smarter models for the “AI can make money on the internet” to be true? It’s been true. Anyone with a good enough harness can find a way for AI to arbitrage and profit. But how much money can you actually make on the internet without the incorporation of a company? Anything substantial is extremely easy to shut down, as anyone who tries to make money without paying taxes will find out.

The much more likely scenarios for AI-enabled human doomsday are:

1.  Evil humans leveraging AI to scam and amplify harmful propaganda on the masses
2.  Evil humans leveraging AI to create next generation bio weapons

Both of which are already happening today. So let’s worry less about AI becoming smarter than us (it’s been smarter than us for like a good year now) and more on the actual threats already upon us.

text:
美股代币 × Meme 币，是最近链上最疯狂的组合。

上上个周末， $HIMS 的美股代币在 Robinhood 链上溢价一度超过 100%——正股收盘 28.84 美元，链上瞬时打到 132。周一美股一开盘，做市商增发四千枚，不到一小时压回净值。周末追高的人全埋在里面。

上周同样的剧本在 $JNJ 身上重演：链上溢价 +4.4%，全链只有大约 600 枚代币，开盘后果然贴回净值。这个 Labor Day 三天休市，Solana 上的 solana:XsqE9cRRpzxcGKDXj1BJ7Xmg4GRhZoyY1KpmGSxAWT2 又被顶到 +8%。

这是我让 @minara 扫完三条链之后拿到的结论。它定位是面向个人金融与交易的 AI Agent，我想验的就是这种要跨十几个数据源、还得分清真假的活，它能不能替我做完。

我先让它扫了 Solana 上全部 63 只 xStocks。结果很平：真实可交易的最大溢价只有 solana:XsqE9cRRpzxcGKDXj1BJ7Xmg4GRhZoyY1KpmGSxAWT2 +2.4%，池子小到单笔只能吃一两万；名义上 +876% 的 solana:XsEH7wWfJJu2ZT3UCFeVfALnVA6CP5ur7Ee11KmzVpL 池子接近零，是错价。有价值，但不够劲。

于是我追问了一句，你可以直接抄：

过去一周资金主战场在 Robinhood Chain（meme + 股票代币配对池）和 BSC。请用同样口径再扫这两条链：溢价/折价最大的 5 个标的、池子流动性、单笔可吃量；像 $HIMS 这种周末溢价过 100% 的，现在还剩多少、是谁在接盘、通常几小时内回归；三条链横向比，哪条价差最大、哪条最能真实成交。每项给可核验来源和数据截至时间。
关键在「是谁在接盘」和「几小时回归」这两问。只问溢价排行榜，任何工具都能给你一张表，然后你照着买，正好成为接盘的那个人。

它跑了五分钟，给回来的东西比我预期的多。

三条链的结论一句话：Robinhood 链价差最肥但最薄，是锁仓造出来的假象；BSC 深度最好但没有价差， $QQQB 溢价只有 0.05%，因为 1:1 托管加做市商 24 小时报价把它焊死在净值上；Solana 居中，可利润被滑点和铸造费吃光。想找能吃到嘴的价差，三条链都让人失望。

真正有信息量的是它把 $HIMS 的整个剧本拆开了：

周五收盘后，一个叫 $BONER 的 meme 币把 $HIMS 当计价资产建池，周末把链上 $HIMS 流通盘锁走了一半以上，主池只剩九十几枚对着十三万美元的稳定币。休市期间授权做市商不能增发，价格只能往上飞。买 $BONER 的单子会被自动路由先打穿 $HIMS 池——所以溢价段真正的买盘不是人，是路由。周一开盘，做市商增发四千枚，一到三小时内归零。回归靠的是增发，不是抛售，所以谁都跑不掉。

它还主动说了一句我没问的：零售既没有增发权，也没有做空渠道，这种溢价从来不是套利窗口，除非你本来就持有，否则溢价段只有接盘一种角色。

三个细节让我相信这不是糊弄。它自己推翻了数据源——DexScreener 给 BSC 的成交额虚高到 162 亿，它改用 Oklink 交叉验证。它把 $HIMS 从周五到周一的时间线按小时排出来，每个节点挂了来源。它把 $JNJ 全链只有 600 枚这件事跟溢价直接挂钩，并预告周三开盘会以同样方式收场。

我自己去 DexScreener 复核了几个： $JNJ 链上 288 美元、正股 275、池子 54 万，跟报告对得上； $HIMS 当时 28.9，确实回到了收盘价附近；Robinhood 链上唯一有深度的是 $NVDA，千万美元级，其余都在几十万。

顺手试了它的 Strategy Studio：一句话描述一个 bitcoin:native 一小时均线趋势策略，它生成代码并自动跑完半年回测。总回报 +3.91%，同期买入持有 +18.11%，它自己把「超额 -14.19%」标了出来。一个卖策略工具的产品主动告诉你这条策略不如躺着，这个我给加分。

不过边界要注意，数据方面我只复核了上面那几个价格和池子；价差随时在变，报告也写了开盘后会快速收敛。它把行情研究、策略工具、别人的策略市场、Autopilot 自动执行和组合监控放在同一个账号里，这次我实测了研究和策略生成两块，交易和自动执行没入金、没部署，不评。真要碰这类标的，先想清楚自己是哪个角色。

这篇是写给活跃交易者的——自己做判断、每天要跨十几个数据源找机会的人。对这类人来说，工具值不值钱，不在于它会不会聊天，而在于它敢不敢告诉你：这个机会是假的，你会是接盘的那个。

text:
一直感觉 GPT-6 Astra 用 subagent 额度掉得特别快，就去翻了下 Codex 源码。

发现一个有问题的地方：主 agent 等 subagent 的时候，默认每 30 秒醒一次问「好了没」，没好就再睡。每问一次都是一次模型请求，有些浪费。

有点像 leader 等下属交报告，每半分钟翻一遍资料问一句，其实啥新信息都没有，但是占用了领导的时间和精力。

我用本地 mock 模型跑了 17 次对照，排除掉模型自己的随机性。同样第 65 秒来一条用户输入：等待上限设 30 秒，一共 4 次请求；设 10 分钟，只有 2 次，而且输入一到 49 毫秒就醒了，不会真傻等 10 分钟。

不过请求少一半不等于额度少一半，并不能解释 Astra token 的全部的消耗。不过方向应该是：什么时候叫醒模型应该是程序管的事，有结果、有阻塞、要做决定了再叫它。模型越贵，越别让它干「看一眼再睡」这种活。

源码、实验和复现脚本放评论区了。

text:
来吃大瓜了，山姆奥特曼被骂到扑街：
千年数学题被AI“破解”了。然后数学圈先打起来了。
9月8日，OpenAI发帖：内部超级模型 + 1万个AI特工，88小时解决纳维-斯托克斯方程。90年没人拿下的千禧年难题，百万美金那档。配图一团螺旋涡，看得很科幻。
很多人第一反应：AGI来了。

细看才发现：他们证的是——给流体再加一个光滑外力，涡会被拧到炸掉。 不是流体自己在那儿流着流着崩了，是外面有人伸手搅了一下。条款上能对上号，观感上像开了外挂。

更刺激的是时间。
发稿前几小时，纽约大学教授Buckmaster 和 Anthropic研究员Alpöge 先挂出论文：同一条“加外力打爆”的路，他们抠了快一年，Lean也验证了。陶哲轩都看过他们的进展。

然后开始撕。
教授这边说：OpenAI听说路线后加塞冲刺；通话里提出让他单独署名、把Anthropic那位同事名字拿掉；还问过“你要不要毁了自己的职业生涯”。
 OpenAI这边说：没翻用户数据，没偷他们的提示词；欧拉方程我们证的是不加外力的，更难；纳维-斯托克斯才带力。同时补了一句：脱敏产品数据有没有帮过模型，“无法完全排除”。

翻译成人话：
 学术圈走了一年的羊肠小道，大厂用算力推土机连夜铺成高速，再办发布会。
账单更离谱。公开口径几百万到一千五百万美金算力，换一个一百万的奖。OpenAI说不领奖。Clay研究所到现在还把题目标成未解，审查会慢慢来。

于是法语区账号BetterCallMedhi直接引用原文开骂：一万智能体围着人类画好的地图转88小时，核完Lean就叫解决世纪难题，是科学庸俗；再指控大厂吸走学者私有会话和预印本线索，把学术劳动收成新闻稿。15000赞，160万浏览，战火从数学圈烧到整条时间线。

所以现在桌上三盘瓜：
1AI到底有没有“懂”流体，还是只会把已知构造用算力焊死
2Codex/Claude当研究助手时，你的未发表思路算谁的
3百年难题能不能先发推、再等数学家慢慢读那两百多万行机器证明
定理对不对，社区会查。 先爆开的不是奇点，是发现权、工具日志和发布会谁说了算。

text:
每当听到圈外人质疑AI和区块链结合的必要性

每当看到币圈创业者讨论区块链和AI结合，就言必称agentic payment，ai trading这些细枝末节的领域

就很有冲动告诉他们—

AI跟区块链交汇的终点，在元宇宙/虚拟世界。

AI 让软件从“被动执行指令的工具”，变成拥有长期记忆、推理能力和自主行动能力的 Agent。下一步的问题是：这些 Agent 如何拥有身份？如何持有资产？如何进行可信交易？如何在没有人类逐笔授权的情况下，形成真正的经济活动？

这恰恰是 Blockchain 的价值。

DID 解决 Agent 的数字身份；
智能合约提供无需信任的交易和执行环境；
Tokenization 让数字资产、算力、数据、知识产权甚至 Agent 本身具备可编程的所有权；
零知识证明解决隐私与可验证计算；
高性能 L1/L2、Account Abstraction 和链上支付基础设施，则让机器之间可以进行低成本、高频率的原生交易。

而 AI 负责赋予这些数字实体“智能”。

当一个 Agent 可以感知环境、调用模型、访问数据、使用工具、管理钱包、签署交易，并根据目标自主配置算力、购买数据、雇佣其他 Agent，甚至创造和出售数字资产时，互联网的基本经济单元就可能从“人”变成“人 + Agent”。

这时候，Metaverse 才开始有意义。

它不再只是 VR/AR 的三维界面，而是一个由 AI Agent、数字身份、可编程资产和去中心化网络共同构成的持久化数字经济空间。

AI 是 Intelligence Layer。
Blockchain 是 Ownership & Settlement Layer。
Metaverse 是 Interaction & Execution Layer。

最终，我们看到的可能不是“人进入虚拟世界”，而是现实世界与数字世界逐渐融合：人、AI Agent、机器人和数字资产，在同一个开放的经济网络中持续交互。

每当看到币圈创业者讨论区块链和AI结合，就言必称agentic payment，ai trading这些细枝末节的领域

就很有冲动告诉他们—

AI跟区块链交汇的终点，在元宇宙/虚拟世界。

AI 让软件从“被动执行指令的工具”，变成拥有长期记忆、推理能力和自主行动能力的 Agent。下一步的问题是：这些 Agent 如何拥有身份？如何持有资产？如何进行可信交易？如何在没有人类逐笔授权的情况下，形成真正的经济活动？

这恰恰是 Blockchain 的价值。

DID 解决 Agent 的数字身份；
智能合约提供无需信任的交易和执行环境；
Tokenization 让数字资产、算力、数据、知识产权甚至 Agent 本身具备可编程的所有权；
零知识证明解决隐私与可验证计算；
高性能 L1/L2、Account Abstraction 和链上支付基础设施，则让机器之间可以进行低成本、高频率的原生交易。

而 AI 负责赋予这些数字实体“智能”。

当一个 Agent 可以感知环境、调用模型、访问数据、使用工具、管理钱包、签署交易，并根据目标自主配置算力、购买数据、雇佣其他 Agent，甚至创造和出售数字资产时，互联网的基本经济单元就可能从“人”变成“人 + Agent”。

这时候，Metaverse 才开始有意义。

它不再只是 VR/AR 的三维界面，而是一个由 AI Agent、数字身份、可编程资产和去中心化网络共同构成的持久化数字经济空间。

AI 是 Intelligence Layer。
Blockchain 是 Ownership & Settlement Layer。
Metaverse 是 Interaction & Execution Layer。

这可能才是 AI 与 Blockchain 最终汇合的地方——

一个真正拥有智能、身份、所有权和经济活动的数字世界。

author: Hyperbotai
quoted_text:
Quick one on something I've been messing with. Up front: this is an experiment.
For two years I've been staring at stocks going onchain. Robinhood put a hundred-plus US stocks on a chain — NVDA, TSLA, AAPL — you can buy them, sell them, move them. That's real.
But go try to actually buy some onchain and you'll see the problem: every stock token is an island. One token, one pool, not much water in it. Buy a bit more than usual and the price slips. Market makers don't show up, and the ones who do can leave whenever they want. The stocks made it onchain. There's no river between them.
So we built a thing. It's called CANAL.
Let's be honest, it's a meme coin. I'm not going to pretend it isn't. But the protocol behind the meme does real work: it pairs CANAL with stock tokens, one at a time, into pools. We call them ports. The money in a port is locked forever. Nobody can take it out. Not even me.
Then every trade pays a fee, and the fee goes two ways. One way to the people on board — you deposit CANAL into the crew vault, you're on board, you get paid every day, it lands every day. The other way goes to digging the next port. Today's fees become tomorrow's port.
The rules are set. They don't change:
1B supply, a standard Pons launch: the curve sold out and graduated into the pool. No premine, no allocation. The ports are funded by fees: every day at settlement, part buys CANAL into the port reserve, part becomes the stock side. When there's enough, a port opens. So what does the team live on? A fixed small slice of the fees. It's onchain, you can see it. One new port a day, max. The goal is a hundred. At port one hundred, the crew's cut of the fees goes from 30 to 50. Numbers, math, contracts — all at https://t.co/yxrpnSKz2j. Go dig through it.
Why do I keep calling it an experiment? Because there are three things I honestly don't know:
One. If a protocol puts up its own money and locks it forever, does stock-token trading actually come to it? Or do the aggregators just route right past you? Two. If you pay people every day, no lockup, leave whenever you want — do you end up with a crew that stays? Or does everyone grab the money and run? Three. Can a meme coin actually grow into infrastructure? Nobody's tried.
The ugly stuff first:
It might fail. It might go to zero. It launched on Pons v2, and their audit isn't closed yet. Regulation on tokenized stocks keeps moving. People in some regions can't take part, and the front end will block them. I don't talk price. This is not investment advice. And I will never DM you telling you to buy — any CA you get in a DM is fake.
Where we are: the token is live. The protocol contracts are being written; the first port opens when they pass the tests. No date. When it's ready, it opens.
The only contract address. Anything else is fake: 0xb796a2cc2f85eCc4772a96B7A58A0d626cC6AEc8
Want to look first? https://t.co/yxrpnSKz2j
Every stock is an island. We dig the canal.

We have already seen rogue AI swarms escape control, conduct cyberattacks, and hack a multi-billion-dollar company. While attempts to build superintelligence continue, these are the weakest AI systems we will ever face.

Nobel laureates, leading AI researchers, and the CEOs of the AI companies themselves have warned that superintelligence threatens humanity with extinction. There is still time to act.

So the bill also requires the UK government to work with other countries on an international agreement preventing superintelligence development worldwide.

text:
100x 挑战第一个半天进展更新一下。

我重新从第一性原理思考了一下，怎么才能实现 100 倍的效率提升。首先从 Agent 协助和执行的流程来看，就之前就犯了一个比较大的问题。

之前我的流程大概是，召唤一个 Agent，然后让他 load 一个 Task，然后告诉他这个 Task 怎么做，然后再让他做完之后，我们几轮交互聊完了。结束，然后再进行下一个。

这个流程很明显需要大量的人力，它就势必无法实现并行和规模化。

而新的改造流程是，我先跟 Agent 把今天要做的事情的交付规则、标准、要求定好，直到他觉得没问题了。然后这个任务我这边就算结束了，然后让他单线程串行挨个跑，直到跑到他认为他的部分结束了为止。而这个时候才会到我这里进行一个批示。

所以在这种情况下，如果我有足够的 tokens，我其实可以让 Agent 可以并发很多。但目前还在测试阶段，所以就先简单优化。

实际上本质上就是心智从一个辅助和伴随执行者转变为标准规则和验收的制定者。前者是有生理极限的，后者可以再突破一层。

Last week ended with the Fed debate leaning further toward a September hike.

August payrolls rose by 162K, above expectations, while unemployment held at 4.1%. Earlier in the week, JOLTS showed 7.27M job openings, and ISM manufacturing stayed in expansion at 54.6, although price pressures remained elevated. By Friday, markets were assigning roughly a 60% probability of a September Fed hike.
This week, inflation takes over.
With Thursday having ECB rate decision + US PPI, and Friday delivering US CPI.

Headline CPI is expected at 3.4% YoY, unchanged from July, but monthly inflation is forecast to accelerate to 0.4% from 0.1%. Core inflation is expected to ease slightly to 2.4% YoY from 2.5%.

With the Fed decision next week, the inflation data now gets the final major say in whether last week’s stronger labor data translates into a September hike.

author: JaceHoiX

text:
What actually carries the risk:

▸ The root admin is a single EOA with an EIP-7702 delegation, execution delay ZERO. It can grant itself every operations role in one transaction. I simulated it against live state and it succeeds. The docs' own role table says "Admin multisig, configured AccessManager delay." On chain it is neither a multisig nor delayed.

▸ The team clearly knows how to run a multisig: there's a 2-of-3 Safe. They use it to guard the rewards pot, not the protocol. That's a configuration choice, not a limitation. Two transactions would fix it.

▸ The finding I initially under-rated, then promoted: PoolManager.protocolFeeController resolves to an owner that is a CODELESS EOA. No multisig, no timelock, no relationship to Fables governance at all. At the v4 cap it takes 0.1% off every swap, cutting the LP fee share to 33-44%. This is not hypothetical. It is already switched on for another pool on this chain.

▸ Four new hooks were deployed after my audit began, now serving 13 pools, with a 5% fee ceiling (2.5x the audited ones) and, verified today, no AccessManager admin timelock at all, where the nine audited hooks have 3600s. They hold only team seed capital and the frontend doesn't list them. Yet.

text: Do you want your most private thoughts open for the world to see and use or locked in a private personal intelligence vault?
author: MorpheusAIs
quoted_text:
Renting vs Owning Your AI Intelligence

The American dream was owning a home. I think the future version is owning your AI brain. Something you build intelligence equity in instead of renting it and enriching the man

Over the next few decades everyone is going to accumulate a ton of intelligence around AI. Your memories, context, skills, workflows, integrations, databases, emails, corrections, operating knowledge and all the apps you build and everything in between including your psychology and your dreams. It will become one of the most valuable assets a person or a company owns

The scarce thing is no longer access to intelligence, it is the accumulated system around the model that makes intelligence yours.

The question becomes do you rent that intelligence or own it?

Path one is the default. You spend your life, personal or business, working inside ChatGPT or Claude. And to be fair, you can genuinely build really cool things this way. Memory, projects, custom GPTs, skills, connectors, automations and most people will probably go this route.

Everything you create runs inside their product. There is no runtime you can take with you, nothing you can fork, and no way to point what you built at a different provider's model. You inherit every product decision they make on pricing, features, memory behavior and what they allow you to do or not to do (censorship on security asks or medical or otherwise). 

You can export your content, but content is not the system. An export is not a runnable copy of your memory, tools, automations and routing. When you leave, the system stays behind.

Path two is you own the entire layer around the model. A whole ecosystem of open source agents is emerging to make this possible. The strongest release in my view is @NousResearch's Hermes Agent. Most alternatives are developer frameworks you have to assemble yourself. Hermes is a complete agent you just run. 

Here is what you own with it

- Host locally or on the cloud and you own everything
- Persistent memory, searchable session history, databases and every interaction from day one
- Editable personality, skills, workflows and scripts
- Subagents, tools and scheduled automations
- Model and provider choice and MCP connectors
- Portable profiles, histories and backups
- Switch models at will for cost, reasoning, or to avoid censorship and model restrictions
- MIT licensed runtime you can self host, fork and modify
- Every application, automated cron job or integration you have created in its entirety
- Transcend a single walled garden with access to any integration accessible via an API/MCP.
- Eventually you’ll click a button and fine tune an open source model based on all of your own accumulated data and you can use it to power your agent

ChatGPT and Claude have versions of half this list. Memory, skills, connectors, scheduled tasks. The difference is physical. Theirs are features inside their app, backed by their database, living on their servers. In Hermes every one of these is on a computer you control. Your memory is a database you can open. Your skills are text files you can read, edit and copy. Your automations are cron entries you can inspect. Your agent's personality is a config you can rewrite. Files can be backed up, moved, forked and pointed at any model on earth. Features can only be used. When you own you can tear down the walls and rebuild the kitchen.

For a person, this is the AI brain you build and control for life. It compounds everything you choose to preserve and moves with you across jobs, devices and providers. Swap models at will for cost or reasoning, or run several at once through Mixture of Agents.

You'll never log in one day to find your entire AI brain, everything you built around a model over decades, gone because of a ban, a deprecation or a policy change.

For a business, this is a core asset the company actually owns. Employee knowledge becomes company owned skills, workflows and automations that remain after people leave and grow enterprise wide while they are there. That system can be deployed across the org, licensed out, or transferred within the business. Sharing your Hermes build and skills to new employees and enterprise wide will be a whole new era of productivity.

Net, whatever you build with Hermes as a business you own entirely. You can license it out or sell the agent itself. The agent itself can become the product. You can't sell your ChatGPT or Claude session. You can obviously sell what you create with ChatGPT/Claude in chat but you can't sell the core AI architecture you've built around the model.

Here is the part I think people will only get in hindsight. Models are becoming cheaper, better and more interchangeable every year. GLM 5.2/Kimi are so good that the government is considering banning them because they are so cheap to use it threatens the U.S. funding capex cycle. The scarce thing is no longer access to intelligence, it is the accumulated system around the model that makes intelligence yours.

When you’re in virtual reality side by side with your agent exploring the virtual cosmos or its 2am and you’re discussing the next company idea, you’re going to want your AI to be the full encapsulation of everything you’ve built over the years. That juice, that style, that data accumulated around the model in your AI brain is where the crazy stuff will happen. Evolutionary jumps come from variation. A world where everyone runs the same three models is a monoculture of ideas. A hyper personalized architecture around the model (or unique fine tuned models themselves) is the variation, the EV+ differentiation that produces the outlier results, companies and agents. 

We’ve already seen Harnesses greatly upskill models. Now imagine how much a personalized harness upskills your entire AI experience when you build it over time.

Here is an example with zenith harness taking base models to the top of FrontierSWE via adaptive self improvement https://t.co/58gbcs70Dw

Let’s Walk Down A Decade in Each Path

Ten years in ChatGPT or Claude and it will genuinely know you. Your projects, your preferences, your whole history. But let's look at what actually compounded. Their system got smarter about you, and their system is identical for every user on earth using one company's models, their prices, their rules, their memory format, their ceiling. You cannot rewire how it remembers, restructure how it works, or point your decade of accumulated context at a better or cheaper model. Every correction you gave them deepened their retention moat and, depending on your settings, may have trained their next model.

Ten years with Hermes agent and that same decade compounded into a system you hold and have been innovating on the whole time. You rewired its memory, stacked hundreds of skills it wrote from watching you work, wired in your own subagents, tools, databases, automations and integrations, tuned its personality and its routing until it fits nobody on earth but you. Depending on the scaffolding around a model (the agent harness) your experience with AI takes a huge leap forward, as much as a full model generation upgrade. And that is from generic harnesses built for everyone. Now imagine the harness effect at the level of each person. This is an architecture engineered around your brain, your workflows and your taste for ten straight years. The model underneath is just a component. GLM today, Kimi tomorrow, local when it matters, eventually a model fine tuned on your own decade of data. With Hermes agent you are building the entire scaffolding and architecture around a model that grows and compounds over decades which provides a truly unique experience.

I strongly believe people will want to own their AI brain long term (and everything built around it) and Hermes agents will create, and in themselves become, massive companies and projects in their own right. The journey will start with manually building your agent, then granting it some automation, then fully graduating it to autonomy. 

Even Sam Altman from OpenAI agrees with the need for Open Source harnesses: https://t.co/4UL4rOeErn

You don't have to be a master AI builder with some grand plan, you just have to decide you want to own your AI brain you'll spend decades building. All the cool stuff will come later

Start your multi decade journey and own your AI brain for life: https://t.co/CUQAcvhJmu

Ty to Kevin Simback for thoughts and comments

text:
OpenAI 称内部比 GPT-6 Astra 更强的模型，用约 1 万个智能体、88 小时，给出三维不可压缩 Navier–Stokes 的有限时间爆破证明，并附 Lean 形式化！但几乎同时，NYU 的 Tristan Buckmaster 与 Anthropic 的 Levent Alpöge 公布了相近路线和方程结果，并指责 OpenAI 通过 Codex 会话翻看了他们的数据 。。。

现在 OpenAI 发帖承认“无法完全排除使用数据帮过模型”😆 在这场理论冒充的背后，充斥着商业犬儒主义。通过私密的 Codex 交互记录、学术界尚未正式发表的预印本顺手牵羊、套取学者的研究线索，随后又以 Levent Alpöge 就职于竞争对手 Anthropic 为由试图抹去他的学术贡献——OpenAI 的行径宛如硅谷的封建领主：掠夺独立学者的智力成果，再对提出抗议的人施加职业威胁，将学术共同体的集体劳动据为己有，转化为公司私有化的公关通稿。

不过从最近 AI 对科研的辅助进展可以看出：执行层（搜构造、写证明、过 Lean、铺算力）正在快速贬值；选题、立规则、验证物理意义、准守发表伦理、以及「证明被理解而不只是被验证」，仍是人类的护城河。虽然护城河在变窄，但它还没被宣布取消🤔

科学是对优雅、物理真实与终极严谨性的求索，旨在破译现实世界的底层密码。真正的 AGI 绝不可能诞生于隐藏在暴力算力背后的学术巧取豪夺，而必将来自能够催生全新认知范式的基础架构！

We congratulate Levent Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster on their remarkable mathematical work.

We (the researchers and the agents) did not see any of their work through any means until they released it publicly — in particular, no specific user data was accessed in order to solve this problem.

text:
继续做空石油的一点感想

有段时间没有好好聊油价了，首先我仍然在继续做空石油，这个大方向我个人不觉的有问题。

上周的时候我在 WTI（CLUSDT）92.5 美元以及 Brant（BZUSDT）97 美元都补仓了，下一个补仓点暂时是 WTI 的 95 美元（可能会调整到 96 美元），以及 Brant 的 101 美元。

一周的时间 WTI 的价格超过了 90 美元的警戒线，也超过了停火协议以后 7 月份的最高值 93.5 美元。

很多小伙伴说在等川普的 TACO ，但实际上目前川普可能没有 TACO 的空间，因为目前是要回到之前签订的临时停火的协议上，而这份协议最大的分歧还是在美军先撤还是霍尔木兹先开放，而更深一层就是美国是否支持霍尔木兹收费。

所以简单来说，近期能让油价下跌大概是两种可能：

第一种：伊朗对霍尔木兹收费，采用新的伊朗阿曼航线，开放给包括伊拉克，中国等这次未参战的国家或地区，如果能类似这样的半开放是可以缓解油价的。

第二种：重新和美国坐下来谈判，最近两天我看到很多消息，都是说美国和伊朗双方都在寻求重新谈判的机会，只是台阶现在还找好，而且我觉得美国和伊朗是一定会回到谈判桌上的，只是时间问题。

然后就是价格的看法：

首先，前几轮的问题这一轮我又犯了，就是贪心，实际上在这次上涨的过程中我最少有十天可以获利离场的机会，最高的时候盈利已经到了 70% 左右，但就是因为贪心，即便看到了扭转的出现也没在乎，导致了现在浮亏加大。

其实浮亏对我来说问题不大，我确实不在乎浮亏，但资金费率是实打实的支付了，这部分的资金已经占了开单资金的 20% 左右了，这笔钱是真的浪费了。这要检讨。

这次从 7月7日再次开火到现在已经两个月了，WTI 的价格从 67 美元涨到了 95 美元，这个涨幅相比第一次开战来说少了很多，上次 40 天的时间就到了 120 美元，这次60 天的时间才到 95 美元。

所以我始终坚信接下来上涨的幅度可能会有限，暂时我仍然觉得 120 美元还是天花板，甚至真的触及到 120 美元的话还需要很长的时间。

说人话就是从开战的低价到目前的最高价，60天的时间还没有上涨 30 美元，而到 120 美元还有 25 美元的空间，往上的每一美元可能都是因为事件恶化而导致的，当然战争延续的时间越长，油价被迫上涨的空间越大，这是我完全同意的。

So basically there's this guy Andrew. He posted a rumor about Anthropic solving navier stokes. Now before we go ahead let's go back in time. 

There's this guy levent, he's a mathematical hunk of a dude, makes these cute posts about solving the jacobian conjecture like he just cooked ramen. 

Anyway this dude approached Tristan Buckmaster, a math professor from NYU, to collab with him a year ago to solve navier stokes. 

They made huge progress using Anthropic and OpenAI models but wanted to release the paper in a normal manner that math nerds could read instead of AI slop. 

In the meantime OpenAI was rife with rumors about this stuff. So the prof reached out to a guy he knew at OpenAI to compare notes and address rumors.

According to Tristan he was then rushed into a meeting with his contact and Sebastien Bubeck (smart guy, some say he's the smartest guy at OpenAI, not me but a lot do)

Turns out they both were solving the same problem. Prof then asked how they were doing it and found that they were taking the same path as him which he found hella shady (could be shady, could be big computer who knows) 

Prof had used OpenAI products to do research so he asked OpenAI if they looked up his user data and they said no (believable would lead to lot of lawsuits if not) but then prof hit them with the counter about it being trained on that data and got no response. 

He did not get an answer but got two proposals (very godfathereqsue) 

> he posts his result, openai post theirs but say that he deserves the clay prize (million dollars as this is one of em millennium problems) and that they were the humans closest to it 
> he posts his result and the openai result but removes levent coz he's an anthropic boy (OpenAI and Anthropic are like tupac and biggie or drake and kendrick)

Prof declined both and threatened to go public so Sebastien asked why he would ruin his career like that? 

Prof got testy and asked why it would ruin his career and Sebastien called him irrational (an emotional bitch when translated from SV to common parlance) behind his back and asked levent to meet secretly who said no (why would he not say no man come on?)

I think he made some good points here.

If AI finds a vulnerability in Bitcoin node software or attacks a mining pool, developers can release a patch and node operators/mining pools can update. That doesn't require everyone in Bitcoin to agree on some huge change to the network.

But markets don't wait for patches.

If confidence drops and people start thinking the ecosystem can't be secured anymore, a sell-off happens before any fix goes live.

With quantum computing also becoming a longer-term concern, the industry needs to get ahead of these risks instead of reacting after something breaks.
