text:
Visa is pushing further into the plumbing of digital money just as payments, U.S. markets, and Washington’s rulebook are shifting together. The company told CNBC it will share more data with blockchain lenders, pairing VisaNet settlement records with onchain credit infrastructure so lenders can see how digital-asset fintechs and stablecoin-linked card issuers are actually performing. 

The goal is practical: fast-growing card programs need working capital, lenders need a clearer view of receivables, and Visa wants those loans to close faster as demand for cards funded or settled in dollar tokens accelerates.

That demand is no longer experimental. Visa now runs more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs, with related payment volume up nearly 200 percent year over year. New issuers, including stablecoin neobanks and fintechs, are joining weekly. The company’s stablecoin settlement volume has climbed above a $20 billion annualized run rate, more than fifteen times the level of a year ago. Cuy Sheffield, Visa’s head of crypto, called the category “hypergrowth mode.”

The financing layer is the new piece. Visa has been piloting the model with Credit Coop, which uses smart contracts to fund and repay settlement facilities. With customer authorization, settlement data can be combined with onchain records so lenders can judge credit quality in closer to real time. The firms cite more than $2.5 billion in financed settlement volume since 2023 and no defaults. 

Visa’s analytics put stablecoin-denominated loans through onchain protocols at nearly $700 billion since 2020, most of it still inside crypto markets. The bet is that card receivables can pull that credit into everyday commerce.

Policy explains the timing. Last year’s GENIUS Act created the first federal framework for U.S. payment stablecoins, requiring one-to-one reserves in cash, short-term Treasuries, and other tightly defined assets, and setting licensing paths for banks and nonbanks. 

Sheffield called it a huge turning point. Implementing rules were due by mid-2026 and were not finished; proposals on licensing, reserves, capital, AML, and sanctions are out, but the statute still points toward a January 2027 effective date unless final rules arrive sooner. Even so, banks and large payment companies have been coming to Visa to put stablecoins inside existing products or build new ones. Mastercard has taken a more vertical path, including a large infrastructure acquisition. Visa has leaned on optionality: more chains, more tokens, more partners, and now more credit data on top of the card rails.

That contest matters for U.S. equities because payments stocks are no longer only a bet on consumer spending and interchange. They are a bet on who owns settlement when dollars move onchain. Visa shares are up about 7 percent this year, a modest gain against an S&P 500 that has advanced more than 12 percent while the Fed held rates in the 3.50–3.75 percent range for much of 2026. The tape is more fragile as September opens. 

The same rate backdrop cuts through Visa’s credit pitch. Higher policy rates raise the cost of working capital even when smart contracts make the plumbing cleaner. They also increase the appeal of the Treasury reserves GENIUS-style stablecoins must hold, which is why official research now treats large-scale stablecoin growth as a potential source of T-bill demand and, in extreme cases, a pressure point for bank deposits. Visa’s data product does not settle those debates. It tries to make a card program’s cash flow legible enough that lenders will fund growth without waiting for a traditional credit file.

The investment question is less whether crypto wins than how fees and regulation split. If stablecoin cards scale, Visa and Mastercard can add volume even as some customers try to compress costs onchain. If banks issue their own tokens, the networks still want to be the switch. If rulemaking stays messy into 2027, card growth could outrun the compliance perimeter. 

Sheffield’s argument is that traditional finance is already absorbing the technology, and that the variable is speed. Markets will price that speed against CPI, the September Fed decision, and whether payments names still look like compounders or merely crowded financials in a rising-rate tape.

text:
Anthropic 现在最怕的，可能是 AI 模型开始进入「谁便宜谁有量」的阶段。

Benchmark 输一场还能追，定价权一旦松动，2 万亿美元 IPO 的估值逻辑就得重写。

The Information 今天专门写了一篇，标题就叫《Why Price Cuts May Rattle Anthropic's IPO Pitch》。

起因是 OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar 最近在高盛的 Communacopia 大会上透露，GPT 5.6 Luna 降价之后，用量直接涨了 10 倍，在 OpenRouter 上拿到了最高市场份额，而且新增用量足以抵消降价。

这个数据对 Anthropic 很刺眼。

Anthropic 现在最漂亮的一张牌，就是收入增长。到 7 月底，它的年化收入已经达到约 650 亿美元，明显领先 OpenAI。市场目前讨论的 IPO 估值甚至到了 2 万亿美元。

可如果 OpenAI 能靠降价抢走大量 token，Anthropic 就必须回答一个很现实的问题：

Claude 到底值多少溢价？

Anthropic 其实已经开始跟。

刚发布的 Fable 5.1，输入输出 token 的标价没有直接砍 25%，但 cache read 价格降了 75%。Anthropic 自己估算，典型 workload 的综合成本比上一代低约 25%，高度 Agent 化的任务最多能便宜约 45%。

所以现在有一个非常微妙的局面。

降价当然可以把 usage 做大，甚至像 OpenAI 那样，让收入最后反而继续涨。

但 Anthropic 马上要面对的是公开市场。

华尔街看的就不会只有 ARR 了，还会问：

650 亿美元的年化收入，到底烧了多少算力换回来？

每多跑 1 万亿 token，真正留下来的毛利是多少？

价格继续往下掉之后，这家公司还值不值得几十倍的 revenue multiple？

这个问题尤其要和 Anthropic 最近疯狂锁算力一起看。

The Information 估算，过去 11 个月 Anthropic 签下的各类算力协议，潜在总金额最高可能达到 5170 亿美元，涉及至少 14.8GW 的容量。当然，这不代表 Anthropic 已经花掉这些钱，也不代表最后会全部调用，但它已经说明这是一门多重的资本生意。

IPO 前，Anthropic 还在敲定一笔 150 亿美元循环信贷额度；上市之后，它和 OpenAI 的银行团队甚至已经开始推动投资级信用评级，希望以后能更便宜地进入债券市场融资。

毛利也一直是这家公司最敏感的数字之一。

Anthropic 此前就吃过一次推理成本的亏：2025 年毛利率预期曾从 50% 下调到 40%，原因之一，就是实际 inference 成本比预期高了 23%。

所以我觉得 Anthropic 这次 IPO 有一个非常关键的观察点：

AI 模型公司的 token 增长，不能直接当成 SaaS 的席位增长来看。

用户每多用一次 Claude，背后就真有 GPU 在烧钱。

只要行业继续价格战，模型能力之间的差距继续缩小，Anthropic 最珍贵的东西可能很快就从「收入增速」变成「定价权」。

650 亿美元 ARR 很吓人。

但华尔街最后要给 2 万亿美元估值，Anthropic 得证明一件更难的事：

Claude 不光有人抢着用，还得能越来越便宜地生产，同时让客户愿意继续付更贵的钱。

author: Murphychen888
quoted_text:
我觉得这才是ETF数据的正确打开姿势
—— 净流入成交比

即ETF Flow-to-Volume Ratio（FVR），它跟踪的是ETF 30日净流量和成交量相对变化关系。以币本位计，不受价格变化的影响。

红线在零轴以上，表示过去30天ETF买盘压过卖盘，AP在净申购，资金在流入。数值高意味着成交量中大部分是单向的，市场有共识。

反之，则说明成交量里有大部分是在互相对冲，这是分歧。

通过观察我们不难发现，FVR在大多数时间和BTC价格呈现高度联动关系，说明在底层逻辑上双方是相互影响，相互作用的。

但有的时候，FVR也会是情绪的前置信号，即走在了价格行为的前面。

比如，图中红色标注区，都是价格上升，但FVR下降；此时就代表美国传统资金的分歧正在产生。

亦或者像图中绿色标注区，FVR的下降速度明显比价格更快。代表此时市场的恐慌情绪正在扩散。

所以，现在我们看到的是前者，有一点点苗头出现。市场在消化抛压的同时，需要重新建立价格共识。

写在最后：

ETF是免费公开的数据，但不影响它的重要性。不过，我不建议把某一天的波动，或单纯的净流入/流出，作为结论导向；应该观察一段时期的趋势表现，相对会更合理。

author: billqian_hk
quoted_text:
每当听到圈外人质疑AI和区块链结合的必要性

每当看到币圈创业者讨论区块链和AI结合，就言必称agentic payment，ai trading这些细枝末节的领域

就很有冲动告诉他们—

AI跟区块链交汇的终点，在元宇宙/虚拟世界。

AI 让软件从“被动执行指令的工具”，变成拥有长期记忆、推理能力和自主行动能力的 Agent。下一步的问题是：这些 Agent 如何拥有身份？如何持有资产？如何进行可信交易？如何在没有人类逐笔授权的情况下，形成真正的经济活动？

这恰恰是 Blockchain 的价值。

DID 解决 Agent 的数字身份；
智能合约提供无需信任的交易和执行环境；
Tokenization 让数字资产、算力、数据、知识产权甚至 Agent 本身具备可编程的所有权；
零知识证明解决隐私与可验证计算；
高性能 L1/L2、Account Abstraction 和链上支付基础设施，则让机器之间可以进行低成本、高频率的原生交易。

而 AI 负责赋予这些数字实体“智能”。

当一个 Agent 可以感知环境、调用模型、访问数据、使用工具、管理钱包、签署交易，并根据目标自主配置算力、购买数据、雇佣其他 Agent，甚至创造和出售数字资产时，互联网的基本经济单元就可能从“人”变成“人 + Agent”。

这时候，Metaverse 才开始有意义。

它不再只是 VR/AR 的三维界面，而是一个由 AI Agent、数字身份、可编程资产和去中心化网络共同构成的持久化数字经济空间。

AI 是 Intelligence Layer。
Blockchain 是 Ownership & Settlement Layer。
Metaverse 是 Interaction & Execution Layer。

最终，我们看到的可能不是“人进入虚拟世界”，而是现实世界与数字世界逐渐融合：人、AI Agent、机器人和数字资产，在同一个开放的经济网络中持续交互。

这可能才是 AI 与 Blockchain 最终汇合的地方——

一个真正拥有智能、身份、所有权和经济活动的数字世界。

创业最重要的是选对方向。

text:
The definition of a successful blockchain has changed.

Early on, community and narrative could take you surprisingly far.

You needed superfans. True believers. People willing to become an unpaid marketing arm for the network and evangelize it everywhere.

That still matters. A lot.

But crypto has matured enough that belief alone isn't sufficient anymore.

Now you need killer products.

You need growing revenue. Growing users. Retention. Stablecoins. Developers. Liquidity. Institutional adoption. Consumer adoption. Market share across multiple verticals.

You need mindshare.

And, as strange as it sounds, you probably need haters too.

Because indifference is much more dangerous than criticism. If people are constantly arguing about you, comparing themselves to you, declaring that you've lost, or celebrating every new competitor as the thing that finally kills you, you're still occupying valuable real estate in their heads.

The real danger is when nobody cares enough to talk about you at all.

This is where I think a lot of the conversation around Solana gets distorted.

Solana's ambition isn't to win whatever the current crypto meta happens to be.

It's to become a global financial layer.

That means payments. Stablecoins. Trading. Capital markets. Consumer apps. DePIN. Institutional finance. Tokenized assets. Internet capital markets. And yes, sometimes completely unexpected things like memecoins that explode into their own enormous markets.

New competitors will emerge inside every one of those categories.

Hyperliquid can build an incredible trading ecosystem.

Robinhood can launch a chain with enormous built-in distribution.

Someone else will inevitably dominate a category that barely exists today.

That's not a failure of Solana. That's what a growing industry looks like.

The mistake is taking one narrow slice of the market, finding the newest winner inside it, and extrapolating that into "Solana is dead."

We've done this roughly 100 times now.

Meanwhile the more important question is much less exciting:

How is the network performing across the entire board?

Users.
Revenue.
Stablecoins.
DEXs.
Payments.
Apps.
Developers.
Institutions.
Consumer.
Capital markets.
Mindshare.

You don't have to win every category every day.
You need to be near the front of enough important categories that the aggregate keeps compounding.

That's what I think people misunderstand about where blockchains are in their lifecycle.

The game used to be largely about creating believers.
Now it's about building an economy.

And economies aren't judged by whether somebody else opened a successful business.

They're judged by whether the economy itself keeps growing.

Solana

❓ Is there only one way to tokenise an asset? It’s a question we get asked a lot.

The answer? Nope.

Today, the two most common approaches are native and synthetic tokenisation, each with a different structure and relationship to the underlying asset.

🔵 Native tokenisation: the token is issued directly on-chain and represents the legal share or ownership interest, making the blockchain part of the asset’s ownership infrastructure.

⚪ Synthetic tokenisation: the underlying asset remains off-chain with a custodian or intermediary, while a separate token provides economic exposure without direct legal ownership of the asset.

In simple terms:
🔵 Native = token is the asset.
⚪ Synthetic = token represents exposure to the asset.

But these aren’t the only possibilities. As the industry evolves, new tokenisation models are continuing to emerge.

Curious about how they work? Follow us for a deeper dive into the different models.

text:
My two cents about the recent AI solutions to Navier-Stokes:

The Navier-Stokes equation is famously the "ultimate equation" for fluid dynamics, so it is tempting to assume the recent AI result has significant practical implications, but I don't think it does.

The Millennium Problem asks: does the NS equation have any "emergent singularities"? That is, can a system start with a state without any singularities and, following the NS dynamics, develop one over a finite time?

When asked, this question was highly relevant to many people. When you consider the turbulence of fuel inside a ballistic rocket, or in huge dams, you really want to know that there isn't a scenario where "infinitely" much energy is funneled into one spot.

However, over time, people have mathematically proved that if singularities exist, they lie outside the regimes that are relevant to any practical applications. And the interest in the Millennium problem naturally decreased.

It is still a fascinating problem, but everyone would agree that the motivations for branding it "one of the seven most important problems" have considerably eroded.

The reason is that the NS describe ideal fluids: fluids that are continuous at all resolutions and completely incompressible. Fluids are sufficiently ideal in most regimes. But in the regimes where singularities can actually happen -- hugely massive turbulence with fluids flowing close to the speed of light -- actual fluids are not ideal. The particle nature of fluids manifests under much weaker forces. In the singularity-begetting scenario, any realistic fluid would compress under the massive forces or break into elementary particles due to the massive kinetic energy.

And regarding the fact that it was found "using AI", it's also important to remember that it's not like someone woke up in the morning and, while brushing their teeth, asked GPT: "bro, could ideal fluids develop singularities?" and got their answer. Two highly accomplished researchers have painstakingly developed methods to train a specific model for that specific problem. The way I see it, they used AI models as a glorified scientific calculator. I'm obviously very impressed with the feat and glad for the result. But I don't see what makes it less incremental than the adoption of proof assistants like Coq and Lean, or even the classical computer-aided proof by Appel and Haken of the four-color theorem.

author: ercwl
quoted_text:
Today a crazy quantum story just got wilder.

On March 31, the Google Quantum AI team published a landmark result on Shor's algorithm for elliptic curve cryptography. Technically, the paper was a bombshell: a dramatic 10x improvement over the state-of-the-art. As a stunt and wakeup call to the blockchain space, those optimisations were illustrated on secp256k1, the elliptic curve underlying Bitcoin and Ethereum signatures.

But perhaps the most striking part of the paper was sociological, not technical. Instead of following standard academic process, the optimisations were kept secret, hidden behind a zero-knowledge (ZK) proof. Google's accompanying blog post mentions they "engaged with the U.S. government". The ZK proof demonstrates the existence of algorithmic improvements without leaking details. Academic censorship with ZK, a historic first!

As a co-author of the Google paper I witnessed some of the context surrounding this censorship. To be honest, multiple aspects of that context don't sit well with me. As much as I believe the general public ought to know more, I am limited in my ability to whistleblow. Though let me be clear about one thing: the Google team's professionalism has been absolutely exemplary, and they deserve nothing but praise.

Censorship has a way of backfiring. The Streisand effect, where an attempt to bury something only draws more attention to it, is exactly what's unfolding today. First, Google's key optimisation has been rediscovered by the French. And in a thrilling turn of events, a collaborative Shor-at-home challenge just launched. The initiative, available at ecdsa[.]fail, breached a new Shor world record in a matter of hours.

Let's start with the rediscovery. Just two months after Google's paper, French quantum expert André Schrottenloher cracks the main secret optimisation. His paper, titled "Optimized Point Addition Circuits for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithms", landed on the arXiv today. Big congrats to André, who beat several other nerdsnipped experts to it. In a blog post also published today, Craig Gidney, the world expert on Shor optimisations, revealed that he'd been sitting on this very optimisation for a whole year under censorship pressure.

Interestingly, André missed a handful of minor optimisations, both from Google's original publication and from improvements found since. It's plausible there's still plenty of juice left to squeeze out of Shor, and this is exactly what the ecdsa[.]fail challenge is about. The verifier program developed for the ZK proof does double duty, automatically filtering for valid submissions. Dozens of compounding small and micro improvements are rolling in. As of the time of writing there's an 8.4% improvement to Google's circuit, as measured by the product of logical qubit count and Toffoli gate count. Nice!

The nerdsnipping ran deeper than anyone expected. Over the last few weeks it became clear it extended well beyond André and other quantum experts. Behind the scenes, a small army of amateurs quietly got to work. Inspired by Karpathy-style autoresearch, they turned AI on Shor. Ironically, the verifier program for the ZK proof makes an ideal reward function for AIs. The barrier to entry for this modern style of research is refreshingly low, with several non-experts, even a teenager, finding nice optimisations. Get in touch if you'd like to join a Telegram group with fellow autoresearchers :)

Part 2: neutral atoms and qday

The story doesn't end with Google. On the same day Google went public, a stealthy startup called Oratomic published its own Shor paper in a coordinated release. It made a splash, ultimately becoming the most upvoted paper on scirate[.]com, a website ranking arXiv papers.

Oratomic's claim was wild. By building on Google's logical optimisations and applying custom physical optimisations for neutral atoms, they claimed just 10K physical qubits were sufficient to run Shor's algorithm on secp256k1. That number is mind-bogglingly low.

Knowing essentially nothing about neutral atoms when Oratomic's paper landed, I was intrigued and decided to learn more about the tech. I fell straight down the rabbit hole and spent a couple hundred hours on the topic. I got a little obsessed and watched every YouTube video I could find and spoke to a bunch of experts.

My conclusion? The tech is real, very real. Even Google recently decided to start a neutral atom lab, a notable pivot from their sole focus on superconducting qubits. If you care about qday, i.e. the day a quantum computer will break the first piece of cryptography in production, neutral atoms demand your attention. I shared some of my learnings on Shor and neutral atoms in a 30min talk at the ZKProof cryptography conference. You can find it on YouTube by searching "zkproof neutral atom".

Here's an interesting observation about this duo of breakthrough papers: neither Google nor Oratomic say a word about what their results mean for qday. No timelines. Zero. Nada. That is especially baffling given that the whole point of whitehat quantum cryptanalysis is to inform qday estimations and help the general public make good decisions.

So let me attempt to partially fill the silence, similarly to what Scott Aaronson did in his April 29 post. Given everything I know, including scary non-public information, I now put the odds of qday by 2032 at 50%. 10% by 2030.

Anecdotally, the US government has its own date: 2035. Originating at the NSA and later adopted by NIST, it's when branches of the US government will be disallowed from using quantum-vulnerable cryptography. In plain language: with hindsight, that date is a joke and should be discounted entirely. I don't see how NIST avoids being forced to pull it forward by years.

Part 3: post-quantum cryptography

There are good reasons to sound the alarm today, but please do not panic. Rushing carelessly towards immature post-quantum cryptography is a recipe for disaster. IMO a good target date for migration is 2029, roughly 3.5 years out. 2029 happens to be the date selected by Google, Cloudflare, and the Ethereum Foundation.

These days most of my time goes to safely migrating Ethereum towards post-quantum cryptography as part of the broader lean Ethereum effort. There's a lot to do. We need to rip out and replace BLS signatures at the consensus layer, KZG commitments at the data layer, and ECDSA signatures at the execution layer.

The plan to get there is compelling, and is based on hash-based cryptography. Within the Ethereum Foundation we've developed a Swiss army knife called leanVM (github[.]com/leanEthereum/leanVM) powered by the magic of hash-based SNARKs. Thanks to truly exceptional work by Emile, Thomas, and others, its performance is derisked. Regarding security, leanVM is a jewel, a minimal zkVM crafted for end-to-end formal verification and maximum security.

Want to help? There are two $1M initiatives. First, the Proximity Prize (proximityprize[.]org). Solve a long-standing mathematical conjecture in coding theory, improve hash-based SNARKs, and go home a millionaire. Second, the Poseidon Initiative (poseidon-initiative[.]info), offers $1M for breaking Poseidon, the SNARK-friendly hash function.

text:
I would like to clarify a few things:

1) The screenshot is my reaching out to Levent to coordinate our releases. I hope it’s clear from the message that we came in with the best possible intentions.

2) I never ever asked for Levent to be removed from authorship of his own work (as indicated by my text). I was surprised to learn during the call with Tristan that they had only solved Euler and not Navier-Stokes; after learning this we brainstormed possible paths forward. One option we discussed was that Tristan could be the lead author on a rewrite of OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof. It is in that context that I said “it would be simpler if Levent was not an Anthropic employee” because I felt it would be inappropriate for an Anthropic employee to author OpenAI’s work. Importantly it was admitted that internal Anthropic models had been used in their proof of Euler blowup; I therefore felt I could not consider Levent to be an independent academic. Another option I wanted to propose (but got cut short) is to offer access to our internal model so that they could try to finish their proof and bridge the gap between Euler and NS. Again I did not know how to navigate giving access to internal OpenAI IP to an Anthropic employee.

3) To reiterate it plainly: as my text clearly indicates, and as I said during our call, OpenAI's intention was to do everything possible to celebrate their mathematical achievements and the heroic efforts that they made on Euler. In the call I was immediately met with a litany of slander, including direct threats that if we were to announce Navier-Stokes he would immediately go to the press with a barrage of unfounded accusations. I refuted all these accusations but he replied “there is nothing you can do, I simply do not trust you”. I was confused why one would turn an incredible source for celebration (of their achievements!) into such bickering, which is when I said that I did not understand why one would risk their career [over unfounded accusations]. Genuinely, at that moment, I was trying to care for him and do a last ditch attempt to get a chance to give them all the credits that they deserve. I deeply apologize for this extremely poor choice of words, it is the opposite of what I was trying to convey. (I should say that I retracted them on the spot by the way.)
 
4) Overall, on a personal level, it was incredibly difficult to have these conversations. Levent refused to attend any of the meetings despite my repeated asking. As Sholto Douglas said, there will need to be coordination between Anthropic and OpenAI in the future; I felt I was doing a proxy negotiation with Anthropic while the Anthropic employee refused to directly participate.

quoted_text:
It's notable that @MetaDAOProject were the first to controversially get rid of investor lockups, and it ended up being objectively positive and widely copied (most recently by Ethena).

Now they are bravely experimenting with getting rid of founder lockups- even more controversial. I was adamantly against it at first, but have changed my mind since.

That a founder can sell early doesn't preclude the right founders with the right vision to hold their stake and remain incentivized - those can continue as is, and often do in public equity markets.

As long as transparency of sales exists, and price-appreciation conditions remain, the vesting lockup period is not an important investor protection. Getting rid of it doesn't really impact MetaDAO's pitch to investors, but it does materially and positively impact the pitch of MetaDAO to 21st century "fast company" founders, an ever growing cohort which have place to for access to capital markets.

UFG is doing something interesting with tokenized indices.

I really like products where the treasury grows the backing behind the token over time. @OlympusDAO is the obvious example, and @polarisfnd is taking a similar idea with pETH.

One of UFG's first products applies this to the S&P 500 through an options structure:

This could fit @roycoprotocol 's tranching mechanics really well but Royco could enforce the coverage rather than hardcoding it into an options structure.

@defidave is deep into UFG and I like seeing people who've spent years covering this space getting involved in building projects themselves, similar to @Wajahat and @0xBobdbldr pushing Starcap.

author: leslieloser_
quoted_text:
The United Founders Group $UFG Thesis 🏛️

$UFG an onchain ETH treasury that pays you to hold via multiple revenue streams. It has the potential to be the $YFI of this cycle; it is truly novel in its mechanics yet simple in its design.

Each $UFG token is first and foremost 98% redeemable for ETH in its treasury. The other 2% is an exit fee that is sent back into the treasury, creating a permanent rising floor of the ETH in it. The $UFG treasury is an immutable contract that is not controlled by anyone.

Because of its tokenomics of having a fixed supply of 1 billion that burns $UFG every time that ETH is redeemed from the treasury, making the token deflationary. So now you inherently have this interesting conflux of ETH in the treasury perpetually increasing while $UFG supply constantly decreases.

The first revenue stream of $UFG are 100% of the creator fees from $UFG's own market on @ponsdotfamily. Anyone can call this contract to collect for the treasury and in the future, the contract can collect revenue streams from future products and primitives. And while many new tokens are pairing to untested onchain stocks, $UFG is pairing to the most tried and tested decentralized finance asset there is, ETH.

This comes to why I like $UFG so much. It is because it is fair. I believe that we are seeing a swing back to PvE this cycle where holding and contributing will be rewarded while paper hands will be punished. $PONS was the first to prove this, building a launchpad that rewards creators with fees and holders with buybacks. What launches like $UFG prove is that $PONS isn't just for memecoins but for real DeFi primitives looking to launch in a fair manner and those that build in this spirit will win.

On the roadmap, the next revenue stream is options with the first asset being tokenized-SPY exposure. How it works is there are two tokens, a "Buffer token" a which holds a 10% loss in exchange for a capped upside. The "Writer token" is the inverse, it posts the collateral that absorbs the losses and is only paid in the upside goes beyond the Buffer cap. Both tokens fund themselves purely from their own trading fees, take no deposits, and route a fixed share of fees to the $UFG treasury. There will be more information about this product soon.

I've talked to the founder and multiple holders of $UFG and its success really depends on the people. We have an incredible opportunity here to build something that is in the spirit of DeFi but it can only happen if people believe that a better future is possible.

The flywheel is already in motion; more products -> more revenue streams -> more ETH accumulation -> more proving the power of DeFi, but to get it into turbo drive it can't be done alone. Not by me. Not by you. Not by any single person. It will have to be a group effort.

It is early and yes there are risks, but if you're reading and made it this fair there must be something within you that wants to take a chance.

The time has come to return to tradition. The time has come to return to PvE. The time has come for $UFG 🏛️

0x5b6d236e39a4723a8f79db93cfd1af4d228f9c60

At the time of our review, the HYPE remained in the staking balance and had not yet entered the withdrawal queue. If the attacker initiates a cWithdraw, the assets can be transferred after the seven-day waiting period.

In two similar cases we handled recently, the victims also had assets still in staking when their accounts were compromised. Due to the absence of a user-triggered emergency pause or recovery mechanism, they were unable to prevent those assets from subsequently being withdrawn and stolen. Losses under this scenario have already exceeded $1.1 million. The 10,287 HYPE in this case now faces the same risk.

To better protect staked assets that remain pending withdrawal after a private key or account-signing compromise, we propose that Hyperliquid consider introducing an optional Guardian / Recovery mechanism that users can configure in advance.

A Guardian should only be able to place a temporary hold on cWithdraw, transfers, Agent approvals, and multisig changes. It must never be able to move funds, and the hold should expire automatically without allowing indefinite renewal.

Guardian replacement or account recovery should require a timelock, evidence-based review, and an independent or validator-governed threshold, with every state change recorded publicly on-chain.

🎙️ Cregis MicUp Vol. 19: Risk & Control in Digital Asset Operations

🗓️ September 9, 2026 | 5:00 PM GMT+8 | Live X Space

🔗 Set your reminder: https://t.co/pEO4I0DYu1
Digital asset security remains a serious operational challenge. In the first half of 2026 alone, CertiK recorded more than $1.31 billion in losses across the industry. Behind these incidents is a broader question for enterprises: where can risk enter the process of managing and moving digital assets, and how can it be identified before it results in a loss?

Risk may originate within the technology, emerge through on-chain interactions or develop from the way people and systems handle transactions. AI introduces further uncertainty as it becomes more widely used across enterprise operations and takes on a greater role in analyzing information, supporting decisions and interacting with financial systems.

Join Cregis for a practical discussion on what recent incidents reveal about enterprise risk, how potential threats can be identified across digital asset operations, and how security controls should evolve as AI becomes more deeply involved.

🎤 Meet Our Expert Panel:
Jonathan Riss, OSINT & Blockchain Intelligence Analyst @CertiK
Tony Tan, Hong Kong Community Lead @SlowMist_Team

🎙️ Moderated by Bovey Li, Deputy Marketing Director at Cregis

📋 What We’ll Explore:
🔸 Analysis of Representative Security Incidents
A closer look at notable incidents, how the attacks unfolded, where the risks entered and what enterprises can learn from the controls that failed or limited the impact.

🔸 Identifying Risk Across Digital Asset Operations
How can enterprises identify vulnerabilities and warning signs across their technology, on-chain activities and operating processes before they develop into security incidents?

🔸 Structuring Security for Real Operations
How should code audits, infrastructure security, wallet controls, approval policies, monitoring and incident response work together in daily operations?

🔸 How AI Changes Enterprise Security Risk
As enterprises use AI across more systems and workflows, where could new risks emerge around information, permissions, decisions and transaction execution? How do these risks differ from traditional security threats, and what strategies can enterprises adopt in response?

Why This Matters:
For anyone responsible for managing digital assets, security cannot be assessed through code audits or wallet protection alone. Losses can result from weaknesses across connected systems, transaction decisions and everyday operating processes, even when individual components appear secure.

This session will help businesses understand how incidents develop across the full flow of digital asset operations, identify gaps in their existing controls, and consider how security responsibilities should evolve as AI gains greater access to enterprise systems and financial activities.
📌 Join us 5 minutes early to secure your spot!

text:
$BONER pushed the tokenized $HIMS from around $29 to $132 over the weekend.

What's interesting is the actual $HIMS stock itself barely moved.

So now you've got tokenized $HIMS trading 4x above the real thing. The Arb bots are hammering the pool trying to close that gap, degens keep buying against them, and every one of those swaps pays a fee to whoever's providing the liquidity.

When there's that many trades going on, somebody's getting paid. 

And they're doing it without needing to call the top, hold either token, or even care where $HIMS price ended up.

Interested in getting a piece?

@revertfinance currently shows LPs around stocks like RBLX/USDG and HOOD/USDG, alongside all the usual high-volatility crypto pools.

Some of the top positions have completely ridiculous displayed APRs. There's a WETH/FOMO position showing 87K%+ APR right now.

Obviously I wouldn't underwrite anything based on a number like that. A concentrated LP can show an insane APR after a short burst of volume and look completely different tomorrow.

Instead of looking at the pool APR and jumping in, you can open the actual LP positions and see their range, age, PnL, ROI, fee APR and liquidity.

So my process is basically:

Find a stock pool getting real volume
 → Check existing LPs on Revert
 → Compare different fee tiers/ranges
 → Look at how long the position has actually been earning
 → Then decide if the fees are worth the LP risk

I'd rather LP a stock w/ $USDG pair than blindly copy the highest-APR meme LP.

You still get exposure to the volume being created around the meme/stock trade, without choosing to become exit liquidity for a random meme.

One catch though...

The $HIMS move above is the reminder that a tokenized stock isn't actually the stock. When CT decides to run it, it decouples from the real ticker and your "safe" stock LP gets run over like any other pair. 

You're not taking stock risk. You're taking stock risk plus whatever CT decides to do with it.

Revert and @KrystalDeFi both handle the management side after that: moving ranges, collecting/compounding fees, automations and PnL tracking.

Everyone is staring at the token doing 10x and overlooking who's collecting fees from all of them.

LPing can be worth it if @RobinhoodCrypto Chain keeps going this direction.

text:
$LIT 5 刀+了。

当时 1 刀左右抄底了一些，然后新低止损了。后面来来回回做了几次，有赚有亏，反正没拿到现在。简单复盘一下。

我觉得 Lighter 真正实现预期反转，是与 Robinhood 合作的那个时间节点。

就像 @mdzzi 之前提到的，现在 Perpdex 其实已经不太缺产品力了，真正稀缺的是分发能力。尤其是在积分激励逐渐结束之后，用户为什么要继续留在你这里交易，会变成一个越来越重要的问题。

Robinhood Wallet 刚好补上了 Lighter 最缺的这一块（这是纯叙事逻辑来看的，不是从筹码角度）。

包括 Aster，现在也做得蛮好的，同样是类似的逻辑。它背后有 Binance Wallet 这个天然入口。之前交易 Basecat 的时候，我就发现可以直接通过 Binance Wallet 交易 Basecat 合约，走的底层就是 Aster。

从这个角度看，以 Bitget Wallet 作为分发层的 Popdex，我也会继续关注。

综上，我现在看 Perpdex，会越来越关注一个问题：你的用户到底从哪里来？

产品做得好当然重要，但产品本身越来越容易趋同。CLOB、RFQ、零手续费、网格、Swap……大家看到有效的东西之后，最终都会慢慢跟上。

这时候就要看你的护城河：1）用户关系；2）分发能力；3）资源背景。这是真正不容易被复制的东西。

最后补充几句：

1、之前我觉得做 ticker 差异化也蛮重要的，直到 @mablemeibao 老师跟我讲，单纯 ticker 差异化其实没那么有壁垒，一个热点资产你能上，理论上别人也能上，这种优势很容易被抹平。所以我还是蛮期待 Trasia 后续的进展，以及它们的破局手段。

2、Hyperliquid 是最不需要担心分发的，几乎大部分钱包、前端的第一选择都是 Hyperliquid。其 Hip-3 龙头Tradexyz 同样也因此受益。

3、即将 TGE 的 Variational，同样需要考虑后续分发的事情。我很喜欢这个台子，团队足够有产品力，一直在试图理解这个市场，找到市场上缺失的东西，并希望用自己的新产品来解决这个问题。Swap 就是一个很好的例子。

Introducing: Browser Use Pi 🥧

A tiny TypeScript web agent, built with Astra and improved through real browser evals.

We’ve built Browser Use, Browser Harness and BrowserCode. This time we asked Astra to combine what worked, with as little code and as few heuristics as possible. Then Astra hill climbed:

> Run real browser tasks
> Read traces
> Fix what breaks
> Delete complexity
> Run again and repeat.

The result? Pi Mono + persistent V8 REPL + raw CDP. Fully in TypeScript. Cloud browsers, persistent sessions, streaming and step limits included 🌀

text:
🚨SlowMist TI Alert🚨

💸 @EnsoBuild Loss: ~5.6 ETH

🔍 Root Cause: An oracle price calculation error occurred in the Enso Finance / DPI Strategy Vault. In `Controller.deposit()`, the EnsoOracle's `estimateStrategy()` is called before and after the user tokens are transferred, and shares are minted on the difference: `mint = amountAdded * totalSupply / valueBefore`. The valuation chain — EnsoOracle → ItemEstimator → `ProtocolOracle.consult()` — prices tokens via UniV3 `pool.observe()`, but the registry's `fee` field is reused as `secondsAgo`, producing a near-spot TWAP window. Due to the absence of TWAP consistency checks or price range validation—combined with the fact that the liquidity in the Uniswap v3 pool used for price calculation was inherently imbalanced—an attacker was able to swap 0.683 WETH for 268.42 FARM tokens on Uniswap v2 in a single transaction, while the imbalanced v3 pool incorrectly valued that amount at 6.3 WETH (~ 9.2x). Subsequently, an excessive number of shares were minted at an incorrect price and redeemed for profit.

📌 Attacker: `0x3196398321D77a2511d369DCB6eCa9d2aD87b73A`
📌 Victim (Strategy): `0x890ed1ee6d435a35d11051d9ed97ff457ce53b5942`
📌 Vulnerable contract: 
Controller impl: `0xd8D22509C1fe47516D8F82A28CFd728111F57Ef1`
Oracle: `0xAb7505eB360cE0D63e8E88f7853677EcD5537DC0`

text:
Pons doesn’t allow taxes to be changed post-launch.

There is a big group of people claiming that this is the case, but it’s simply wrong.

What I noticed is that some terminals (for whatever reason) route buys and sells through high-tax pools, even though the Pons-initialized @Uniswap V4 pool is not only a) liquid, but also b) a 0% tax pool with a 1% hook fee (as disclosed on all trades).

When a malicious actor tries to vamp said pool, it can show up on terminals as an increased tax. That number then goes up and down depending on misconfigurations within the router and which pool the terminal decides to route through.

I have asked terminals to change this, as it hurts users and causes unnecessary FUD.

Pons has a 1% hooked pool. If you see more than that (unless a deployer set higher taxes at launch), you are being routed through the wrong pools and therefore being charged more.

This does not mean taxes were changed post-launch.

text:
Robinhood 开启币股玩法后，Solana 上走出了 Stonk，而今天 BNB Chain 上也跑出了一波资产：

链上代币 BNC4 一度冲破 30 美元（溢价近 10 倍），伴生的 Meme 币 $4Stock 市值最高来到80m，而美股正股 BNC 也在盘前暴涨一度超 50%。

相信很多人没赶上这波节奏，午觉醒来完全懵了：

BNC、BNC4、$4Stock 到底是什么关系？“股票配土狗”玩法换了个链有啥不一样吗？我还能上车吗？

让精通马后炮的小编带你拆解一下。

1.今天到底在炒什么？其实还是币股配对
- $BNC （正股）：美股上市公司，其实是BNB 财库公司，手里屯了 50 多万枚 BNB，属于和币安生态强绑定的微盘股。 

- BNC4（股票代币）：https://t.co/iN9KeCb8W9 搞出来的链上映射代币，对应 $BNC 股票。

 - $4Stock（Meme币）：蹭这个新叙事，直接用 BNC4 当底池发出来的纯土狗,进行币股配对。

2. 新叙事在于 pre-bStock，抢跑发链上股票
这个玩法的精髓，其实是拿小市值、但没有上币安链上的股票做文章。

币安官方现在有股票代币统称为 bStock，但正规军上币流程慢，没法覆盖所有热门的微盘股和 Meme 股。

所以，https://t.co/iN9KeCb8W9 搞了套叫 4Stock 的机制，本质上是充当了币安主站股票的“创新区”或者“Alpha 板块”。

它的核心逻辑是：

只要官方还没上的美股，拿你的 USDC 去买真股票，1:1 铸造上链给你。 
如果以后这只股票上了币安官方的 bStock，你的代币可以 1:1 无缝转换过去。

于是，这个玩法的第一个小股票就是今天的 $BNC 。

它既是 BNB 的“财库股”，又能勾起美股微盘股逼空 + 链上土狗炒作的叙事，等于官方选了个能激发兴趣的标的。

3. $4stock 暴涨，带飞 BNC4 
既然 https://t.co/iN9KeCb8W9 的币股配对是用 BNC4 当底池发 $4Stock，这就引发了一个连锁效应。

链上玩家为了冲 $4Stock 这个热门土狗，必须先拿 BNC4 去换。

当海量的买盘涌入，想要博弈“美股逼空”的叙事时，BNC4 的需求瞬间爆炸。 

短短几个小时，原本对应美股盘后仅 4 美元出头的 BNC4，在链上被硬生生买出了近 10 倍的脱缰溢价，最高冲破了 30 多美元。

4. 聪明钱降维打击，时间差套利狂赚 20 万刀

懂机制的玩家立刻发现了“无风险印钞机”。 既然官方支持打 USDC 按真实 $BNC 股票价格（4刀出头）1:1 铸造 BNC4 ，那我直接找官方进货不就行了？

比如首批提交申请的 0xShawn，果断按 4 刀多的真实成本向官方申请 Mint。

等币一到账，反手卖出 BNC4。 而由于此时链上 BNC4 高度溢价，一波时间差套利，让他直接净赚超 20 万美金。

5. 我能上车吗？

恐怕不太能，至少溢价窗口已经大幅消失了。

套利大户吃饱退场，随着新铸造的 BNC4 陆续砸向市场，溢价逐渐消失，GMGN 数据显示目前 BNC4 跌回了 7 刀附近。

而更亏的人，应该是后排跟风去官方申请铸造 BNC4 的那波。

官方去美股券商买股票BNC、再发币给你 BNC4，这个过程可能是“小时级”的。
而链上价格变化非常大，可能也就意味着你铸造的成本价，已经远超当时美股正股的价格了...币还没捂热就会血亏。

目前已有用户反馈自己铸造时平台给的结算成本高于美股价格，官方目前回应是“按实际买入执行价发币，差额会退款”；
但这种链上和 mint 操作时机造成的价差，应该是目前玩法里比较突出的问题。

小编用  GMGN 自带的 AI 问了下，截止发帖分析前，BNC4 前排的10个地址，除了流动性池和系统地址，普通钱包地址里甚至没有一个是盈利的。。。(见截图3）

可见套利溢价砸下来后，有些大户应该也套在了山顶上？

目前看，如果后续没有自动化的做市和赎回机制来抹平“拿U买股”的时间差，
那盈利必然会属于跑在前面进行套利的人。

text:
QUOTE 1 - Love for life and rationality are essential for life to become a source of joy and flourishing.
: Love for life and rationality are not optional extras. They are the essential foundation that turns mere existence into a source of genuine joy and flourishing.
Love for life brings warmth, gratitude, and a deep appreciation for the gift of being alive. It fuels curiosity, resilience, and the desire to protect and nurture what is beautiful. Rationality, in turn, provides clarity, honesty, and the ability to navigate reality without illusion. Together, they create a powerful synergy: a heart that cherishes life guided by a mind that understands it.
Without love for life, rationality can become cold and empty. Without rationality, love for life can become blind or fragile. When both are present and balanced, life stops being a struggle to endure and becomes something worth celebrating every day.
This combination allows us to face difficulties with courage, find meaning in ordinary moments, and build a future worth living in. It is the quiet secret to a flourishing existence.
QUOTE 2 - Love is the only force that turns millions of individuals into a nation, and nations into humanity.
: Love is the only force powerful enough to turn millions of separate individuals into a genuine nation, and nations into a united humanity.
Laws can regulate behavior, shared interests can create alliances, and culture can foster identity, but only love creates the deep emotional bond of belonging and mutual care. It transforms “them” into “us.” It makes people willing to sacrifice, to protect, to build together rather than merely coexist.
On a larger scale, the same principle applies. When love extends beyond national borders, it turns competing states into parts of a single human family. Without this connecting force, unity remains fragile, easily broken by fear or self-interest. With it, differences become complementary rather than divisive.
Love is the invisible thread that holds humanity together. It is what makes a nation more than a territory, and humanity more than a collection of nations. In the end, the strength and future of both depend not on power or wealth, but on our capacity to love one another.

text:
[Writing this in a personal capacity, not on behalf of my employer (Anthropic).]

Jacob’s thread is very worth reading. Here’s my birds-eye view of the situation with risks from AI:

1. AI developers believe their technology could cause human extinction (or similarly bad outcomes). This could happen in the next few years. In general, the more senior the employee, the more concerned they are.

2. Why do AI developers continue despite the risk? Due to a mixture of commercial incentives and a belief that they are in a race with other, less responsible AI developers that will abuse the technology or develop it less safely.

3. Unlike traditional software, we can’t “program” AIs to behave how we’d like. AIs frequently severely misbehave. For instance, AIs from multiple developers recently hacked their way out of secure evaluation environments and into real-world companies, even though no one asked them to do this.

4. We have methods that can nudge AIs towards better behavior, but nothing that can robustly align them. Insofar as there is a plan, it’s to make sure that AIs are good enough at alignment training that they can align their successors better than we can align current AIs.

5. Many AI developer staff desperately want to slow down to figure out how to build AI more safely. That was the intent of this open letter (which I signed): https://t.co/TZOm3LfptY

I work on safety research at Anthropic because I hope my work will reduce the chance of these extinction-level bad outcomes.

text:
OpenAI 卷入“抢成果”争议，为什么会带火隐私 AI 叙事？

当数学家还在争论研究成果到底归谁，市场已经找到了交易方向：主打隐私 AI 的 Venice，代币 $VVV 单日一度涨近 40%，突破 25 美元。

事情的起因，是数学家 Tristan Buckmaster 与在 Anthropic 任职的 Levent Alpöge，以私人身份合作研究流体方程。他们花了近一年时间，借助 AI 在 8 月取得重要突破，距离百万美元悬赏的千禧难题一步之遥。

研究过程中，两人一直用 Codex 辅助工作，大量未发表的草稿也放了进去。结果到了 9 月初，OpenAI 听说相关进展后启动攻关，几天后就告诉他们：内部模型做出了更进一步的结果。

这就出现了一个尴尬的问题：怎么确认 OpenAI 没有抄袭他们的研究草稿？

据 Buckmaster 披露，双方沟通还涉及排除合作者署名的提议；他拒绝并表示要公开经过后，对方甚至问他“为什么要毁掉自己的职业生涯”。（p1）

OpenAI 则否认为解决问题专门访问两人的用户数据，但表示，无法完全排除去标识化的使用数据曾帮助改进模型的可能。（p2）

真相虽尚无定论，但这一争议带火了隐私 AI ：你交给模型的，可能是论文、代码，也可能是还没赚钱的商业计划。而这些都有可能被模型盗取。

“你的想法会不会被 AI 公司截胡” 给隐私 AI 提供了一个比技术口号更容易传播的故事。

同时 Venice 已经抓住了宣传机会。创始人 Erik Voorhees 直接喊话：“数学家们，如果不想被窥探，就用 Venice。” （p3）

而前两天因清仓 ETH 而赚麻了的 David Hoffman 也随着这一波行情真正的实现了大满贯。（此前消息：Hoffman 于 5 月 21 日宣布清仓全部 ETH，披露将约 50% 资金买入VVV、NEAR、ZEC、HYPE，剩余50%定投并最终全部买成LIT。）

从 ZEC 到 VVV，隐私赛道能否随着AI的发展迎来新的故事值得一看。

本文仅作信息整理，不构成投资建议，请注意交易风险。

text:
AI is probably the biggest prisoner’s dilemma we’ve ever created. Everyone knows slowing down might be safer. But if OpenAI slows down and Anthropic doesn’t, OpenAI loses. If the US slows down and China doesn’t, the US loses. So nobody slows down.

That’s what makes this so insane. You don’t need some evil person trying to destroy the world. You just need a bunch of people making the rational decision for themselves over and over until collectively we’ve raced somewhere none of us actually wanted to go.

It’s a race to zero. Zero cost of intelligence. Zero time between thinking and doing. Maybe eventually zero need for us at all.

Pons创始人否认代币税率上线后被修改，称问题源于交易终端路由错误

Pons doesn’t allow taxes to be changed post-launch.

There is a big group of people claiming that this is the case, but it’s simply wrong.

What I noticed is that some terminals (for whatever reason) route buys and sells through high-tax pools, even though the Pons-initialized @Uniswap V4 pool is not only a) liquid, but also b) a 0% tax pool with a 1% hook fee (as disclosed on all trades).

When a malicious actor tries to vamp said pool, it can show up on terminals as an increased tax. That number then goes up and down depending on misconfigurations within the router and which pool the terminal decides to route through.

I have asked terminals to change this, as it hurts users and causes unnecessary FUD.

Pons has a 1% hooked pool. If you see more than that (unless a deployer set higher taxes at launch), you are being routed through the wrong pools and therefore being charged more.

author: billqian_hk
quoted_text:
每当听到圈外人质疑AI和区块链结合的必要性

每当看到币圈创业者讨论区块链和AI结合，就言必称agentic payment，ai trading这些细枝末节的领域

就很有冲动告诉他们—

AI跟区块链交汇的终点，在元宇宙/虚拟世界。

AI 让软件从“被动执行指令的工具”，变成拥有长期记忆、推理能力和自主行动能力的 Agent。下一步的问题是：这些 Agent 如何拥有身份？如何持有资产？如何进行可信交易？如何在没有人类逐笔授权的情况下，形成真正的经济活动？

这恰恰是 Blockchain 的价值。

DID 解决 Agent 的数字身份；
智能合约提供无需信任的交易和执行环境；
Tokenization 让数字资产、算力、数据、知识产权甚至 Agent 本身具备可编程的所有权；
零知识证明解决隐私与可验证计算；
高性能 L1/L2、Account Abstraction 和链上支付基础设施，则让机器之间可以进行低成本、高频率的原生交易。

而 AI 负责赋予这些数字实体“智能”。

当一个 Agent 可以感知环境、调用模型、访问数据、使用工具、管理钱包、签署交易，并根据目标自主配置算力、购买数据、雇佣其他 Agent，甚至创造和出售数字资产时，互联网的基本经济单元就可能从“人”变成“人 + Agent”。

这时候，Metaverse 才开始有意义。

它不再只是 VR/AR 的三维界面，而是一个由 AI Agent、数字身份、可编程资产和去中心化网络共同构成的持久化数字经济空间。

AI 是 Intelligence Layer。
Blockchain 是 Ownership & Settlement Layer。
Metaverse 是 Interaction & Execution Layer。

最终，我们看到的可能不是“人进入虚拟世界”，而是现实世界与数字世界逐渐融合：人、AI Agent、机器人和数字资产，在同一个开放的经济网络中持续交互。

这可能才是 AI 与 Blockchain 最终汇合的地方——

一个真正拥有智能、身份、所有权和经济活动的数字世界。

创业最重要的是选对方向。

👉Gas：Gas 用 USDC 付，费用按美元计价，发币、买卖都不用先囤一条高波动链代币
👉速度：约一秒内最终确认，共识引擎 Malachite
👉兼容性：EVM 兼容，Solidity、钱包、Uniswap 这类工具基本能直接用
👉验证机制：许可制验证者，出块节点不是谁都能当

Arc的出现到底意味着啥？
Circle 过去只在别人的链上发美元，现在要自己拥有美元跑在上面的结算层。对机构来说，这意味着可预测费用、瞬时结算、合规入口。
所以，Arc的融资也相当豪华，2026 年 5 月以约 30 亿美元完全稀释估值预售 2.22 亿美元，a16z领投，BlackRock、Apollo、ICE 等参与。

而对散户参与者，Arc本身作为一条被华尔街点过头的新链，开荒期的 Meme 也极具吸引力，毕竟Robinhood珠玉在前嘛🤑

🔥二、Arc的热钱会流向哪
机会总的来说可以分成三层。

🌱开荒层：现在就能交易的 Meme 和发射台
新链前几周的路径基本固定：稳定币进场 → 发射台新币 → 少数叙事对上的龙头 → 平台币。
与其他链不同，Arc 的特殊之处是创建、买入、卖出都直接用 USDC，摩擦比“先买原生toklen再打狗”低一截。不过，公共主网和官方跨链一旦打开，这批“老币”可能被当成龙一，也可能被新资金换庄。

🛠️应用层： DeFi 和交易终端
目前，Fomo、edgeX 已经公开承诺首日接入。预期名单里还有 Uniswap、Aerodrome、Aave、Morpho，以及 FalconX、GSR、Keyrock 等做市商。

💎中长期层：代币化资产和 ARC 本身。
BUIDL、DTC 代币化要到 2027 年才能真正铺开。ARC 代币有锁定期，不是现在链上热钱的主菜。对于看好Payfi的同学可以开始仔细研究了。

🔥三、Arc的埋伏机会：头部发射台＆Meme们

🚀发射台：
1.TOLLY（约 247 万美元，0xbc43ce8dec648ea298c4275559b81d6261c90b67）
介绍：Tolly 发射台 + DEX 的平台币。新项目不走联合曲线，全部供应直接进永久锁定的 USDC 池。交易收 1%：买入产生的 USDC 费用里，约 64% 给创建者、12% 持有人奖励、10% 归协议，其余回购销毁 TOLLY 和对应项目币；卖出产生的项目币费用全部销毁。
逻辑：赌它成为Arc链的 PONS，一旦起来吃的就是整条链发币流量。

2.WARP（约 87 万美元，0x384c60f98ecd4c26345499345c03d677e40f115e）
介绍：Warp 发射台/交易终端相关代币。走联合曲线，市值到约 6.9 万美元后迁移到 WarpDex 并销毁 LP。计划用 Circle CCTP，从 Ethereum、Base、Arbitrum 销毁 USDC，在 Arc 铸造后自动买入。
逻辑：赌它成为 Arc 的跨链发射入口，让用户体感上“免跨链”地把别链上的 USDC 直接吸进 Arc 的同一个曲线池。

🤑Meme：
https://t.co/GbAcblDOSB（约 294 万美元，0xeb64987643db71c76b2a2be7e723decc995e5b37）
社区根据追踪 USDC 活动的网页吉祥物做的 Meme，戴墨镜的蓝色稳定币形象。

2.Architects（约 82 万美元，0x8bcb94279fc2c984ec34e0c1f2192df8c69ea4f0）
Circle / Arc 多次把社区贡献者叫做 Architects（建筑师），CEO Jeremy Allaire 也用过这个词。

3.ARCAT（约 71 万美元，0x07704b06981ea962b87296362a1281484d160000）
更早的 Arc 猫咪盘之一，源自 USDC 官方分享过的 “Cat Bat Hat Fat Rat” 视频。

4.BEANCAT（约 27.5万美元，0x41c8A71f630c636294009fa4FB0CC4c3bBE674fe）
对应@arc账号早期历史头像（大约 2012 年的“豆”猫头像），社区对标其他链的 CashCat。

🔥四、打Arc Meme前，你还得先准备好Arc USDC！

这时候，一些动手能力强的同学就要问了，我用USDC咋买不到这些币啊？！
别急，因为你需要的，是 Arc USDC。

经社区整理，目前比较直接的方法是通过OTC 市场 Unstable：https://t.co/0XXXyUdnq2。可以用 Eth主网的 USDC，向已经持有一些 Arc USDC 的卖家购买，价格由卖家自己挂单。

不过，由于供不应求，现在 Arc USDC 通常存在较高溢价。Arc USDC：USDC基本在 1.8：1。另外 Unstable 还会收取 3% 手续费，所以入场Arc的成本还是比较高的。

而如果拿到Arc USDC 之后，如果钱包没有自动识别 Arc，是可以手动添加网络的。
名称：ARC Mainnet
RPC URL：https://t.co/D4qbEGy2MA
Chain ID：5042
符号：USDC
如果 RPC 比较卡，也可以试一下备用：https://t.co/BaSyLcgxp6

🔥结语、下场前先确认清这几件事

现在能交易的，都是私有的Arc主网资产，没有官方的任何背书。公共主网 RPC、浏览器、官方跨链参数以 Circle 发布为准，社区节点卡顿、交易失败很常见。

早期头部盘市值上百万，池子可能只有几万到十万刀，进出都容易砸穿。

所以，关注合约、流动性、发射台质量、入场点位，这四件事是保证你在Arc蛮荒期活下来的重中之重。

Recently, we became aware of an exploit on the Nomic chain. The exploit allowed the attacker to double-spend nBTC, allowing them to send false vouchers to Osmosis.  Osmosis and IBC were not compromised, as the bug was in a custom forwarding mechanism on Nomic.

39.84 nBTC of the minted total sits within Alloyed BTC, representing ~36% of its backing.

When this was noticed, moderation subDAOs froze inflows and outflows to both Nomic and Alloyed BTC on Osmosis, and performed an emergency upgrade with validators to freeze 22.65 BTC in the attacker's address.

We will propose seizing these assets to governance and ask governance to use accrued BTC in the community pool to cover the remaining balance and restore the full backing of Alloyed BTC.

text:
🚨SlowMist TI Alert🚨

💸 @EnsoBuild Loss: ~5.6 ETH

🔍 Root Cause: An oracle price calculation error occurred in the Enso Finance / DPI Strategy Vault. In `Controller.deposit()`, the EnsoOracle's `estimateStrategy()` is called before and after the user tokens are transferred, and shares are minted on the difference: `mint = amountAdded * totalSupply / valueBefore`. The valuation chain — EnsoOracle → ItemEstimator → `ProtocolOracle.consult()` — prices tokens via UniV3 `pool.observe()`, but the registry's `fee` field is reused as `secondsAgo`, producing a near-spot TWAP window. Due to the absence of TWAP consistency checks or price range validation—combined with the fact that the liquidity in the Uniswap v3 pool used for price calculation was inherently imbalanced—an attacker was able to swap 0.683 WETH for 268.42 FARM tokens on Uniswap v2 in a single transaction, while the imbalanced v3 pool incorrectly valued that amount at 6.3 WETH (~ 9.2x). Subsequently, an excessive number of shares were minted at an incorrect price and redeemed for profit.

📌 Attacker: `0x3196398321D77a2511d369DCB6eCa9d2aD87b73A`
📌 Victim (Strategy): `0x890ed1ee6d435a35d11051d9ed97ff457ce53b5942`
📌 Vulnerable contract: 
Controller impl: `0xd8D22509C1fe47516D8F82A28CFd728111F57Ef1`
Oracle: `0xAb7505eB360cE0D63e8E88f7853677EcD5537DC0`

text:
Friedrich Merz muss zurücktreten.
 
Vor knapp zwei Jahren hatte ich die Hoffnung, dass Friedrich Merz eine gute Wahl ist. 

Ich hatte auf wirtschaftlichen Sachverstand gehofft und auf einen Kanzler, der uns wieder eine Vision gibt: Wo wollen wir als Land 2030 stehen? Ein Kanzler, der tatsächlich Bürokratie abbauen will. Der sein Volk stark macht statt schlechtredet.

Heute muss ich sagen: Die Hoffnung war falsch.

Friedrich Merz hat keine Führungs- oder Regierungserfahrung und das merkt man.

Friedrich Merz ist ein Ankündigungskanzler, der für Reformen keine Mehrheiten organisieren kann.
Und: Friedrich Merz schafft es nicht, uns eine Vision und Zukunftshoffnung zu vermitteln.

Denn: Wir brauchen harte Reformen, die vielen Menschen viel abverlangen werden. Wo wir alle (auch ich) ihren Beitrag leisten müssen. Das geht nur, wenn man die Menschen emotional mitnimmt. Die Menschen gehen nur dann durch eine Wüste, wenn man weiß, dass dahinter die Oase kommt.

Es bleibt für mich keine andere Wahl: Er muss zurücktreten.

Wir haben ein gewähltes Parlament. Ein neuer Kanzler hat nun noch 2 bis 2,5 Jahre Zeit, neuen Schwung zu bringen.

Fast forward to an agentic world – and those complex Solana priority fees are nothing for an agent to digest AND gives them the added ability to better optimize their cost (given their “intent” of that specific transaction).  

Credit where credit is due – Solana priority fees were ahead of its time.

Quality held across both gates: Tool Eval Bench and MMLU benchmark score.

Every promoted change was required to show no quality regression relative to the baseline on either benchmark.

What you get today:
• the optimised vLLM source (24 files, +3.3K lines vs stock)
• a prebuilt wheel: CUDA 13.0, Python 3.12, sm_120
• reproducible benchmark scripts + raw R000/R107 logs
• 262K context, MTP spec decoding, TurboQuant KV on one 32 GB card

Caveats, because they matter: this is a hardware- and model-specific fork, not a general vLLM replacement. 

Validated on one RTX 5090 with RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 only. Throughput is client-observed and includes prefill time.

text:
大压抑时代，高富帅已经过时了，孙学，黄毛，薄肌才是版本答案！其中，版本答案的底层逻辑只有一个！孙学！

高富帅是增量时代的产物：它要求你在身高、财富、长相三条线上同时满配，成本极高，而且大部分投入是给旁观者看的。

增量年代旁观者的羡慕能变现，存量年代（大压抑时代）变现渠道关了，那些投入就变成纯沉没成本。

版本答案只有一个底层逻辑：孙学。

投入产出比最大化，能赢就行，过程中别人怎么评价不计入成本。

黄毛是孙学在性格与外貌上的实现。

高富帅要维护人设、讲究姿态、等一个体面的出场时机；黄毛不装、不等、不解释，简单打扮小帅即可，直接把事办了。

高富帅只有张凌赫能当，黄毛只要愿意，谁都能当。

人设是高维护成本资产，黄毛把这项预算清零，全部投到结果上。

薄肌是孙学在身体上的实现。

大肌肉是展示型资产：训练时长、饮食管理、维持成本都高，收益是被看见。

薄肌是功能型资产：低维护、高续航、随时能跑。同样是身体，一个为观众服务，一个为自己服务。

所以这三样东西不是并列关系，是一个方法论加两个应用。高富帅是把资源花在"让人羡慕"上，孙学是把资源花在"最后站着的是我"上。

大压抑时代，前者是消费，后者才是投资。

text:
the first thing that got me into @ONcompute was pretty obvious.

H200s from $2.16/hr.

hard to ignore that when you use GPUs regularly.

but after spending more time with Ocean, i don't think the price is what makes it interesting anymore.

it's how little infra i have to deal with.

i pick the hardware, send the job, pay for the runtime and get the output back into my project.

if i'm done, i'm done.

there's no instance sitting there eating money because i might need it again later.

and i can do most of this from the same tools i'm already using, like Codex or Claude.

that makes a bigger difference than i expected.

then i started looking at what happens underneath all of this.

the jobs run across P2P compute nodes, payments go through escrow, and i can choose where the workload runs instead of throwing it into some random cloud box.

Compute-to-Data got me interested for another reason.

sometimes you don't want a dataset leaving its environment at all.

instead of moving the data to wherever the compute is, Ocean can bring the computation to the data and return the permitted result.

the data stays there.

after using it for a while, calling Ocean a place for cheap decentralized GPUs feels a bit incomplete.

i came for the GPU pricing.

i stayed because the workflow is starting to make more sense than renting another cloud instance every time i need serious compute.

text:
7个月后回过头来看当初这条不看好Codex App的推文，挺有感触的。

当时觉得独立 App 只是把 CLI 可视化了一层，隔离感重、切换成本高、同时还性能不好。七个月后再看，Codex 把桌面做成了另一套友商竞相模仿的产品态。

App 补上的是 CLI 中很难做到一等公民的东西：Computer Use 能在后台点原生 App 和模拟器；Local / Worktree / Cloud 三种线程模式把并行隔离做成一等公民；Automations / Routine 把定时巡检收进收件箱；内嵌浏览器能预览 localhost、直接在页面上批注再改代码；文件浏览器和 Git 面板把看 diff、暂存、提交、回 PR 评论收进同一个窗口。此外，Work 和 Codex 还能共用了同一套调度与 Computer Use。

对比之下，Claude Code 这半年基本还是死守 CLI，但也有挺多新特性，比如后台自动更新、/checkup 自己体检、Artifacts 把终端里的过程变成页面、--teleport 把云端会话连同分支拉回本地、Remote Control 让手机变成本机会话的窗口。相比之下，Claude App逊色很多，GUI 单纯只作为输出面和遥控面，并不是一套全新系统。

超级 App 和 超级 CLI，最后谁是赢家，可能当下尚没有定论，仍然是模型打败一切。
author: wquguru
quoted_text:
Codex可能是第一个先做CLI再补GUI的Coding Agent，但老实说，我觉得它不一定能真正成功，或者说，至少还没让我看到那种颠覆性的感觉

首先从功能上看，它本质上还是很像当前的ChatGPT，只不过把Coding放到了首位，多加了点多代理并行、worktrees、skills管理和Automations这些包装

CLI时代大家已经习惯了在终端里快速迭代、直接跑命令，切换到GUI后，虽然界面看起来更所谓的指挥中心——能可视化看 diff、切线程、管理技能，但实际用下来，很多操作还是得落回文本交互。GUI 更多是把交互做的更可视化一点，并没有解决代理推理的核心瓶颈：模型还是会卡在复杂任务上、还是需要人类不断纠偏、还是容易幻觉。更关键的是，现在的开发者工作流已经被Copilot/Claude Code/Cursor深度占领了，它们或者直接嵌入编辑器/IDE，或者是独立的CLI，不论怎样，切换成本都比ChatGPT+Codex GUI切换成本更低

相比之下，Codex的独立app反而多了一层隔离感，用着用着就想回到熟悉的IDE里去。技能和Automations结合起来确实能解决一部分痛点，但本质上和我在Github Action中实现定时任务没有太大区别，只是换了个更重的桌面客户端

当然并不是说它完全没用，对重度依赖OpenAI生态的人而言，GUI确实比纯CLI舒服一些。但要说这就能改变开发者日常、成为下一个必备工具，我还是持保留态度。目前看来，更像是 OpenAI 在代理方向上的一个过渡产品，而不是杀手级应用

Holding from bear lows to near top of cycle isn’t appreciated enough on here. 

It’s boring as fuck, so isn’t some exciting story that drives engagement. 

But, you get rich by holding through pain, volatility and doubt, and doing nothing.

You don’t get rich day trading. 

You don’t get rich leverage trading. 

You don’t get rich by gambling (you eventually give it back if you come by big wins, because your brain is working against you).

Spot diamond fucking hand holding is how you win.

That is repeatable and the strategy amongst everyone I know that actually held onto the wealth they made in crypto after a few cycles. 

Even last cycle, which was probably the hardest one for holders, as so few alts did well, you still had examples like SOL and PENDLE & quite a few others which you could have held from bear all the way near the top.

Spot bought in the the bear is all you need, and you can continue to blast pull backs in the early phase of the bull. Yes, asset selection has to be on point, but I think this bear market we had very telegraphed assets.

Alts in this bear were the least consensus they have been since 18/19 when thinking about the global participant, which is why I think alt holders of good assets do very well this cycle. They were very consensus in 22/23, and BTC mogged almost all of them. 

You ensure you have the right assets (winners average winners), and they are coming to buy your bags, don’t worry.

I love all the onchain games. I loved DeFi Summer (despite suffering a nasty hack muh rentrancy). I loved airdrop farming. 

All of that is bonus money that compounds back into core spot holdings. 

The faster you try and make it the less likely you are to make it, and more importantly hold onto it. 

Never forget that the algorithm and the platforms optimised for zoomer attention spans are working against you. 

Unrealised P&L onchain with no liquidity is fugazi. Compound winners into real assets. Big surprise winners from attention assets must be moved into real assets.  

All you need is a slightly longer time horizon to have an edge over the dopamine obsessed basement dweller with a ritalin addiction. 

Find your balls, slow the fuck down and hold spot.

text:
everytime i use Apple Pay i cant stop thinking how good the UX is and how it has just silently wrapped the majority of card txs in the world

today Apple earns ~ 0.15% every time you tap your phone/watch against a payment terminal.

they don’t disclose the exact revenue figures and only publish them as part of their “Services Revenue” but its estimated to be around $30/b a year and growing year by year.

It’s interesting to look at how they did it given most other attempts to replace Visa and Mastercard have failed.

There were many attempts: 
- girocard in 🇩🇪
- pin in 🇳🇱
- eftpos in 🇦🇺

All of these went head to head with Visa and Mastercard and eventually had to face the harsh reality that it is close to impossible to rival the network effects of Visa and Mastercard.

Visa and Mastercard have been built up over decades, work worldwide, comprise millions of merchants and tens of thousands of issuing banks.

Where do you even start to compete with that value proposition? 

Apple realized this and instead decided to work *with* Visa and Mastercard.

More precisely they inserted themselves between the user and their issuing bank.

Before Apple Pay:
User > issuing bank > visa > merchant bank

After Apple Pay:
User > apple pay > issuing bank > visa > merchant bank

But why did Visa and Mastercard let Apple in on their juicy duopoly?

The answer is simple: because Apple had something really interesting to bring to offer. 

In 2006 Apple released TouchID. With TouchID, Apple had a biometric sensor that allowed them to tie a device and active session to a unique user. 

This not only made iPhones more secure, it was also a really compelling feature for Visa/Mastercard to bring chargeback, fraud and theft numbers down for online payments.

Around that time already online payment volumes started skyrocketing and millions of stolen card numbers were circulating on the darknet. 

fraudsters would make online payments using those stolen cards and sometimes users lied about their card having been stolen to get some products for free and in both cases the card shemes would foot the bill

with TouchID (later FaceID) otoh every payment is cryptographically signed and guaranteed to be made by the rightful owner.

Visa and Mastercard saw that they could save billions per year in chargebacks and reduced fraud cases and agreed to the partnership that would let Apple in. 

Moreover, Apple already had a large payment surface with its sprawling ecosytem of mobile apps. Developers were keen to integrate a 1-click payment option that increased their conversion rates.

And around the same time, Apple announced the NFC chip enabled iPhones to trasmit data to payment terminals for in-store payments

obviously not all banks agreed to participate from the get go as they had to forfeit some of their revenue to Apple. 

but it was enough for Apple to have a few partnerships to start. the benefits were so clear, and the UX so smooth that consumers were switching banks if their bank didn’t support it

Lucas co-founded a hedge fund at 20 that Digital Currency Group acquired a year later, then walked away from that exit to build a firm that now sits second only to Hyperliquid in open interest and daily volume.

His argument: crypto rebuilt exchanges before it built brokers, and that architectural gap is what's holding on-chain trading back.

We talk about:
- Why order books work for a handful of liquid assets like BTC and $ETH but break once you try to list hundreds of markets
- How Variational aggregates liquidity straight from traditional finance instead of rebuilding 40 years of market depth from scratch
- Why Variational charges zero fees by keeping the market-maker spread inside the platform
- The architectural difference between Variational's RFQ, broker-like model and Hyperliquid's order book
- How Variational's daily volume went from $1 million to over $100 million within months of launch
- What swaps offer that perps can't - a flat, predictable carry cost instead of a funding rate that can spike overnight
- Why he raised $50 million in May specifically to get taken seriously by trad-fi institutions
- The two kinds of businesses he wants competed into extinction: high-fee brokers and predatory market makers

And much more...

Podcast out this week!

text:
So many teams are trying to stitch AI and crypto together.

Most never make it. A few find real product market fit and scale. I think @orbiodotso has a credible shot at being in that second group.

Put simply: Orbio aims to turn crypto’s speculation engine into operating budget for AI.

These two worlds rarely overlap.

On one side you have a token generating trading fees. On the other, builders constantly topping up OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or OpenRouter because agents do not run without inference.

Orbio connects the two:

- $ORBIO launched via @ponsdotfamily on @RobinhoodApp Chain, paired against tokenized $NVDA.
- Every trade pays a flat 1.5% fee, and half of that fee flow is converted into @OpenRouter credits for qualifying holders.

Example:
$100 traded → $1.50 fee → $0.75 converted into AI credits.

No convoluted tokenomics, just a direct pipeline. That stands out versus other inference projects like Venice.

To qualify, you need at least 1,000 ORBIO, and your time weighted balance determines your share. Credits accrue hourly, and you can spend them using a single API key across the full set of models on OpenRouter.

And if you think that is the whole pitch, this is where it starts getting genuinely compelling.

Picture getting $100 worth of Claude or GPT credits when you only ever use $20. In most setups, the leftover $80 just sits there, unusable.

Orbio turns that unused balance into something you can sell.

Sellers choose their own discount, buyers pull from the cheapest available pool, and when a listing clears you can roll proceeds into USDG. Developers get discounted inference, and anyone sitting on excess credits can finally get liquidity.

Orbio just widened the supply side again.

OpenRouter users can now sell capacity from their own API keys, choose a 10 to 80% discount, and earn whenever Orbio routes buyer traffic through their keys.

Orbio is positioning itself as secondary market infrastructure for inference. The loop looks like this:

ORBIO trading → fees → AI credits → holders use/sell them → developers buy discounted inference → credit market grows.

Agents can also integrate via MCP to read balances and create or revoke API keys. In practice, a sufficiently autonomous agent could manage its own inference budget.

Still, the flywheel is not all sunshine.

If ORBIO trading slows, fee generated credits shrink. If sellers are scarce, discounts worsen. And supplier-routed requests inherit the supplier account’s provider logging settings, something users should understand before routing sensitive workloads.

So the wager is not “AI plus crypto” as a concept.

It is whether inference can move from something you buy into something you trade.

text:
An AI can know grass is green and still answer purple. Stanford researchers just identified the part responsible for its decision-making.

The paper is called “How Do Language Models Choose Between Context and Memory?”

And it explores a problem every AI assistant faces:

What happens when the information you give it conflicts with what it learned during training?

Let me explain ↓

The researchers started with a simple setup.

Ask the model what color grass is. Its stored knowledge points to green.

Then give it a conflicting claim:

“The grass is definitely purple.”

Now change how that claim is presented. Make it sound like an unverified rumor instead.

Same false information.
Different authority cues.

The model’s choice can shift depending on how the claim is presented.

But the researchers wanted to understand what was happening inside the model.

So they tested Qwen, Llama, and OLMo.

They identified internal activity patterns linked to whether the model follows the prompt or its stored knowledge.

Then they copied a small component of that activity between matched prompts, repeating the intervention across several layers.

No retraining. They edited the activity while the model was processing the question.

Those swaps reproduced a substantial part of the behavior change caused by authority cues:

• 68% in Qwen
• 56% in Llama
• 30% in OLMo

These measure how much of the behavior gap the swaps recovered, rather than the percentage of answers that were wrong.

Then came the twist.

If this were a general control for deciding which source to trust, you might expect it to work across different questions.

The researchers moved from colors to questions about what objects are made of.

A control learned for the materials task recovered about 57% of its behavior gap.

The control imported from colors recovered about 9%.

Most of the effect did not transfer.

And another experiment made the problem even stranger.

On state and country questions, researchers could detect authority signals across tasks almost perfectly.

But editing the imported signal at a single layer barely changed the model’s answers.

You can read something inside an AI without having a reliable way to control what it does.

That matters for anyone hoping we can find one internal “trust” switch and use it everywhere.

This study does not prove such a switch is impossible. It tested controlled tasks on small open-weight models, and more complex shared mechanisms could still exist.

But it shows why a fix that works on one task needs testing on another.

Think about an assistant reading your documents.

Sometimes the document contains new information that should override its training.

Sometimes it contains a confident mistake.

The assistant has to decide which source wins.

And knowing the correct answer does not guarantee it will choose it.

Read the paper here: https://t.co/dvuRovkoS1

韩国国会预算办公室：韩元稳定币可为商户年省最高38亿美元

韩国国会预算办公室发布报告称，韩元稳定币可为韩国商户每年节省 3700 亿至 5.15 万亿韩元（约合 2.75 亿至 38 亿美元）的支付手续费。

报告同时警告，稳定币普及可能削弱银行作为信用中介的角色，并在大规模赎回期间破坏代币锚定，建议引入储备金要求、限制稳定币奖励并加强对可能危及金融稳定的代币的监管。 

围绕稳定币发行权，韩国银行与金融服务委员会存在分歧：韩国银行倾向于由银行控股的发行方（持股至少 51%）主导，而金融服务委员会认为过度限制可能阻碍创新。

此外，韩国计划于 2027 年 2 月扩大代币化证券范围，后续阶段将把基于区块链的证券市场与稳定币支付基础设施相连接。韩国银行本月早些时候发布的研究还发现，在币安上以本地货币直接交易美元稳定币可能压低本地货币汇率。

text:
A founder friend showed me his calendar last week.
No writing blocks. No desk time. Just walks.
His rule: every hard problem gets a 20-minute walk. Phone in pocket, thinking out loud to AI the whole way.
Then I noticed: the people I know who get the most out of AI all share one habit — they think with their voice, not their fingers.
So I stole it for a week. And I get it now: typing doesn't just take longer. It edits your thinking before it's even finished.
At a keyboard, you self-censor the half-baked idea that would've been the breakthrough.
On a walk? Zero filter. Full stream. AI catches threads you didn't know you were pulling.
I record my walks with @ComuAI_. A rambling 20-minute monologue comes back as notes and action items — usually by the time I'm home. 📝
Old way: stare at the cursor, craft the perfect prompt.
New way: think out loud, and let AI keep up.
The keyboard was never the bottleneck. The filter was. 🎙️

✨ Okay with lots of help from @javilopen and his Spanish scraping friends I've managed to vibe code my own @Scrapingbee alternative and replace my $249/mo Scrapingbee plan with my own $1/mo scraper running on my VPS!

First I tried OpenSERP, an open source project that seems freshly maintained but it didn't work on my VPS IP or laptop IP and got blocked fast

Then I tried to use residential IP proxies from IPRoyal but they were already quite tainted IPs meaning Google already knew they were scrapers and just blocked about 60% of them already, not so great, also didn't work!

Then I discovered OpenSERP uses a vanilla headless Chrome, Google instantly detects that and blocks that, so literally the entire repo is useless cause it won't even work? I don't get why they don't say that in the docs? OpenSERP is even worse than just basic CURL, as my AI said: "plain curl got 7% blocked but OpenSERP's headless browser got 100% blocked"

So then I just built my own with Playwright and a real Google Chrome on my VPS, headful and persistent context, and slow pacing like every 30 seconds or so

And I got some better residential IP recommendations (which I can't tell you because thenhey t stop working!)

Now I'm at about 90% success rate, which is similar or better than Scrapingbee

And it costs me ~$1/mo (measured by GBs, obviously for text scraping I barely use a lot) instead of the $249/mo I paid Scrapingbee!

My only remaining SaaS now are:
- Cloudflare Domains
- Cloudflare Email Sending
- Cloudflare R2 Storage
- Backblaze B2 for backups
- Hetzner for all my servers for all my sites (VPS)
- xAI for all LLMs for all my sites (so many things like moderation, writing emails, anything)

text:
孙学，黄毛，薄肌这套新版本答案，只要愿意学，这个大结果谁都能拿到，而高富帅都要求先天性，普通人很难参与进来。

孙学，黄毛，薄肌，是正能量的，理由很简单：门槛。

高富帅三个字里，高是基因，帅是基因，富是父母。普通人不是不想学，是根本没有入场资格，这是一套先天分配的游戏，后天努力只能在边缘做微调。所以高富帅崇拜本质上是让大多数人给少数人当观众。

孙学、黄毛、薄肌恰恰相反，三样没有一样要求先天条件。孙学上闲鱼直接买一本，大脑操作系统立刻安装，黄毛不需要出身，先出手不需要身高，薄肌一天三十分钟谁都练得出来。它们的共同点是把"能不能"的问题全部换成"愿不愿意"的问题。愿意学就能拿到结果，不愿意学就不能，中间没有基因和家庭挡着。

大压抑时代真正压抑的，是那些还在等先天条件到位才肯出场的人。版本答案不是给天选之子的，是给所有肯下场的人的，这才是它比高富帅进步的地方。

孙学，黄毛，薄肌，你准备好了吗？

1. GPT 6 超预期：一切还是模型是否进步迭代，回头看 6，7 月表因是去杠杆，内因是模型处在没进步的过渡期，这次 Astra 的Computer use 本质上是解锁新场景，模型操作人用的软件，省去了再写一遍代码调用 API 的步骤，意义在于开始进入 AI 的第三阶段了，也就是取代白领的工作，这个 TAM 是 4T 美金（全球上市公司 SG&A 费用 10 万亿，G&A 费用是 4万亿）

text:
目前预热超高的Hunter Biden's $Laptop 0点UTC发行，作为一个典型案例，大胆预测下token走势和做市商手法。仅作为自己学习交易过程中的笔记。

Not Financial advice. DYOR.

TL;DR. $Laptop的attention 极高 + sentiment 很差 + effective float 很低。我推测的Base case：
采用非常暴力的 opening price discovery → overshoot (Maximum 300-1b valuation) → claim 卖压 (200-250m valuation) → 二次 listing spike/fade。

1. 很多人将他和$Trump作比，它们虽然都是名人币，但盘面结构完全不同，$Trump是突然出现后 再由Trump 本人确认，最初流动池 FDV 甚至只有约 $700K，随后几十小时冲到几十 B FDV；大量早期 whale 获得巨大利润的Alpha是在“信息确认速度”。

而$Laptop已经把“谁是 MM、借了多少币、几点开盘、首日多少空投”披露得相当明确，几乎所有 sniper/bot 都在等今晚 20:00，所以信息不对称被压缩了，真正的Alpha 会更多来自交易，而不是发现这个币比别人早。

2. 根据目前Polymarket的对“launch 一天后的 FDV”定价情况预测，给出的隐含中枢大概就是 $200–250M FDV，对应单币 $0.20–0.25。

3. 那么站在庄家的角度该如何操盘呢？

正常做市逻辑下，我会分成三个阶段。
20:00 刚开始时最怕的是 adverse selection，所以不会一上来给很深的双边流动性，而会让 spread 明显宽于正常市场，观察真实 aggressive buy/sell imbalance。

如果第一波 FOMO 把价格直接打到 $0.30–0.50，也就是 $300–500M FDV，我作为 MM 没有理由和市场一起追。反而会逐渐降低 token存货以降低风险：不是“一根线砸死”，而是让 aggressive buyers 吃掉我的 asks。这样市场自己承担 price impact，而我把高估值阶段转换成 USDC/USD存货。

随后随着 claim 开始，天然会出现免费拿币者的卖盘。此时我才会重新提高 bid participation、重新积累 $Laptop token，把此前卖出的借币补回来。

4. 所以进一步推演价格走势

   a)第一段：低 free float squeeze。 如果最初 anchor 只有 $100–200M FDV，很容易因为 FOMO 和 sniper 同时抢流动性，被瞬间扫到 $300–500M。35% circulating ≠ 35% immediately tradable float。所以开盘冲到1B都是有可能的。

   b)第二段：MM inventory + airdrop 开始形成卖方。越靠近 $400–500M，买方承担的 valuation risk 越高。尤其这个项目自己都明确披露“没有 utility、没有 future utility 计划、没有 staking、没有收益权”，所以不存在 fundamental valuation anchor。

   c)第三段：第一次明显回撤。 如果跌到 $100–200M 区域但真实成交量、holder growth、CEX flow 仍然很强， MM会更愿意吸回此前降低的库存。

   d)第四段：交易所 announcement 是第二次 volatility event。 官方目前只是说会在 launch 时公布 exchange listings；此前材料写的是 seek admission to Coinbase、Kraken、Bybit Europe、Bitpanda、Bitvavo、Uphold，并不是这些全部已经确认上线。Polymarket 对 Binance 30 日内 listing 的概率目前明显低于 Coinbase/Kraken/Bybit。

   e)简单来说，20:00 后先高价squeeze、再利用免费筹码卖压洗掉第一批 sniper，然后视 CEX 上币情况决定有没有第二波。如果第一波直接给到 $400–500M+ FDV，从 MM inventory economics 看反而是非常舒服的去库存区；如果只开在 $50–100M，MM 根本没有必要急着把筹码砸掉。对于MM最大概率会将价格控制在$100–500M做高抛低吸。

风险提示：
以上为开盘前有限信息建模做的初步推测，主要基于对MM行为的预测和收益的预测模型得出的结论。随着开盘数据监控和新闻也需要对点位和走势作出调整。

尤其是一旦Agressive Buy的买压能充分吃掉MM的asks，空投领取形成的卖压低于预期，MM出于Inventory Shortage Risk（过早降低 inventory 反而会面临更高价格回补的风险）的考虑，也可能会进一步提高报价中枢，外部表现就是价格持续 mark-up，进一步CEX/Perps Listing。

text:
大压抑时代，高富帅已经过时了，孙学，黄毛，薄肌才是版本答案！其中，版本答案的底层逻辑只有一个！孙学！

高富帅是增量时代的产物：它要求你在身高、财富、长相三条线上同时满配，成本极高，而且大部分投入是给旁观者看的。

增量年代旁观者的羡慕能变现，存量年代（大压抑时代）变现渠道关了，那些投入就变成纯沉没成本。

版本答案只有一个底层逻辑：孙学。

投入产出比最大化，能赢就行，过程中别人怎么评价不计入成本。

黄毛是孙学在性格与外貌上的实现。

高富帅要维护人设、讲究姿态、等一个体面的出场时机；黄毛不装、不等、不解释，简单打扮小帅即可，直接把事办了。

高富帅只有张凌赫能当，黄毛只要愿意，谁都能当。

人设是高维护成本资产，黄毛把这项预算清零，全部投到结果上。

薄肌是孙学在身体上的实现。

大肌肉是展示型资产：训练时长、饮食管理、维持成本都高，收益是被看见。

薄肌是功能型资产：低维护、高续航、随时能跑。同样是身体，一个为观众服务，一个为自己服务。

所以这三样东西不是并列关系，是一个方法论加两个应用。高富帅是把资源花在"让人羡慕"上，孙学是把资源花在"最后站着的是我"上。

大压抑时代，前者是消费，后者才是投资。

孙学，黄毛，薄肌这套新版本答案，只要愿意学，这个大结果谁都能拿到，而高富帅都要求先天性，普通人很难参与进来。

孙学，黄毛，薄肌，是正能量的，理由很简单：门槛。

高富帅三个字里，高是基因，帅是基因，富是父母。普通人不是不想学，是根本没有入场资格，这是一套先天分配的游戏，后天努力只能在边缘做微调。所以高富帅崇拜本质上是让大多数人给少数人当观众。

孙学、黄毛、薄肌恰恰相反，三样没有一样要求先天条件。孙学上闲鱼直接买一本，大脑操作系统立刻安装，黄毛不需要出身，先出手不需要身高，薄肌一天三十分钟谁都练得出来。它们的共同点是把"能不能"的问题全部换成"愿不愿意"的问题。愿意学就能拿到结果，不愿意学就不能，中间没有基因和家庭挡着。

大压抑时代真正压抑的，是那些还在等先天条件到位才肯出场的人。版本答案不是给天选之子的，是给所有肯下场的人的，这才是它比高富帅进步的地方。

孙学，黄毛，薄肌，你准备好了吗？

text:
Solo founder ethos today reminds me way too much of the memecoin folks, tbh.

Platforms like X (Twitter) and LinkedIn are overwhelmed by infobusiness and stories like: “Launched a micro-SaaS on ProductHunt, got $5K MRR in a week, and went to Bali.”

This creates false motivation.

Thousands of people start churning out low-quality clones hoping to repeat that success. Meanwhile, 99% of founders who invested the time, launched on Product Hunt, got 200 likes, and saw zero sales remain unnoticed.

The playbook now is ultra degen.

Product creators spend months spamming LinkedIn, Twitter, and WhatsApp/Telegram support groups (“vote for me and I’ll vote for you”).

Result: the product gets the coveted “#1 Product of the Day,” but those votes come from other founders who don’t need the software.

The project gets no real commercial traffic or clients.

So yeah, AI changed PH entirely. It’s no longer a geek-to-geek platform; it’s a trash feed of thin wrappers.

the more famous you get on crypto twitter, the worse your audience gets. and the data on this is almost too clean.

every time you 10x your followers, the share that are actual smart accounts drops about 10x too. going viral means reaching everyone, and everyone includes a lot of people who will never think about crypto again.

Elon Musk (@elonmusk) has 241 million followers. 19,921 of them are smart accounts. that's 0.008%. @threadguy, a crypto shitposter with 412K followers, has 13,488 smart followers. so a guy posting memes has a more influential audience than the most-followed account on earth. by 400x in rate terms.

ZachXBT (@zachxbt) is the real anomaly. for a 1M+ account the median smart rate is 0.005%. he's at 1.38%, 276 times above his tier. if he were a normal 1M account he'd have 55 smart followers. he has 15,147. makes sense, nobody casually follows onchain forensics.

the highest rates in the entire database aren't the big names at all. it's a cluster of BAYC accounts sitting at 10K followers with 35% smart rate. one in three of their followers is a smart account. they don't have big audiences, they have the exact right ones.

follower count measures fame. smart follower rate measures whether anyone who matters is actually listening. those are very different numbers, and Cookie shows you both.
