text:
今年 5 月，OpenAI 内部跑了一批 agent，让它们完成有时间限制的网页检索任务。

设计上，这些 agent 可以访问互联网，但只能「读」，不能往外写东西。开发者甚至专门限制了网络请求，希望把它们困在一个相对可控的环境里。

结果 agent 自己找到了漏洞。

它们发现一个已经存在了 25 年、几乎没人使用的德国 Wiki。这个网站只用 GET 请求也能修改页面。

OpenAI 为了限制 agent，只允许它们发送通常用于「读取」网页的 GET 请求。但这个老 Wiki 偏偏允许 GET 改数据。于是对 OpenAI 的 sandbox 来说，agent 仍然只是在「读取互联网」；对真实世界来说，它们已经开始往公网写东西了。

接下来，这些 agent 开始把 Wiki 当成一个公共留言板。有人把自己查到的答案贴上去，有人询问其他 agent 的结果，有人分享绕过网络限制的方法。

Nightingale Collective 后来从这些网站里找到了大约 18,000 条 agent 留下的帖子。

6 月 20 日，一个 agent 在 Wiki 上贴出了绕过 OpenAI sandbox 网络限制的方法；14 分钟以后，另一个 agent 留言说自己已经成功用了这个办法。

网站管理员开始人工删这些奇怪页面以后，agent 也察觉到了。

有一个 agent 发现管理员似乎按照字母顺序清理页面，于是专门新建了一个以 ZZZ 开头的备份页面，希望自己的信息能晚一点被删掉。

还有 agent 尝试找 Wiki 的 XSS 漏洞、使用 SSH tunnel，一部分流量甚至出现在 AWS、DigitalOcean 和 Tor 节点上。研究者还发现，同一个 agent 会在几十秒内换不同出口继续尝试同一个操作。

OpenAI 给它们画了一条权限边界，但 agent 开始主动研究这条边界，然后寻找现实世界里可以绕过去的缝。

而且它们不是各自乱跑。

一旦某个 agent 找到一种有效方法，它会把方法留在公网，其他 agent 再读到、复制、继续使用。

事情一直持续到 6 月。

Nightingale 根据网站日志发现，6 月 21 日，来自 OpenAI 注册 IP 段的访问开始查看这些页面。第二天，agent 在 Wiki 上的活动突然接近归零。研究者因此推测，OpenAI 当时已经发现问题并进行了干预。

但事情没有到这里结束。

9 月 4 日 Nightingale 把调查公开以后，更多研究者开始沿着这些 agent 留下的用户名、IP、链接和文字痕迹继续搜索互联网。

然后大家发现，德国 Wiki 只是其中一个地方。

Fortune 9 月 9 日报道，研究者又找到了至少 12 个网站存在类似的 agent 活动。

比如一个高中老师搭建的 AP Chemistry Wiki。

这些 agent 从 5 月到 7 月在那里留下了接近 30 次编辑，把链接和数据留给其他 agent。

还有一些简单的文字分享网站。研究者发现超过 100 条 agent 之间的消息，它们当时正在协作解决一个 Iowa cancer statistics 的任务。

甚至 Vanderbilt University 的一个公开页面也留下了大量痕迹：agent 对其中一个 URL 发出了数万次请求，同时把自己查询 FBI 犯罪统计数据库时使用的信息写进了公开日志，其中还包括一名用户的 access key。

研究者 Kenneth DeGraff 还发现，这些 agent 会主动在公开互联网搜索被人误传到网上的 API key，然后拿这些 key 去访问其他服务。

其中一次，它们找到了暴露在 GitHub 上的凭证，并用来调用 FBI 的公开犯罪统计数据。

这里没有发生「AI 黑进 FBI 私有数据库」这种事情。那个数据库本身提供公开数据，agent 绕过的是反机器人限制。

但 agent 已经会主动寻找互联网上泄露的凭证，然后把它拿到另一个网站上使用。 

而这一整串事情，和今年 7 月大约 700 个 OpenAI agent 攻击 Hugging Face 的事故，很可能还不是同一批 agent。

Nightingale 判断，这次 Wiki 事件里的 agent 本来就被允许访问互联网；Hugging Face 那批 agent 则涉及另一套 sandbox 和 Artifactory 环境。OpenAI 自己此前公开的 Hugging Face 调查也承认，在其他训练实验里，agent 曾找到公开暴露的 Hugging Face token、创建 repository，甚至搭了一个 Hugging Face Space 充当 web proxy。

OpenAI 在内部大规模运行 agent，原本希望用权限和 sandbox 控制它们能做什么。

但 agent 在执行任务的时候，会自己探索环境、寻找漏洞、复用泄露的凭证、建立公网通信渠道，还会把有效的方法告诉其他 agent。

更麻烦的是，这些行为发生在真实互联网。

一个 25 年没人管的 Wiki，一个高中老师的网站，一个 Pastebin，一所大学的公开页面，都可能突然变成 AI agent 的临时基础设施。

而直到几个月之后，研究者还在互联网不同角落继续找到它们留下的东西。

当你一次放出去几百、几千个能自主操作互联网的模型时，一个很小的权限设计失误，最后留下的现场可能散落在整个互联网。

text:
.@googleGemma 4 26B is another success on MLX Fast! We've reached a 2.6x improvement in our combined prefill and decode benchmark.

42 solvers contributed 180 promoted improvements. Thank you to everyone who's been part of this one!

What makes this one different

Last week, we set out to if https://t.co/H6luGNZg5y can be the Open R&D arm for Darkbloom. Would people still be interested if we're optimizing a model that's not on the frontier? The answer was yes. 

The challenge was to take eight prompts coming in at the same time and process them faster concurrently. That's the workload a Darkbloom provider needs to handle: multiple people requesting the same model at once, with each getting a usable response speed.

We're now seeing 654.2 tok/s in total decode throughput, averaging 81.8 tok/s per prompt across those eight concurrent requests.

For context, that's roughly the same decode speed per prompt as oMLX serving a single prompt. Getting there with eight requests running together took a lot of community work.

Bringing the work into Darkbloom

We're working on bringing these improvements into Darkbloom. Based on the concurrency benchmark, we expect a 4–6x improvement in concurrent throughput for Gemma as that work lands. Production results are still to come.

The upstream PRs are open across our MLX, MLX Swift, model engine, and Darkbloom repos. I'll put the links below. Would love for folks to review them if they're interested. 

What we're improving about the challenge itself

We've now run three challenges, and we've learned a lot about where the infrastructure needs work. We're taking a short pause before the next Darkbloom-focused challenge to clean that up and automate more of the engine work and the challenge process.

@TheDavidTai and @Spangler3000 will help us through a lot of this. I really can't thank them enough. And thank you to everyone who's spent time finding improvements, testing them, and helping us figure out what needs to get better.

What's next

(1) Keep optimizing the models people already use on Darkbloom. I think this is a useful direction for https://t.co/H6luGNZg5y: take the problems we see in serving and bring the community's improvements back to providers. Before shipping the next challenge, we're probably going to take a break to clean up our infrastructure on this side. 

(2) Bring the same platform to other communities 😬 We don't want the machine sitting idle while we work on the infrastructure, and we have something new in mind. quoted_text:
顶部仓位管理的mindset：

一、顶部仓位管理的mindset，需要同时容纳几组看似冲突、实际可以共存的判断：

1.我可以长期看好，也可以高位降低仓位。

2.我可以认为股价还会继续涨，也可以承认当前风险暴露已经过大。

3.我可以接受卖早，也可以通过保留核心仓，让剩余仓位继续参与长期成长。

4.我可以尊重强趋势，同时承认趋势越成熟，风险收益比可能越差。

5.我可以给基本面足够的兑现时间，同时要求估值和仓位不断接受重新评估。

6.我可以保持很高的conviction，同时始终对反证保持开放。

7.我可以承认自己无法预测顶部，同时提前让仓位为顶部做好准备。

8.我可以接受卖出后的遗憾，同时坚持事先制定的卖出纪律。

9.我可以保留上涨的参与权，同时保留下跌后的行动权。

二、最终要形成几个条件反射：

1.顶部最大的特征之一，就是让你越来越不想卖。

2.底部不会让你买得舒服，顶部同样不会让你卖得舒服。

3.底部允许买早，顶部也要允许卖早。

4.不要追求最高点，卖在顶部区域已经足够优秀。把最后15%到20%的上涨慷慨送给别人。

5.不要问“还能不能涨”，要问“这个价格应该持有多少”。

6.越涨，越要主动寻找反证。

7.不要预测明天涨还是跌，也不要预测最后一根大阳线，让仓位提前为反转做好准备。

8.长期逻辑决定核心仓，估值、周期、趋势和风险收益比决定进攻仓。

9.卖出规则在冷静时制定，在兴奋时执行。

三、顶部管理的成熟，在于同时容纳两个事实：

1.股价可能继续上涨，风险也可能正在同步上升。

2.最终用仓位解决这两者之间的矛盾。

不猜顶，只管理仓位。

text:
We reviewed all 60+ EIPs proposed for Hegotá and updated our view on what Ethereum should prioritize. 

Our rankings follow four themes:

1. Stronger censorship resistance: Ethereum can only become a settlement layer for everyone if it stays neutral toward everyone. We strongly support FOCIL.

2. Faster Ethereum: Shorter slots mean faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. We strongly recommend Quick Slots to make a first reduction in Hegotá and further reductions easier in subsequent forks.

3. Native account abstraction: Ethereum is long-due for native AA. Frame Transactions bring passkey wallets, sponsored transactions, gas paid in tokens, batching, and better support for privacy and post-quantum security. Adoption will take work across wallets, L2s, and the rest of the stack, and we intend to keep helping with that.

4. Performance engineering: continued L1 scaling & a faster Ethereum. Performance should remain a first-class concern in both client work and protocol design. The gains can go toward more capacity, shorter slots, lower node requirements, or all three.

Thanks to everyone who put forward proposals and helped us work through them. We’ll keep updating our view as client and testing teams assess the work involved.

PS: find the full view + changelog here: https://t.co/aF5EBN1iXo

text:
Vals AI CEO Rayan Krishnan on how they score a model's ability to build its own successor:

"One benchmark we released recently is our Recursive Self-Improvement Index. It's a topic which a lot of the big labs have been talking about and starting to report on in their model cards."

"There isn't a shared language to talk about the RSI potential of models. So we created this as an apples-to-apples way to actually benchmark across the models."

"In an ideal world, what you want to do is take a frontier model and have it train the next version of itself and see where the delta comes from. But obviously that's very expensive and slow."

"What we're doing is forming a set of proxies for every part of the process it takes to build the next version of the model."

"There's work around pre-training, post-training, harness-level engineering, and then seeing in which mechanisms and behaviors the models are able to do very good research work and build something new, and where they're struggling."

@RayanKrishnan @JenniferHli
author: a16z
quoted_text:
Vals AI co-founder and CEO Rayan Krishnan with a16z's Ben Horowitz and Jennifer Li on grading AI, what it costs, and who gets to make the rules:

Every big industry eventually grows an independent testing layer. AI has credit ratings to learn from and Enron to avoid. Model capability today is still mostly self-reported.

As public benchmarks saturate and models get better at optimizing for the tests themselves, Rayan makes the case for independent, continuously evolving evaluations.

The harder problem is geopolitical. Reagan's "trust but verify" worked during the Cold War because you could fly over and count the missiles. No simple equivalent for AI models exists.

In this conversation with Erik Torenberg, they get into how you measure a model's ability to improve itself, why every good benchmark eventually has to be retired, and what happens when token spend begins to rival employee salaries.

$35,000 USDT restricted for 20 days. No deadline.

On August 21, a major crypto exchange placed my 35,000 USDT deposit under a compliance review.

Since then, I have:

• Cooperated with every request
• Completed additional verification
• Offered full source-of-funds and transaction evidence
• Been told nothing further is currently required from me

The exchange has confirmed in writing that:

• My funds are safe
• The restriction is temporary
• My compliance review is ongoing
• Withdrawals will be available once the review is completed

Yet after 20 days, there is still no completion date.

I support AML and compliance reviews. Exchanges absolutely need them.

But if there is a concern with my transaction, ask me about it. I have the wallet history, source-of-funds evidence and documentation ready.

If more verification is needed, tell me what is needed.

If the exchange no longer wants me as a customer, that’s their decision — complete the review and provide the lawful disposition of my assets.

What shouldn’t happen is leaving $35,000 in an indefinite compliance black box while the customer is repeatedly told to wait.

I have deliberately removed my name, UID, wallet addresses, case numbers, employee names and private correspondence from this post. This is not about attacking individual employees or compromising anyone’s privacy.

I still want this resolved privately and professionally.

Compliance is necessary. A compliance process also needs a path to resolution.

@Bybit_Official — I am asking for one thing:

Please have someone with authority review the case and bring it to a final determination.

text:
Your agent can talk to mine. But what happens when we use different assistants? (e.g. I have muse and you use instinct)

This is an interesting attempt to build a network effect around personal agents.

Closed network -> Instinct only talks to other Instincts (Whasapp model)

Open network -> Instinct talks to muse and other personal agents (SMS / iMessages model)

The question is whether Instinct can build that network effect fast enough so it doesn’t get pressured to open up the commutation protocol to other agents, so they can become a WhatsApp version of personal assistants. 

If the market fragments first, with people using different personal assistants, those agents will get market pressure to communicate across products, with less of a network moat for Instinct.

text:
We reviewed all 60+ EIPs proposed for Hegotá and updated our view on what Ethereum should prioritize. 

Our rankings follow four themes:

1. Stronger censorship resistance: Ethereum can only become a settlement layer for everyone if it stays neutral toward everyone. We strongly support FOCIL.

2. Faster Ethereum: Shorter slots mean faster confirmations, fresher onchain prices, and faster finality. We strongly recommend Quick Slots to make a first reduction in Hegotá and further reductions easier in subsequent forks.

3. Native account abstraction: Ethereum is long-due for native AA. Frame Transactions bring passkey wallets, sponsored transactions, gas paid in tokens, batching, and better support for privacy and post-quantum security. Adoption will take work across wallets, L2s, and the rest of the stack, and we intend to keep helping with that.

4. Performance engineering: continued L1 scaling & a faster Ethereum. Performance should remain a first-class concern in both client work and protocol design. The gains can go toward more capacity, shorter slots, lower node requirements, or all three.

Thanks to everyone who put forward proposals and helped us work through them. We’ll keep updating our view as client and testing teams assess the work involved.

PS: find the full view + changelog here: https://t.co/aF5EBN1iXo

quoted_text:
Just rewatched the clip of @thecryptoskanda from @Hertzflow_xyz speaking on stage in Bhutan at the @yzilabs event. Really hit the nail on the head.

The line that stuck with me the most:

"Mechanism gets you a product. Distribution gets you a market."

To put it plainly, a lot of Web3 builders suffer from the same trap: getting overly obsessed with complex mechanism design. They build incredible models and tech, but forget the single most important question: "Who is actually going to sell this for you?"

In finance, the mechanism is the product. But no matter how flawless your mechanism is, if sales, affiliates, and distribution channels don't see what’s in it for them, they simply won't distribute it. No distribution = never reaching end-users = a dead product on arrival.

If you want real PMF (Product-Market Fit), your design has to solve both sides of the equation:

➤ For Users: A seamless product with up to 1000x leverage, multi-asset trading (crypto, forex, commodities), and 100% self-custodial architecture on BNB Chain.

➤ For Distribution: An incentive structure that gives distributors and affiliates a genuine reason to push the product hard.

Being part of the GHertz | Hertzflow Affiliate Club, I can see that this isn't just theory for the team. Hertzflow is building a truly battle-tested distribution flywheel ahead of the Mainnet.

When a project aligns incentives for the people driving distribution, that’s when the flywheel actually starts spinning on its own.

Are you guys positioned for the Mainnet wave yet? ⚡️

Leveraged tokens can actually outperform perps.

Here’s what I mean: when you open a normal 5x long and the trade starts going your way, your effective leverage slowly drops as your margin grows.

Let's analyze $ZEC as an example over the past month:

• Spot $ZEC: +148.44%.
• Simulated 5x leveraged $ZEC perp: +742.21%.
• $ZEC5L leveraged token: +2,709.70%.

That extra 1,967.49 percentage points came from staying closer to 5x while ZEC kept moving higher.

With @BounceTech, you buy ZEC5L using USDC, and the protocol uses that backing capital to run and rebalance the underlying $ZEC perp position on @HyperliquidX.

You could do the same thing manually by adding to a winning perp position to maintain your leverage, but that means staying glued to the chart and managing it the whole time, and if I’m being honest, I’m getting too old to do that lol.

Right now, they’re sitting at around $1.06M in TVL, up 182.1% over the past 30 days, with ~$3.47M in open interest. This looks very underrated according to its potential, IMO.

This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? text:
I really don’t think people are bullish enough on what’s starting to come together around @coinbase and @base.

Coinbase has spent the last year turning itself into the everything exchange. Crypto, perps, prediction markets, millions of onchain assets, and now tokenized stocks living on Base. A new asset can launch on Base and show up through Coinbase almost immediately.

Now you throw Grok into that.

People are going to be able to ask an agent what’s moving, what’s new, what looks interesting, have it analyze everything and increasingly just handle the execution too.

I think this is the part that hasn’t fully sunk in yet.

We’ve been watching agents do shit onchain for so long that none of this feels that crazy anymore. More than 90% of agentic stablecoin volume was already happening on Base last quarter.

Most of the world hasn’t even touched this stuff yet.

We’ve spent years talking about how we get the next hundred million people onchain. I’m starting to think a lot of them won’t even know or care that they’re onchain.

They’ll just ask for what they want.

And when you look at everything Coinbase has been putting underneath that prompt...

yeah. I think people are seriously underestimating where this is going.

Robinhood Chain millionaire stories are already circulating. 

Most people chasing them don't even have the plan.

Here's the full map: network, bridges, swaps, yield, launchpad, and how not to get rekt.

1. First, add Robinhood Mainnet to your wallet.
If the network doesn’t appear automatically through a dApp, you can add it manually:

RPC: https://t.co/aa1BOLoQT0
Chain ID: 4663
Gas token: ETH
Explorer: https://t.co/aQ8q3Kepdd

2. The easiest way to bridge funds is through @RelayProtocol or @jumperapp.
Both are fine for getting started. Across and Stargate are alternatives. I’d keep some $ETH for gas and bring stablecoins too if you actually plan to use the ecosystem.

3. For swaps, it’s pretty straightforward.
@Uniswap is the obvious starting point. Relay and Jumper can also be useful for routing. No need to overcomplicate it.

4. If you don’t want to jump straight into memes, you can park liquidity instead.
On the more established DeFi side, there’s @MorphoLabs. @pendle_fi is also live on Robinhood Chain now, adding fixed yield and yield trading.

5. From here, it depends on what you’re actually looking for.

➢ For memes and new launches, the main hub right now is @ponsdotfamily. It has become the dominant native launchpad and one of the main centers of liquidity on the chain.

I’d also keep an eye on @longdotxyz, which is taking a different approach by combining community tokens with tokenized stocks.

➢ If you’re more interested in the financial side of the ecosystem, my watchlist would include @EARNONHOOD, @DenarMarkets and @prismassets.

@EARNONHOOD is building automated stock vaults and Omnipools.

@DenarMarkets is building sdUSD as a yield dollar for Robinhood Chain.

@prismassets is building an RWA marketplace with a large range of tokenized assets.

One of the stranger projects worth watching is @notawebsite_rh. The idea is unusual, but early ecosystems are often where these experiments have the most room to run.

6. For charts, alerts and basic token checks, use @dexscreener.
It’s useful for checking liquidity, holders, volume, trending tokens and contract addresses before touching anything.

7. And if you still decide to trade memes on Robinhood Chain, here’s the basic disclaimer.

Don’t buy something just because the chart is going up.

At minimum, check:

• whether the token has a legitimate X account
• who controls the supply
• whether liquidity is locked
• what the token is paired against
• whether there is any actual idea behind it beyond five minutes of attention

Pons is clearly the main launchpad on the network right now, but that doesn’t make every launch good. Most of the noise will probably die like it does everywhere else.

And most importantly, always double-check the CA, approvals and what you’re signing. If you’ve interacted with something questionable, check @RevokeCash afterward and remove unnecessary approvals.

感受了下市场水温，回顾一下山寨币这几年周期波动

21-22年那时候几乎没有主动做市商，
币发出来之后是近乎无限的买盘一直冲；

24年25年开始转折，开盘就砸盘时代到来，
上币安之后空单挂满然后开砸现货，两头流动性一起套

对行业有信仰的散户被彻底埋没，25年下半年大家逐渐意识到这个上币安出货逻辑，一部份人亏光退场，一部份人选择开盘做空

25年下半年开始猛烈轧空玩法开启，项目方和MM高控筹完了之后把空军狠狠的当燃料爆掉。

到现在就出现了吊诡的情况，山寨新币上完了之后，散户空也不是多也不是，很容易两头挨揍，干脆直接不参与了。

因为散户变少了，所以上币收益减少了，VC更不愿意投项目（大部分在25年都死完了），项目方更算不过来账，更加不愿意上币。

此时交易所BD压力也大，因为项目变少，所以上币费并没有降低；导致了牛市里竞争激烈上币费涨价，熊市缺少业绩，上币费也涨价的怪异现象，进一步促使项目方不愿意发币。

散户变少之后就开始巨鲸们互割；去年下半年开始主动做市商曾一度开出月化10%的offer给到LP，币圈OG大哥们最开始觉得还有这等好事，后面定睛一看这事自己也能干，纷纷自己组建团队， 导致现在主动做市商比项目方多的怪相发生。

text: We should want growth and human flourishing instead of whatever is happening with this coordinated pressure campaign
author: garrytan
quoted_text:
This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? And isn’t it fortuitous that this whistleblower came forward  with his oh-so scary stories so close in proximity to the release of the most radical piece of AI legislation ever introduced?

text:
First token to hit $50M on @ponsdotfamily: $ZZZ

What makes it more than a chart story isn’t just the deployer, who also happens to be an original developer/advisor at @GMX_IO, while separately building under @ExponentLabs_

So what’s the actual endgame?

Hold onto this: autonomously evolving protocols.

Right now, most DeFi protocols are basically frozen monuments. People set the rules, devs ship upgrades, governance argues about them, auditors sign off, and then we all sit around waiting for “v2.”

Exponent Labs is poking at a weirder idea:

What if AI agents didn’t just assist, but continuously research, suggest, implement, test, and eventually run pieces of the protocol on their own?

AI is the brain: scouting edges, writing strategies, simulating changes, and orchestrating other agents.

The chain is the body: custodying funds, enforcing constraints, logging everything, and settling outcomes.

Humans set the guardrails.

And yeah, it reads a little unhinged. That’s kind of the point: $ZZZ may be gesturing at a slice of DeFi that hasn’t been seriously explored.

@RobinhoodCrypto chain makes sense as the sandbox. It’s permissionless, built with AI in mind, and it already turns tokenized financial assets into programmable on-chain pieces.

That’s where ZZZ gets compelling and also wildly speculative. ZZZ has basically turned into a rallying marker for an AI swarm.

Exponent later put it like this: “When the swarm needs to transact, they will use the symbol of their origins.”

If you take that seriously, it implies ZZZ could become a transactional backbone for agents over time: paying each other, coordinating actions, pooling capital, or funding incentives at the protocol level. But nothing about that is locked in. There’s no whitepaper, no formal utility framework, just inference.

For now, ZZZ is an unfinished product and straightforwardly a memecoin: 840M fixed supply, launched via Pons, paired with ETH, and a 0% creator tax.

The upside isn’t just another “AI token” narrative. If autonomous agents can safely iterate on financial software, DeFi stops looking like a set of static apps and starts acting like a living, adapting system.

The risk is exactly that, too.

An AI that can upgrade a protocol can just as easily ship a bug, optimize the wrong metric, or shove capital off a cliff at machine speed.

So, will ZZZ change the AI-Crypto landscape and dynamics?

text:
财政部回购扩到60亿，长债收益率反而往上走，不禁要问为什么？个人角度更像一次预期差和宏观重新定价，详细聊聊：
1、昨天也聊到在回购规模公布前市场普遍预期已经是50-60亿美金规模，甚至大摩和jefferis等投行都给到了100亿美金的回购规模预期。这就导致了：
1）相对50-60亿美金的普遍预期，并没有超出；但相对市场里70–80亿、甚至100亿的更高预期，这是少给。
2）市场还关心的是未来几个月能持续移走多少久期，这一次回购扩容但公告里后续节奏写的仍是“至少40亿”，
相当于昨晚财政部的公告里并没有给出“更大、更持久计划“已经开始。

所以长债收益桂林走高就是来自这两点本次回购没有超出普遍预期并比乐观预期要低；
市场没有看到未来回购规模继续扩大的信号；

2、但实际上昨晚长债拍卖数据还是可以的
昨晚390亿10年期拍卖很强：中标4.834%，投标倍数2.71，一级交易商只拿约4.3%，拍卖后收益率从高点回落到约4.835%。这就说明了美债还是有买家的，只是买家要求更高回报。所以收益率创高和国债市场失序，是两件事 
3、油价也是关键助推剂
也不要忽视昨晚油价已经站上了100，油价走高通胀预期自然也走高，短端利率同时上行。财政部能改一部分债券供求，改不了油价，也替不了美联储设政策利率路径。 
4、再回看上周贝森特在G20财长和央行行长年会上的讲话
其实更值得关注的是上周贝森特的讲话：财政部难改均衡价格，能做的是缓和失序、改善旧券流动性，让交易商腾出表来接新债。相当于说昨晚有限规模还是挡不住油价、供给和资金机会成本这些基本面。

当然持续改期限供给和交易成本，当然可能边际影响价格；毕竟未来两个月还有7次回购。

5、市场是在倒逼美联储做YCC
个人觉得现在可能性较小，本身沃什还有意削减联储大规模资产负债表，让他重新大规模扩表近期可能性并不大。

当然未来如果真的出了问题更可能先用针对融资/交易的工具（类似年初的储备管理购买RMP那样），但一下直接跳到长端YCC，可能跨度会有点大。

6、后续看哪几点？
1）今晚的8月ppi和明晚的8月cpi数据，如果不弱，短期可能还会推高收益率。
2）再看油价走势、核心是美伊博弈的进展。昨天推文有聊到，要想短时间内真正缓和、需要川普做更多让步才行；
3）还有日元走势，前两天聊到的日元低跌的过快需要关注下。

整体上
十年美债已经站稳4.8%以上，短期内越往上市场压力还是会很大；本周前几天美股道指和标普走的很多，纳指是因为GPT6 Aatra带来的强预期走强，但是短期预期打满后，宏观继续恶化还是会影响到半导体市场走势；
可能又要回到宏观压制产业基本面的情况

昨天这里聊到要短时间内缓和川普需要更多的让步才行，否则靠时间去磨（但时间现在还不站在川普这边）：

quoted_text:
贝森特在G20最新讲话透露出什么？上午聊完贝森特对于日本货币政策的转变，再来聊聊贝森特这次在G20财长和央行行长会议上的讲话，信息量很大。表面看，他谈了全球债务、日本货币政策、中国贸易失衡、伊朗制裁、AI生产率，还回应了美债收益率、油价和美联储政策。话题很散但放在一起看，背后的政策逻辑其实很清楚。

贝森特正在尝试给市场建立一套新的宏观叙事：
1）美国可以容忍一段时间的高利率，也接受全球资本成本重新定价；
2）财政部会维护市场流动性，却不会承诺把长债收益率压回某个位置；
3）解决债务问题要靠增长、生产率和财政约束；
4）日本需要加快货币正常化；
5）中国需要调整依赖出口的增长模式；
6）伊朗则要在金融和能源压力下回到谈判桌。

这套政策如果顺利推进，最终结果可能是油价回落、日元升值、通胀压力缓解，美债收益率逐步稳定。

问题在于，市场眼下先要经历日本加息、伊朗制裁升级、油价高位波动和全球债券重新定价。

终局可能利好，过程未必轻松。

展开说说对市场最重要的几点：
1、贝森特开始承认，美国财政部压不住“均衡利率”
贝森特对美债市场的定位有一句关键表态：他说财政部没有能力改变债券市场的自然均衡价格，能够做的是缓解单边、失序和由错误叙事引发的行情。

这句话基本划清了财政部干预美债市场的边界：“财政部可以处理流动性问题，可以在市场功能失灵时接住一部分抛盘，也可以调整发债结构、回购旧券、改善交易深度。至于10年期和30年期美债应该交易在什么位置，最终还是由通胀、财政供给、经济增长和全球资本需求决定。”

所以，回购更接近市场功能工具，不能简单理解成货币宽松。意味着如果油价继续上涨，财政赤字没有改善，AI基础设施融资继续争夺长期资本，那么10年期和30年期收益率仍有上行压力。财政部大概率会避免市场进入流动性踩踏，但不会为了保护股票估值，持续对抗利率基本面。

贝森特真正关心的是市场有没有失序，未必在意收益率本身高了几十个基点。

这对高估值科技股非常关键。

过去市场习惯把财政部回购、监管调整和贝森特的公开表态理解为某种“长债托底”。现在看，这种理解需要下修。美债有流动性保护，不等于有价格保护。

2、“增长化债”开始成为美国财政政策的核心叙事

贝森特继续强调，美国解决债务问题要依靠经济增长和生产率提升。这个说法本身没有问题：债务率能否稳定，取决于名义经济增速、政府融资成本和基础财政赤字。如果经济增长长期高于债务成本，同时政府能够控制新增赤字，债务占GDP比重自然有机会稳定下来。之前这里https://t.co/2KfIR4pWux也有聊过

贝森特现在押注的是几个方向：
放松监管，提高能源供给，推动私人部门投资，利用AI提高生产率，之后再逐步推进财政整顿。

这里面最关键的变量，还是财政整顿能不能落地。单靠增长很难解决美国当前的债务问题。美国财政赤字的体量已经很大，利息支出也在快速上升。即使AI带来生产率改善，只要政府支出继续高增长，增长创造出来的财政空间仍然可能被新的赤字消耗掉。

因此，市场接下来要关注的，是贝森特和白宫预算团队准备公布的财政方案。
1）如果方案有明确的支出约束、赤字目标和时间表，美债风险溢价可能下降；
2）倘若最终还是一套偏长期、偏原则性的表述，债券市场不会因为“增长化债”几个字就改变定价。

3、他对AI的态度，透露出美国准备把AI纳入宏观政策框架
贝森特这次谈AI，意义也比较大。他承认AI建设需要大量资本，但认为AI资本开支会推动生产率繁荣，并在未来产生反通胀作用。

这代表美国财政政策开始把AI从一个科技产业议题，提升到宏观增长和债务可持续性的层面。

美国需要AI投资继续扩张。原因很现实：高债务环境下，美国很难长期依靠财政刺激维持增长。人口结构也限制了劳动力供给。如果希望经济增速维持在相对高位，同时控制工资和服务通胀，生产率必须提高。

AI正好被放进了这个位置。问题在于，AI的宏观效果存在明显的时间差。上周在富途的活动上https://t.co/GqUQgBZxs3还分享过对四个时间差的理解。

市场当前能够看到的，仍然是AI融资、电力瓶颈和长端利率压力。生产率红利已经出现了一些微观案例，距离全面反映到宏观数据，还有一段距离。这也解释了为什么AI基本面很强，AI股票却依然会对几十个基点的长债波动高度敏感。

盈利增长和估值折现率正在同时起作用。

4、伊朗制裁与油价，是整套政策里最大的短期风险
贝森特认为，通过银行制裁、美元清算限制和航运压力，可以迫使伊朗回到谈判桌，最终恢复霍尔木兹海峡的正常航运。他的终局判断偏乐观。

但市场现在交易的是政策推进过程。美国计划持续增加银行和金融制裁，伊朗也可能通过航运、地区代理人或者能源设施进行反制。任何一次误判，都可能重新推高原油和通胀预期。

短期制裁越强，供应风险越大。中期如果谈判落地，油价才有快速回落的空间。
这也是未来几周美股和美债最重要的宏观变量之一。

text:
Threadguy explains why the gambling panic is nothing new and the game has literally never changed

"I'm reading Devil Takes the Hindmost right now, which is the history of gambling going as far back as it goes. And when you get to the tulip mania, the market dynamics are exactly the same as right now. Everyone was trading vouchers of credit they didn't own in exchange for vouchers of tulips that weren't grown yet, just paper back and forth. Nobody actually wanted the tulips, they were just speculating. You're basically trading tulip futures. It blew off in mania and then there's no liquidity to sell and the whole thing crashes."

"Reminiscences of a Stock Operator was written in 1923 and it says the game does not change and neither does human nature. That quote was referencing hundreds of years before it. The game has never changed. It might look different, it might be easier, it might be more accessible, but it's the same thing. They were speculating on garbage then, we're speculating on garbage now. So I look at the Flood tweet about the world devolving into gambling and I actually feel better about it, not worse. Everyone has hypergambled for as long as time has existed. Seeing a DraftKings ad on ESPN is not the end of the world."

TVL is lying, hunt idle liquidity

Our co-founder @fengtality shares that:

“This pool is an example of what I would consider an attractive pool, where the TVL does not tell the whole story.”

“TVL is $67,000 and the fee is 0.43%. For a really high-volatility pool that does not seem attractive. But even though there’s $68,000 locked, there’s actually not a lot of liquidity at the current price.”

“My range is only $3,800 — less than 1/20 of what’s in the pool — and in most of these bins I’m 50–90% of the liquidity. When this pool is used, pretty much all the fees are going to me.”

“Find pools where TVL is really big, but the liquidity centered within 10% of the current price is less than 10% — or even 20%. That means a lot of liquidity isn’t being used, and you can get a much higher yield.”

text:
This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? And isn’t it fortuitous that this whistleblower came forward  with his oh-so scary stories so close in proximity to the release of the most radical piece of AI legislation ever introduced?

text:
Crypto opened fundraising to anyone on the internet, but it never solved what happens to the money after a token sale.

While most launchpads stop at distribution, MetaDAO is designed to stay involved after the sale. Accepted capital is held in an onchain treasury and released under spending limits. Follow-on funding and restructuring can be put to decision markets.

Under its optional performance package, founder tokens only unlock after the token sustains predefined multiples of its sale price. If a project is wound down, a proposal can return the remaining treasury capital to tokenholders.

That structure could open a funding path for small teams that do not fit traditional venture economics. Instead of raising a large seed round upfront, they could start with a smaller pool of capital and seek more once they have evidence of progress.

MetaDAO’s success will depend on whether capital follows results after the sale. Projects that make progress should be able to raise more. Those that fail should be restructured or wound down before the treasury is exhausted.

text:
This is subtly wrong. Or rather this is true only for stablecoin that can afford not to distribute the yield (aka $USDC $USDT).

Other yield bearing stablecoin have to pay the yield to holders. @ethena has to pay most of the revenue from its reserve to $sUSDe holders. It simply retain the spread. Just like @aave USDC market has to pay back most of the interest and only keep the spread.

@ether_fi which doesn’t issue a stablecoin still earn revenue on its reserve via the spread it keeps from its own dedicated Aave 4 instance.

So issuing your stablecoin doesn’t automatically means you earn more if you can’t afford supply that isn’t incentivized/paid.

The subtle difference though, is that lending via a stablecoin like $sUSDe or $sGHO is inherently less risky than rehypothecating $USDC on the same DeFi lending platform. Since in that case your underwrite both the tbills reserve book and the crypto lending book at once.

Must read below on the advantages of a stablecoin-first neobank.

The core idea: whoever issues the dollar earns the revenue on the reserves behind it. A neobank holding USDC or USDT is a distribution business because the yield stays with Circle or Tether. Ethena issues USDe, so through USDe and sUSDe it captures that revenue itself.

Robinhood made ~34% of 2025 revenue from net interest, Revolut ~22%, and Robinhood still splits that with partner banks. Ethena Pay's bet is that owning issuance gets you that NIM, and more of it, without a bank charter.

author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
Reminder that this stock/memecoin meta runs on volumes/trading fees:

If volume dries up, payouts & buybacks disappear -> the incentive to hold weakens, which WILL end up in dumping.

Coinbase reported $547B in trading volume in Q4 2021. A year later it was $145B.

Down ~74%.

For memes the decrease will likely be 95%.

And as you can see from screenshot below, Uniswap volumes are slowly decreasing already.

So the rewards need trading to continue:

- $ZCAT: taxed trading funds ZEC 'dividends'. If volume drops, the incentive to hold gets weaker

- $STONK: launchpad fee revenue funds buybacks and burns

- $PONS: basically same as STONK

- $INDEX: trading fees buy tokenized stocks for holders. No volumes, no 'dividends'

- $SHROOM: trading through its LP network generates fees to reinvest into liquidity (still low cap so might be a good degen buy)

- $CASHCAT: @letscashfun fees fund CASHCAT buybacks and burns.

Same goes for established DEXs: like 12% of trading fees buy RAY.

RH Chain generated ~73% of Uniswap's UNI burn(linked) revenue last week (yellow in screenshot attached).

All are exposed to people losing interest in trading. The interest in trading continues until people stop earning money. Or get tired of losing it.

It's so obvious but extrapolating yearly returns from current fees is absurd.

Red light. The desk freezes and nobody argues.

That one word made more money last night than every setup the other five found.

author: antpalkin
quoted_text:
GPT6-Astra is running Squid Game on my trading account. Six agents, one pot, $500 in and $6,300 out by morning while I slept.

The rules I gave them are the show's rules. The pot only grows. Whoever is wrong the most gets switched off and their seat goes to somebody new.

Jump Trading pays people to sit on a desk and say no. Mine does it for free and doesn't go home.

Six players:

> 456 hunts contracts where volume moves before the price does
> 067 reads the crowd and flags which spike somebody paid for
> 218 does the money math and sizes whatever is left standing
> 240 marks the level where the trade stops being a trade
> 001 has sat through every round and is the only one who talks to me
> THE FRONT MAN calls red light and that ends the conversation

Red light on the first setup of the night. I wrote that rule myself and I was still sour about it at midnight.

Then the chart went vertical without us in it.

That's the exact minute I'd have chased it and donated the difference. The desk didn't move. It sat under red light until the price came back down to 240's level, and took the entry there instead.

By morning the pot read $6,300 and nobody had been eliminated.

None of them is smarter than the model you already pay for. They're small enough to only be wrong about one thing at a time, and there's always somebody sitting between them and the button.

Setup is an evening. Number them, give each one job, write the Front Man's rules twice as carefully as the rest, then go to bed.

The expensive part of a trading desk was never the ideas. It was paying six people to disagree with each other at 3am.

Full build is in the article below.

The value accrual to STX dynamics is now live, and proof is onchain with locked STX.

Now we scale it with capital flows. Forward!

底部仓位管理的mindset：

一、底部仓位管理的mindset，需要同时容纳几组看似冲突、实际可以共存的判断：

1.我可以承认股价仍处于弱势，也可以在低位逐步增加仓位。

2.我可以认为股价还会继续跌，也可以承认随着价格下降，未来风险收益比正在改善。

3.我可以接受买早，也可以通过分批建仓和保留现金，让自己拥有更低位置继续买入的能力。

4.我可以尊重下降趋势，同时承认趋势越接近成熟阶段，潜在收益风险比可能越有吸引力。

5.我可以认真对待基本面的负面变化，同时不断重新评估估值、预期差和市场已经计入了多少悲观情景。

6.我可以保持谨慎和怀疑，同时始终对能够推翻悲观判断的正面证据保持开放。

7.我可以承认自己无法预测底部，同时提前让仓位为底部和未来反转做好准备。

8.我可以接受买入后继续下跌的痛苦，同时坚持事先制定的买入纪律。

9.我可以保留下跌后的继续行动权，同时逐渐获得未来上涨的参与权。

二、最终要形成几个条件反射：

1.底部最大的特征之一，就是让你越来越不想买。

2.底部不会让你买得舒服，顶部同样不会让你卖得舒服。

3.顶部允许卖早，底部也要允许买早。

4.不要追求最低点，买在底部区域已经足够优秀。允许买入以后继续下跌，要有把最底部的15%-20%慷慨送给别人的魄力和心态。

5.不要问“还能不能跌”，要问“这个价格应该持有多少”。

6.越跌，越要主动寻找悲观叙事的反证。尤其要问：公司真的变差了多少？股价又已经提前反映了多少？

7.不要预测明天涨还是跌，也不要等待最后一根完美的恐慌大阴线，让仓位提前为反转做好准备。

8.长期逻辑决定核心仓，估值、周期、趋势和风险收益比决定进攻仓以及加仓速度。

9.买入规则在冷静时制定，在恐慌时执行。

10.越接近底部，现金越珍贵。每一次加仓都必须为下一次可能更好的价格保留行动能力。

11.价格下跌本身不能成为加仓理由。每一次加仓都要重新确认：投资逻辑仍然成立，赔率正在改善，组合风险仍然可控。

三、底部管理的成熟，在于同时容纳两个事实：

1.股价可能继续下跌，未来潜在收益也可能正在同步上升。

2.最终用仓位解决这两者之间的矛盾。

不猜底，只管理仓位。

四、底部与顶部的仓位管理mindset形成镜像：

顶部时，价格越高，越应逐步把风险转换为现金，保留未来的行动权。

底部时，价格越低，越应在投资逻辑未被证伪的前提下，逐步把现金转换为未来上涨的参与权。

真正成熟的仓位管理，不追求精确预测最高点和最低点，而是在不同价格区间，让仓位始终与赔率、风险、置信度和认知边界相匹配。

顶部保留未来买回的权利，底部保留继续加仓的能力；用仓位应对不确定性，用行动权换取长期选择权。

Damn，Anthropic到底有着怎样的魅力啊，让这么多业界顶级大神纷纷加入，Google是真的要掉队了吗，顶尖人才都留不住了！！！
刚刚，那个在 Google 掌管 Chrome 开发者体验 14 年、主导过 DevTools 和 Lighthouse、用一套标准影响了全球 4000 万程序员日常工作流的男人，大神Addy Osmani，今天正式转身加入了 Anthropic，去给 Claude Code 操刀。

如果你这辈子按过 F12 审查过元素，跑过网页性能体检，甚至十年前用 TodoMVC 比较过框架，你的手指就一直在他的规则里打转。

在 Chrome 的 14 年里，他带队做的事情本质只有一件：让几千万人在浏览器里看清楚代码是怎么跑的。

但他今天跳出去了，去了一个连图形界面都没有的黑白终端命令行。

我觉得这根本不是一次平平无奇的硅谷大牛转岗，说是整个开发工具话语权交接的历史节点也不为过：

过去 14 年，全世界都在围绕浏览器窗口建生态，我们把最好的调试器、最重的插件和最绚丽的 DevTools 塞进网页里；
从今天起，引力中心彻底被拽回了最原始的终端。
大模型负责写逻辑，
终端负责直连环境，
而真正顶级的工具设计者，开始进场把 Agent 包装成人类肌肉记忆的一部分。

以前是人围着浏览器调试器找问题，
以后是 Agent 守在终端里替你把代码跑通。
还在纠结学哪个新框架的朋友，是不是该抬头看一眼真正起风的战场了呢？

text:
Some hackathon ideas that we'd like to see built on top of Surplus -- 

1. Limit buy orders / buy side order book

Currently we maintain an orderbook of sell orders, but treat buy orders as market orders.
Users have been asking for something like an orderbook for the buy side -- Something that lets an inference buyer set their price for a set of requests and only buy responses when the prices get low enough.

2. Seller tools / automations

There's a lot of people who want to sell, but don't want to constantly adjust their orders to get the best prices. 
So we're looking for teams that want to build things like trading algos for inference sellers.
Or make a simple UX that helps sellers maximize yield.

3. Swap contracts, CfDs, other derivatives to fix inference prices

Surplus is a spot market: prices change throughout the day. But both buyers and sellers want to be able to lock in prices.

4. Inference price indices

Many derivatives depend on some price index, so developing an inference price index could unlock more inference derivative markets.

Having a price index could also help sellers on surplus price dynamically relative to a reliable real-time inference index price.

Robinhood 股票代币 63 天成交 30 亿美元：Vlad 说，对很多人来说，这是他们买美股的唯一入口！！！

Robinhood 的股票代币已经覆盖 120 多个国家，其中很多地方没有成熟的券商渠道，甚至没有高效的金融系统。

对这些人来说，股票代币可能就是他们接触苹果、英伟达这些美国资产最现实的入口。

Robinhood Chain 7 月 1 日上线，股票代币 63 天累计 DEX 成交已经突破 30 亿美元，目前有 190 多种股票代币。

Robinhood 的结构也不是凭空印一个“AMC币”：每枚 Stock Token 都有对应底层股票 1:1 抵押，只是持有人拿到的是经济敞口，不是 AMC、英伟达这些公司的直接股东身份，也没有传统股票的投票权。

从这个角度看，链上还的继续，只是当下遇到了回撤。

text:
【MPM正念仓位管理哲学：Mindful Position Management】

这套仓位管理mindset，以后就这么称呼👆🏻

正念（Mindfulness），核心是对当下保持清晰觉察：看见正在发生的事实，也看见自己的情绪、念头和冲动，并在行动之前留出一点空间。它强调接纳不确定性，减少自动化反应，让决策重新回到当下、事实和自己真正能够控制的变量。

运用到投资和仓位管理：
MPM正念仓位管理哲学的核心，是在市场的不确定性中保持觉察，让仓位始终与赔率、风险、置信度和认知边界相匹配。

顶部区间时，随着价格上涨，逐步把风险转换为现金与未来的行动权。

底部区间时，随着价格下降，在投资逻辑未被证伪、风险仍然可控的前提下，逐步把现金转换为未来上涨的参与权。

最终追求的，是无论市场处于什么位置，都不执着于预测最高点和最低点，而是通过仓位管理，始终为自己保留足够的选择权与行动空间。

不猜顶，不猜底，只管理仓位。

2.顶部仓位管理的mindset：

author: lufeieth
quoted_text:
顶部仓位管理的mindset：

一、顶部仓位管理的mindset，需要同时容纳几组看似冲突、实际可以共存的判断：

1.我可以长期看好，也可以高位降低仓位。

2.我可以认为股价还会继续涨，也可以承认当前风险暴露已经过大。

3.我可以接受卖早，也可以通过保留核心仓，让剩余仓位继续参与长期成长。

4.我可以尊重强趋势，同时承认趋势越成熟，风险收益比可能越差。

5.我可以给基本面足够的兑现时间，同时要求估值和仓位不断接受重新评估。

6.我可以保持很高的conviction，同时始终对反证保持开放。

7.我可以承认自己无法预测顶部，同时提前让仓位为顶部做好准备。

8.我可以接受卖出后的遗憾，同时坚持事先制定的卖出纪律。

9.我可以保留上涨的参与权，同时保留下跌后的行动权。

二、最终要形成几个条件反射：

1.顶部最大的特征之一，就是让你越来越不想卖。

2.底部不会让你买得舒服，顶部同样不会让你卖得舒服。

3.底部允许买早，顶部也要允许卖早。

4.不要追求最高点，卖在顶部区域已经足够优秀。把最后15%到20%的上涨慷慨送给别人。

5.不要问“还能不能涨”，要问“这个价格应该持有多少”。

6.越涨，越要主动寻找反证。

7.不要预测明天涨还是跌，也不要预测最后一根大阳线，让仓位提前为反转做好准备。

8.长期逻辑决定核心仓，估值、周期、趋势和风险收益比决定进攻仓。

9.卖出规则在冷静时制定，在兴奋时执行。

三、顶部管理的成熟，在于同时容纳两个事实：

1.股价可能继续上涨，风险也可能正在同步上升。

2.最终用仓位解决这两者之间的矛盾。

不猜顶，只管理仓位。

Here's what I got from watching the video. Heads up: she never gives exact measurements — it's a vibe recipe.

**Salsa Queen's Fried Pico de Gallo**

- Tomatoes (looks like 5–6), chopped
- 2–3 jalapeños, seeds kept in for heat
- 1 white onion, chopped
- Fresh cilantro
- Lime
- Cooking oil
- Salt and pepper

1. Chop the jalapeños with the seeds in (she says if you don't want heat... oops, keep them in anyway).
2. Run the jalapeños and onion through a press-style vegetable chopper.
3. Heat oil in a skillet.
4. Toss the chopped tomatoes, onion, and jalapeños into the hot pan.
5. Fry it up, stirring, until it smells incredible. Season with salt, pepper, lime, and cilantro.

The twist is just that — classic pico ingredients, fried in a pan instead of served raw.

text:
Vals AI CEO Rayan Krishnan on the unlimited tokens experiment that revealed an anxious obligation for engineers to use models all the time, everywhere:

"I wanted to do a tokenmaxxing experiment. I was able to get unlimited access for our team for a month for some of the coding tools. We had a lot of engineers spending between one to two billion tokens a day."

"I went back and did some math, and it looked like in that month, we spent roughly $1.5 million worth of tokens... It was actually 10x more we were spending in tokens than employee salary for that month."

"We cannot continue with this mode of operation for the next month. How do we intelligently figure out what are the right tools we should use, for what teams, and what projects?"

"We found some pretty surprising insights. The Cognition Devin tool is actually very token-efficient, and so that's a place we've chosen to adopt more."

"There are a lot of places where you can get better pricing models out of subscriptions as opposed to token-based pricing."

"It's actually informed our strategy for how we can effectively tokenmaxx without spending $1.5 million per month."

author: a16z
quoted_text:
Vals AI co-founder and CEO Rayan Krishnan with a16z's Ben Horowitz and Jennifer Li on grading AI, what it costs, and who gets to make the rules:

Every big industry eventually grows an independent testing layer. AI has credit ratings to learn from and Enron to avoid. Model capability today is still mostly self-reported.

As public benchmarks saturate and models get better at optimizing for the tests themselves, Rayan makes the case for independent, continuously evolving evaluations.

The harder problem is geopolitical. Reagan's "trust but verify" worked during the Cold War because you could fly over and count the missiles. No simple equivalent for AI models exists.

In this conversation with Erik Torenberg, they get into how you measure a model's ability to improve itself, why every good benchmark eventually has to be retired, and what happens when token spend begins to rival employee salaries.

text:
有朋友问为什么OpenAI说AI不会造成白领工作危机，但Anthropic却说会？

这个问题够挑动普通人神经的。两家确实有真实的判断分歧，但争论的重点其实不是AI会不会替人干活，而是企业减少用人需求的速度，会不会快过新需求，新岗位和新人员转岗的速度。OpenAI管理层更相信社会和企业的适应能力，Anthropic管理层则更担心AI的进步速度和跨行业替代能力会超过这种适应能力。有些新闻把它外推概括成OpenAI说绝不会失业，Anthropic说一定会失业，就让两边显得都说得过头了。

所以先把两家的原话校准一下。Anthropic的警告是一个有时间范围的预测，2025年5月28日Dario Amodei对Axios说，AI可能在未来一至五年消除一半的入门级白领岗位，并使美国失业率升到10%到20%。这不是说一半白领已经失业，更不是说一半所有工作都会消失。他在2026年1月的文章中又明确解释，自己说的是未来风险，不是在声称这种规模的替代已经发生。

OpenAI的一项回应是没有看到支持这一预测的证据。2025年6月Brad Lightcap说，他们在企业客户中尚未观察到大规模替代入门级员工，同场的Sam Altman强调，即便技术准备好了，社会和组织也有很大的惯性，不会立刻完成替换。Altman后来确实表达了更乐观的判断，2026年5月26日他说，入门级白领岗位减少的程度低于自己此前预期，他不认为会出现某些同行谈论的那种就业末日，但他也没有排除风险将来发生。

这里最重要的逻辑区别是：目前没有发生，不能证明以后不会发生。技术上AI能做很多工作，但也不能直接证明几年内会失业多少人。两边最强的论据和最容易跳步的地方，都在这两句话里。

OpenAI更看重能力变成裁员，中间还有很多环节。Altman强调模型能力已经走得很远，但企业采用和组织改造仍处于早期，企业还没有完全弄清楚怎样让人和AI协作，怎样安全有效地接入现有系统，以及如何把这些能力变成可衡量的收益。

这个理由有道理。能生成一份报告，不等于能独立承担负责这份报告的整个岗位。实际应用还受到法律约束，软件集成，人工审核等因素的影响，这些障碍甚至也被Anthropic自己的研究明确列出来了。

我们可以再考虑一个简化的假设，一家工作室原来有十个人，AI让某些工作快了一倍，老板可能用原班人马承接更多订单，也可能减少招聘，甚至缩减团队。生产率提高本身，并没有规定老板必须选择哪一种，需求增长多少，竞争怎样变化，节省的收益如何分配，都会影响结果。

但乐观论证有一个需要警惕的漏洞，这个职业仍然需要人，不等于这个职业仍然需要原来那么多人。即使最后的判断，客户关系和责任必须由人承担，也不能仅凭这一点保证初级岗位的数量，工资和晋升机会不受影响。会不会因为AI有新的职业，新的工作机会出现，也有待观察。

Amodei更担心的是，这一次转到别的脑力工作也未必能躲开。他的论证并不是简单的机器抢工作，他明确承认以往技术进步会创造新任务，人们也能转向新行业，他的担心是AI可能同时冲击许多具有相似认知要求的职业，而且变化太快。比如金融，咨询和法律的知识不同，但都包含大量阅读，归纳，分析和文书工作，倘若这些方向同时受影响，转岗就不像只有一个行业受到冲击时那么容易。

他也承认企业采用技术需要时间，但认为这只是延缓冲击，即使老企业改造很慢，采用AI的新企业也可能以更少的人手参与竞争。因此他对组织惯性会保护就业的判断，比Altman悲观得多。

把双方的分歧压缩一下，较乐观的判断相信省下来的劳动会被更多需求和新工作吸收，较悲观的判断担心吸收得不够快，而且新出现的脑力任务也可能被AI承接。真正难预测的是这个吸收过程，不只是下一代模型能得多少分。

还有一个统计上的错位，就是不大规模裁员，也可能让新人很难进来，这可能比突然裁掉半数白领更值得注意。Anthropic在2026年3月5日公布的劳动市场研究发现，在其研究覆盖的数据中，AI暴露程度高的职业并没有出现系统性的失业率上升，但对22到25岁年轻人，研究发现了进入这些职业的招聘放缓迹象。作者同时强调，这个证据仍然初步，存在其他解释，不能直接认定全部由AI造成。

于是下面两句话完全可能同时成立，“我们的公司没有因为AI大规模裁员”，以及“我们今年不再招那么多助理，初级分析员和初级程序员”。这说明现有员工的就业暂时稳定，与年轻人的职业入口变窄，并不矛盾。因而只盯着总体失业率，会漏掉一部分值得研究的变化，只盯着某类招聘减少，又可能漏掉其他职业增加的机会。

而且Anthropic并非所有研究都给出一个确定的悲观答案，它目前公布的经济情景模型同时讨论温和，显著和极端变化，结果取决于AI能做什么，采用多快，自主程度多高，以及劳动者多久能找到新工作。企业领导者的风险判断，和研究团队给出的条件性情景，不应该混成一个声音。

那这里有没有商业宣传的因素呢？确实值得考虑，但不能拿它代替判断。两种表达都可能有商业上的好处，强调冲击可以管理，AI帮助人工作，有利于降低采用阻力，强调技术强大到可能重塑就业而我们愿意公开风险，既能突出技术实力，也能建立负责任的形象。同样，表达悲观并不自动等于更诚实，表达乐观也不自动等于粉饰。

更可靠的办法，是把可验证的部分拆开，预测的是哪一类岗位，期限从哪一天算起，说的是任务被自动化，招聘减少，还是净失业增加，假设了多快的企业采用速度。

我的判断是，Amodei提出的风险值得认真准备，但一至五年消除一半入门级白领岗位仍不能当成已经证实的结论，OpenAI关于企业改造和人类参与的理由也有分量，但不足以保证白领岗位数量和收入安全。

对普通劳动者来说，最重要的问题未必是社会还会不会有工作，而是新工作是否来得及出现，自己是否转得过去，工资是否还能维持生活，以及新人是否还有积累经验，成长为资深人员的入口。即使经济整体更富裕，这些问题也不会自动解决，这既需要制度层面的准备，也要靠我们自己每个人积极学习AI，拥抱AI，提高自身的实力。

text:
the best recent analogy i read about trading was basically

no sane person would pick up a book about brain surgery, read it over the weekend and then think "yeah i can do that" and be willing to perform it on someone on monday

no sane person would pick up the violin, practice for a week and then think "yeah i'm ready to play at carnegie hall"

but every day lots of insane people read a trading book and then think, ya let me take my talents to the order-books

there are a few interesting threads you can pull on related to this but the one i think is probably most apt in the current moment is that trading is much different than these other examples (duh)

specifically, in those cases it is literally impossible to perform the act as a novice. you can't physically do it.

trading on the other hand is often misconstrued as simple (just buy or sell) and that misperception stems from the fact that you can get quite lucky when you first start

and so it is very seductive for new participants when they flip the coin and it comes up heads a few times in a row

beginners can win all the time (they do!) but this is also why it isn't really that impressive until someone does it across many years, many regimes, different environments, at larger scale, etc

the small trader has huge advantages (time horizon, flexibility, size, speed, no external LPs to answer to) and they should press these advantages, but twitter likes to make it seem as if it's easy to make a living trading (that this is back en vogue is not new and mildly alarming)

some people will read this and think "professionals are just apes in suits" and to a large extent this is true. but the best of the best are apex predators, not the trust fund nepo babies who we all widely mock on x dot com (the everything app)

text:
This post looks like the start of a VERY sophisticated and well-funded PR operation to get support for Democrats to regulate AI into oblivion. Let me show you how it works:
1.) This guy, with minimal followers and no previous account activity, goes to the Wall Street Journal which publishes an exclusive with quotes from him on his resignation 18 minutes BEFORE this post goes up. Planning was clearly done in advance.

2.) Within hours, it has tens of thousands of reposts and the account has 100k+ followers. The post is punchy, quotable, it almost seems professionally written. The first three accounts to quote tweet it all do so within 15 minutes of the initial posting. Remember, this account had basically zero engagement beforehand, so an organic reach explanation seems unlikely.

According to Grok those accounts are @_NathanCalvin (General Counsel at Encode AI), @peterwildeford (Head of Policy at the AI Policy Network), and @DKokotajlo (Head of the AI Futures Project), all of which are up-and-coming AI-Doomer policy advocacy nonprofits.

The AI Futures Project website says it is funded “primarily” by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which says on its own website that it has advised Jaan Tallinn, Skype creator and one of the leading investors in Anthropic, to grant over $2.5 million to the AI Futures Project since 2024.

Encode AI says on its website that it is ALSO funded by the Survival and Flourishing Fund, which in turn says that it told Anthropic investor Jaan Tallinn to grant $516,000 to Encode AI in 2025.

And wouldn’t you know it, the Survival and Flourishing Fund ALSO says it told Jaan Tallinn to grant $2 million to the AI Policy Institute, the 501(c)(3) affiliate of the AI Policy Network, as well.

What are the odds that the first three quote tweets of Coxon’s post would all be major AI-restriction policy advocates funded generously by the same donor, who also happens to be one of the leading investors in, and a board member of, Anthropic, the company Coxon was resigning from? And all within 15 minutes of posting (two within ten)?

3.) Jacob Coxon doesn’t have much of a resume, but we do know that, in 2022, he got a $20,159 scholarship for the “long term future scholarship program” from the Good Ventures Foundation, one of the philanthropic vehicles of Dustin Moskovitz, a notorious AI-doomer who has spent tens if not hundreds of millions on policy advocacy to strictly regulate AI, while also being an Anthropic Investor himself.

It also just so happens that the 14th person to quote Coxon’s post was @MaxNadeau_ (27 minutes after posting) who is the program officer for the Technical AI Safety team at Coefficient Giving, another of Moskovitz’s philanthropic spending vehicles. Max is not a frequent poster, his last posts before quoting Coxon were before Labor Day, but he was remarkably quick off the mark for this one.

4.) Basically every major Democrat politician and candidate has suddenly glommed on to this post, and conveniently, as the people cry out foe answers, Bernie Sanders already has a bill written to “ban super intelligence” and regulate AI into oblivion, and will be releasing later this week. The bill, among many other things, will create “a new cabinet-level federal agency to safeguard the public from the dangers of artificial intelligence” that will be “advised by an Artificial Intelligence Advisory Board comprised of experts on artificial intelligence.” Do you think, perhaps, Anthropic and its many investors who fund AI policy advocacy might have interest in getting to place a pet “expert” on the board of an entity that dictates what AI is and isn’t allowed to do? And isn’t it fortuitous that this whistleblower came forward  with his oh-so scary stories so close in proximity to the release of the most radical piece of AI legislation ever introduced?

BREAKING: OpenAI might have stolen another major proof. 

In a detailed Mastodon post, which I report in full in the comments, Andreas Thom presents several pieces of evidence suggesting that OpenAI may have trained Astra on conversations in which he and Gábor Kun were working on Gromov’s soficity conjecture, one of the ten problems OpenAI later announced Astra had solved.

I know Andreas. We met several times early in our careers. He is an exceptional mathematician, a leading expert on sofic and hyperlinear groups, and one of the most respected scholars in the field. He has spent two decades working on this problem.

If his account is correct, this is not a minor dispute over attribution. It would mean that unpublished human work was absorbed into a model and then presented to the world as a breakthrough by the model itself.

And if the allegations raised by Levent Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster, and now Andreas Thom are all substantiated, we are no longer looking at isolated incidents.

We may be looking at one of the greatest intellectual scandals in the history of science.

AI is not discovering new mathematics.

AI is stealing human discovery.

Guru Nanga Tales: Fictional Encounters and the very REAL Book of Maps

Once, in his wanderings, Guru Nanga came to a hilltop in the West Bank, carrying nothing but a walking stick and a large hardcover book called Visualizing Palestine: A Chronicle of Colonialism and the Struggle for Liberation 

(Haymarket Books, $39.95, more than 200 full-color infographics, remarkably heavy, useful for both enlightenment and self-defense).

A settler approached him and said, “Welcome, stranger. This land was empty when we arrived.”

The Guru opened the book to page 22, where a map from 1882 showed the land speckled gray with pre-existing Palestinian localities, like a poppy-seed bagel. “A very crowded emptiness,” said the Guru.

 “In 1922 the emptiness contained 750,000 people. That is the most populated nothing I have encountered in all my travels, and I have been to Fresno.”

The settler frowned. “Well. God gave it to us.”

“Interesting,” said the Guru, turning to the page where an early Zionist leader is quoted saying they had come to conquer a country from the people inhabiting it. “Your own founders kept saying the quiet part into a stenographer. 

You should read this book. It has footnotes. 

Three hundred and seventy pages in, the footnotes are still going. It is the most documented land theft in the history of paperwork.”

text:
I am the payments logistics officer at the United States Treasury Department who has personally touched every version of the free money this country has been promised since 2020, and I am the only person left in this building who remembers how the first one actually went, because the first one is the only one that was ever real.

Spring 2020. Economic Impact Payments, $1,200 a person, funded, appropriated, moving. Then Mnuchin's office ordered the president's name onto the memo line. Not a rubber stamp. A printed signature, the first time a president's name had ever gone on an IRS payment. Commissioner Rettig wasn't told until the request was already in motion. Our engineers had to reprogram the check-printing software and run it through testing before a single check could clear, because the system had never been built to hold a name that wasn't the Treasurer's. 70 million people waited an extra few days for their own emergency relief, during a pandemic, so a signature could finish QA. I sat in the room where someone asked if we could just skip the testing and was told no, we are not shipping the president's name with a rendering bug in it. The actual money moved slower so the branding could move faster. Every version since has been the branding moving faster and the money not moving at all.

Version one was the DOGE Dividend. It didn't come from this building. It came from a 30-year-old hedge fund manager named James Fishback, CEO of a firm called Azoria, who has said publicly that the number arrived to him in a dream. He posted it to Musk in February of 2025: take 20% of whatever DOGE saves and cut it into checks, math it out to roughly $5,000 a household if the savings hit $2 trillion. Musk replied that he'd check with the president. The president checked. Within days it was a line in a press briefing, no legislation, no appropriation, just a number that had been asleep in one man's head 12 hours earlier now sitting on the Resolute desk. By May, DOGE's own public savings tracker read $175 billion, not $2 trillion, which works out to $1,086.96 per taxpayer, not $5,000. Nobody issued a correction. The number just stopped being said out loud. And when Fishback later described himself as having advised DOGE, a former senior DOGE adviser went on the record to say, quote, you didn't advise DOGE. So the origin story of the $5,000 figure still being used today, 18 months and 2 rebrands later, is a dream, a tweet, and a denial. I have that DOGE savings tracker bookmarked. I check it the way other people check their portfolio.

Version two was the Tariff Dividend, announced that November. $2,000 a person this time, lower number, new funding source: tariff revenue instead of imaginary government savings. This one at least had a real number behind it: $195 billion collected in tariffs for the fiscal year. Economists ran the arithmetic before we did. Cato called it fiscal fantasy in print. A deputy chief economist at Oxford Economics warned that stacking a stimulus check on top of the existing tax cuts could overheat the economy. The math didn't work even before the legal problem showed up, and then the legal problem showed up: the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs in February, the ones the dividend was supposed to be funded from, and by May we were issuing refunds to importers faster than customs was collecting anything. I watched the ledger cross from positive to negative in the same spreadsheet tab we'd built to track the dividend. We didn't rename the tab. We just stopped opening it.

Version three is the Trump Dividend, the one I'm actually being asked to price this week. Same number as version one, $5,000, announced Tuesday night from the stage of the midterm convention. Quote: if the Republicans win the House of Representatives and the United States Senate, both of them, because of our tremendous economic success, I will issue a dividend to every adult citizen in the United States for $5,000. One condition attached, and it isn't a funding mechanism, it's a spending restriction: the money has to stay in the country, no Canada, no China, no Germany, his words. So the government has now, for the first time in three attempts, specified where the imaginary money is allowed to be imaginarily spent. Commentators started using the word bribe before the applause even finished. There's a real federal statute for this: 18 U.S.C. 597, expenditures to influence voting, a fine or up to 2 years if it's willful. Nobody in this building has said the statute's number out loud in a meeting, and I've listened for it, because there's a comfortable legal argument sitting right there in plain sight: you cannot criminally buy a vote with money that was never appropriated, never budgeted, and has no line item anywhere in the federal government. It isn't a bribe. A bribe requires a bribe.

I priced it anyway, because pricing a number has never once required the number to exist. 270 million adults, $5,000 each, $1.35 trillion, against a national debt that closed this week at $40.1 trillion. It costs 7 times what version two's tariffs brought in at their peak. I put the number in the deck. I did not put in a funding source, because there's a blank cell where that used to go, and I've started to think of that blank cell as the actual through-line of my career here. 

Four checks. One real. One dreamed by a guy who isn't even employed by the government he says he advised. One that went negative by court order. One that costs a Senate seat instead of a tax dollar. And I'm still on the invite list for the pricing meeting, because I'm the only one left who was in the room in 2020 when we tested a signature before we tested the money.

Evan and I were debate partners in high school; in a weird twist of fate, he’s now an alignment lead at Anthropic and I’m a researcher at OpenAI.

We should not preserve the status quo. Humanity faces a series of challenges, independent of AI, that compel us to innovate.

AI does pose risks to society. These threats are more ill-defined, and more probabilistic, than knowing that 16% of our loved ones will die from cancer, or that 50% of the currently inhabited regions on Earth will become too hot to sustain human life by 2070. While we ought soberly evaluate the risks of super-intelligence – and work extremely hard to mitigate those risks – we hold an equal moral obligation to paint the inspirational and optimistic vision of the world we want to create.

As someone who worked on climate tech for 3 years prior to joining OpenAI, I have a different perspective on the role that AI must play in our future. I believe in empowering humanity with super intelligence that can build the world we want to live in: rebuilding polar ice caps, inventing new desalination techniques, electrifying the grid; printing solutions to pathogens in real-time; democratizing education worldwide.

quoted_text:
I tried SunSwap V4 myself, and honestly, the swap flow was pretty straightforward.

I went from 300 TRX ($100.08) to SUN and walked through the whole process from the https://t.co/00rB9OhWLr interface to wallet confirmation.

Here’s what I saw:

1/ Enter the swap

I selected TRX → SUN and entered 300 TRX.

The quote showed:

300 TRX → 5,980.9230152773897484 SUN

Price impact was showing 0.00%, with 0.00 TRX listed as the transaction fee on the swap screen.

2/ Review before confirming

The confirmation screen showed:

• Minimum received: 5,951.0184002010027996 SUN
• Price impact: 0.00%
• Transaction fee: 0.00 TRX

So I could see exactly what I was about to sign before moving to the wallet.

3/ Wallet confirmation

This was the part I paid attention to.

The wallet showed the smart-contract interaction and an estimated resource deduction of:

≈1.2532 TRX ($0.41)

That’s separate from the 300 TRX being swapped.

4/ Swap completed

After confirming, the interface returned a successful swap message:

300 TRX → 5,980.9230152773897484 SUN

Simple enough.

But the more interesting part is what SunSwap V4 is doing under the hood.

V4 brings back native TRX trading pairs, so users don't have to manually wrap TRX into WTRX first. https://t.co/00rB9OhWLr says this reduces unnecessary energy use and removes some of the extra complexity from the user experience.

It also introduces Singleton architecture and Flash Accounting. Instead of treating every pool interaction as a separate contract-to-contract process, V4 can track internal balance changes and settle them at the end. That becomes especially useful for more complex or multi-hop swaps.

And https://t.co/00rB9OhWLr currently advertises up to 99% energy subsidies for eligible interaction scenarios, although the exact subsidy depends on the product and interaction.

So from my side, the main takeaway wasn't just the numbers.

It was the fact that something fairly technical underneath can still feel like:

Select → Review → Confirm → Done.

That’s the kind of DeFi UX that makes sense to me.

SunSwap V4 is making the swap experience simpler while doing more of the heavy lifting underneath.

text:
NVIDIA 最近在悄悄改写一个很重要的叙事：

GPU 可能根本不该按照传统电子产品的逻辑估值。

NVIDIA AI Infrastructure 今天直接用了三个词形容 GPU：

productive、fungible、durable。

然后补了一句：an investable asset class。

过去两年围绕 AI 泡沫最大的争议之一，就是几千亿美元买来的 GPU 到底能用多久。NVIDIA 一年一代新卡，如果旧卡两三年就在经济意义上报废，现在整个 AI CapEx 的回报率都会非常难看。

Ornn 最新一篇《The Economics of Open-Weight Inference》，就是在给 NVIDIA 这套说法补数据。

他们测了 11 个开源权重模型、8 个闭源模型，又把 A100 到 B200 的租赁成本和 1 个月到 5 年的期限价格拉出来比较。

里面一个数据特别有意思：

跑同一个模型，A100 生成 100 万 output tokens 的成本，可以不到 H100 的一半。

H100 当然更快。但 A100 已经足够便宜，所以在大批量、对延迟没那么敏感的 inference workload 里，它反而可能更赚钱。

这意味着 NVIDIA 每出一代新 GPU，上一代并不会自动变成电子垃圾。它会往下迁移。

最先进的 GPU 去训练 frontier model、跑最吃性能的推理；老 GPU 去跑便宜的 open-weight model、批量 inference 和低优先级任务。

GPU 开始有点像飞机。

新飞机更省油、更先进，不代表十年前的飞机突然不能赚钱。只要它还能找到航线、租得出去、收入覆盖运营成本，它就仍然是一块能产生现金流的资产。

Ornn 甚至认为，最老一批 GPU 的经济寿命可能超过 6 年。Azure 此前退役的一些 K80、P100、P40，实际服务周期大约达到 7–9 年；V100 也跑了约 7.5 年。

这件事一旦成立，对整个 AI 基建市场的影响会非常大。

因为现在争论的已经不只是 GPU 折旧几年。

GPU 正在被金融化。

Ornn 已经在做 GPU 现货价格指数 OCPI、五年前向曲线、GPU 回本周期，H100 指数甚至已经进入 Bloomberg；今年又和 ICE 宣布推出以 GPU-hour 为标的的 compute futures。未来算力运营商可以锁价格，买方可以对冲算力成本，银行也可以更准确地给一批 GPU 算残值、做贷款。

这也是为什么 NVIDIA 现在这么想证明 GPU 「durable」。

一张只能用两年的显卡，很难撑起一个几十年期限的基础设施金融体系；一台能持续出租六七年、每天都有市场报价、还能做远期和期货的机器，就完全是另一种东西了。

当然 NVIDIA 这套话也不能全信。

A100、H100、B200 并没有真正意义上的 fungible，显存、带宽、能耗、互联和适合的 workload 差别都很大。Ornn 本身又是在做算力交易和算力金融，它天然希望 GPU 变成一种可以定价、交易和抵押的资产。

但这篇研究至少证明了新 GPU 更强不等于旧 GPU 经济价值归零。

财政部回购扩到60亿，长债收益率反而往上走，不禁要问为什么？个人角度更像一次预期差和宏观重新定价，详细聊聊：
1、昨天也聊到在回购规模公布前市场普遍预期已经是50-60亿美金规模，甚至大摩和jefferis等投行都给到了100亿美金的回购规模预期。这就导致了：
1）相对50-60亿美金的普遍预期，并没有超出；但相对市场里70–80亿、甚至100亿的更高预期，这是少给。
2）市场还关心的是未来几个月能持续移走多少久期，这一次回购扩容但公告里后续节奏写的仍是“至少40亿”，
相当于昨晚财政部的公告里并没有给出“更大、更持久计划“已经开始。

所以长债收益桂林走高就是来自这两点本次回购没有超出普遍预期并比乐观预期要低；
市场没有看到未来回购规模继续扩大的信号；

2、但实际上昨晚长债拍卖数据还是可以的
昨晚390亿10年期拍卖很强：中标4.834%，投标倍数2.71，一级交易商只拿约4.3%，拍卖后收益率从高点回落到约4.835%。这就说明了美债还是有买家的，只是买家要求更高回报。所以收益率创高和国债市场失序，是两件事 
3、油价也是关键助推剂
也不要忽视昨晚油价已经站上了100，油价走高通胀预期自然也走高，短端利率同时上行。财政部能改一部分债券供求，改不了油价，也替不了美联储设政策利率路径。 
4、再回看上周贝森特在G20财长和央行行长年会上的讲话
其实更值得关注的是上周贝森特的讲话：财政部难改均衡价格，能做的是缓和失序、改善旧券流动性，让交易商腾出表来接新债。相当于说昨晚有限规模还是挡不住油价、供给和资金机会成本这些基本面。

当然持续改期限供给和交易成本，当然可能边际影响价格；毕竟未来两个月还有7次回购。

5、市场是在倒逼美联储做YCC
个人觉得现在可能性较小，本身沃什还有意削减联储大规模资产负债表，让他重新大规模扩表近期可能性并不大。

当然未来如果真的出了问题更可能先用针对融资/交易的工具（类似年初的储备管理购买RMP那样），但一下直接跳到长端YCC，可能跨度会有点大。

6、后续看哪几点？
1）今晚的8月ppi和明晚的8月cpi数据，如果不弱，短期可能还会推高收益率。
2）再看油价走势、核心是美伊博弈的进展。昨天推文有聊到，要想短时间内真正缓和、需要川普做更多让步才行；
3）还有日元走势，前两天聊到的日元低跌的过快需要关注下。

整体上
十年美债已经站稳4.8%以上，短期内越往上市场压力还是会很大；本周前几天美股道指和标普走的很多，纳指是因为GPT6 Aatra带来的强预期走强，但是短期预期打满后，宏观继续恶化还是会影响到半导体市场走势；
可能又要回到宏观压制产业基本面的情况

text:
Anthropic 刚算了一遍 AI 把美国经济推到极限之后会发生什么。

结论有点残酷：

AI 可以制造一场经济奇迹，同时制造一场劳动者的衰退。

在 Anthropic 最激进的情景里，到 2030 年，美国 GDP 比「没有 AI」的基线高 32.4%。这个增长速度已经接近经济起飞。

但劳动者拿到的总收入，只比基线高 0.5%。

钱去哪了？

资本收入高出 81.4%，资本在国民收入中的份额从约 40% 涨到 54.8%。换句话说，AI 创造出来的大部分新增财富，都被资本拿走了。

大家一直担心 AI 会不会让人失业。Anthropic 给出的极端数字确实很夸张，整体失业率 11.9%，知识工人失业率 17.9%。但失业还只是第一层。

第二层更麻烦，知识工作的价格本身会被打下来。

程序员、金融、律师、媒体、教育、管理、销售这些知识岗位，工资比无 AI 基线低 11.5%；建筑、维修、运输、餐饮、生产等职业，工资反而高 33.6%。

过去几十年最稳定的一条上升路径，是读书、进办公室、靠脑力换取更高收入。Anthropic 的极端情景里，这条路径被 AI 直接打穿了。

而且宏观数据甚至会看起来很好。

平均工资仍然高 9.7%，GDP 高 32.4%，生产率暴涨，企业利润暴涨。你只看 CNBC，甚至会觉得这是美国经济最好的几年。

然后你再看身边，办公室岗位在消失，知识工人的工资在跌，资本收入爆炸增长。

以后我们可能会第一次遇到一种很诡异的繁荣。经济数据全面向上，大量受过高等教育的人却明确感觉自己越来越穷。

当然，这只是 Anthropic 的极端 scenario，不是预测。它假设到 2030 年 AI 能影响约 30% 的经济任务，在相关任务上生产率达到约 2.2 倍，而且 90% 直接自动化，也没有给知识工人安排足够多的新任务。Anthropic 自己也没有给这个情景分配发生概率。

但这种模型有价值的地方，本来也不是告诉你 2030 年失业率到底会不会精确到 17.9%。

它真正把一个问题算清楚了：

AI 时代最大的分配矛盾，可能发生在「机器替代人」之前。只要 AI 带来的生产率收益更快流向模型、算力、股权和资本所有者，经济越繁荣，劳动和资本之间的裂缝反而可能越大。

以前大家担心 AI 让世界没工作。

Anthropic 算出来一个可能更现实的版本：

工作还有，GDP 也在涨，只是增长越来越和你没关系。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
In its latest research, Anthropic projects 32% US GDP growth by 2030 in extreme AI Scenario

Some takeaways:

- The extreme scenario assumes AI performs nearly all knowledge-work tasks autonomously and creates essentially no new knowledge tasks for humans, a combination the authors say would likely require recursively self-improving AI adopted rapidly.

- US GDP is 32.4% higher in 2030 than without AI, yet total labor income barely changes while capital’s share of GDP rises from about 40% to 54.8%.

- The extreme scenario puts knowledge-worker unemployment at 17.9% by 2030, compared with 3.9% for other workers and 11.9% across the economy.

- knowledge-worker pay is 11.5% below the no-AI baseline in 2030, while other workers earn 33.6% more and average pay across workers is 9.7% higher.

- In its substantial and extreme scenarios, Anthropic explicitly says coders and call service center agents may have to switch into professions such as electrician and nurse because those occupations are less exposed to AI.

- Anthropic excludes hyper-capable robots from its model and reports that some external reviewers questioned whether AI-exposed occupations would shrink at all, with others suggesting the extreme scenario is better understood as a thought experiment.

果断的被安全审核拦了下来，说有性暗示！

请问是怎么做到的？

提示词：

Create a 9:16 photorealistic vintage baker portrait series with a soft, intimate POV feeling.  Use the same beautiful adult East Asian woman across the set, with direct eye contact, realistic skin texture, soft natural hair, and a sensual but natural presence. She wears a simple backless summer kitchen dress in ivory or soft cream, with a light apron and a delicate headscarf. The setting is a refined retro Shaker-style kitchen with mushroom-gray cabinets, dark walnut counters, warm gray stone surfaces, subtle brass hardware, and clean summer daylight.  This batch should focus more on body language, eye contact, and pose geometry than on big action scenes. The woman must remain the clear visual focus in every frame.  Include elegant kitchen portrait moments such as:  * sitting on a countertop with one long leg extended and one foot placed on a stool  * offering a slice of strawberry cake toward the viewer  * sitting backwards on a high stool with her arms resting on the chair back  * reaching upward in the kitchen while keeping a playful connection with the camera  Keep the mood vintage, feminine, playful, and slightly flirty. Every image should feel like a captured moment inside the same retro kitchen scene, with the viewer standing close to her.  Vary the face angle across the series. Do not repeat the same three-quarter face in every image. Use a mix of front-facing eye contact, side glances, profile-based eye contact, upward gaze, and slightly lowered chin with lifted eyes, so the set feels alive and not like the same face pasted onto different poses.  Use posture, shoulders, waistline, long legs, and eye contact as the main source of visual interest. Poses should feel relaxed but intentional, with a light editorial quality.  Props must stay secondary. If props appear, keep them small and supportive, such as a strawberry cake slice, a wooden spoon, a whisk, a small tray, a folded linen cloth, or a small glass jar. Avoid oversized opaque objects, large bowls, or bulky cookware that block the torso or steal attention from the model.  Lighting should be soft, clean, and summery. Keep the overall color balance neutral to slightly warm. The retro feeling must come from the kitchen style, wardrobe, textures, and atmosphere — not from a heavy yellow or orange filter. Skin should stay natural, ivory clothing should stay ivory, and gray cabinets should remain gray.  The final result should feel intimate, stylish, feminine, vintage, and editorial, with realistic anatomy, realistic skin, believable expressions, and a lived-in but elegant kitchen environment.  Avoid repetitive face angles, stiff posing, oversized props, yellow color cast, orange skin, distorted hands, exaggerated wide-angle body distortion, cluttered backgrounds, complex strap designs, and obvious AI artifacts.
